    mathjax: null
    pandoc_args:

    toc_float:
      collapsed: false

format:

    toc: true
    toc-location: left
    toc-depth: 3
    toc-expand: true
    page-layout: full          # body fills the window (minus the TOC sidebar) while KEEPING Quarto's grid intact
    df-print: paged
    html-table-processing: none # preserve kableExtra colspan/footnotes (pandoc re-parsing drops them)
    embed-resources: true       # single self-contained .html

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Initializing code
rm(list = ls(all.names = TRUE))
gc()

# ---- where this script lives -------------------------------------------------
# Found automatically when the document is KNITTED. Running chunks one at a time
# in an IDE it cannot be, so set CODE_DIR to the folder holding this file. Leave
# it empty for a normal knit.
CODE_DIR = ""   # e.g. "C:/Users/you/StarlinkAmazon/code"

rmd_file = tryCatch(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
code_dir = if (nzchar(CODE_DIR)) {
  normalizePath(CODE_DIR, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
} else if (!is.null(rmd_file)) {
  dirname(normalizePath(rmd_file, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE))
} else if (file.exists("starlink_results.Rmd")) {
  normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
} else {
  stop(
    "Cannot locate this script's folder.
",
    "  working directory: ", getwd(), "

",
    "Either knit the document, or -- if you are running chunks one at a time --
",
    "do ONE of:
",
    "  * set CODE_DIR above to the folder holding starlink_results.Rmd, or
",
    '  * setwd("<package>/code") before running this chunk'
  )
}
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(code_dir, "starlink_results.Rmd")))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = code_dir)
setwd(code_dir)

# ---- sample end years --------------------------------------------------------
# The calendar panel runs Jan 2022 to Dec 2024. The PRODES panel is built on
# PRODES years (August to July) and ends with PRODES year 2025, which closes in
# July 2025. Nothing from August 2025 onward enters either panel.
CAL_END_YEAR = 2024L
PRODES_END_YEAR = 2025L

# ---- data locations ----------------------------------------------------------
# The two analysis panels are committed; raw provider downloads are listed in the
# README and fetched locally. Everything is relative to this script's folder.
# ONE knob, matching work_dataframe.Rmd: every path is relative to this script's
# own folder, and every data path hangs off DATA_DIR.
DATA_DIR = "../data/"
panel_dir = DATA_DIR
raw_dir = paste0(DATA_DIR, "raw/")

# Fixed climate specification. The analysis panels carry corrected CHIRTS-ERA5
# maximum temperature and corrected CHIRPS precipitation as contemporaneous
# controls. Copernicus ERA5-Drought SPEI-12 supplies a separate, internally
# consistent accumulated water-balance control: its precipitation and
# Penman--Monteith PET components both come from ERA5.
message(paste(
  "climate controls: corrected CHIRTS-ERA5 Tmax; corrected CHIRPS precipitation;",
  "Copernicus ERA5-Drought SPEI-12"
))

# Municipal polygons for the variance-share map. This is the submission-built,
# panel-matched 772-unit geometry, including the Santarem--Mojui merge.
mun_legal_amazon_geometry = paste0(DATA_DIR, "processed/mun_zone.RDS")

panel_end_year = 2025L
stopifnot(PRODES_END_YEAR <= panel_end_year)

# The upstream pipeline stores the commodity-price RDS files directly in
# December 2024 BRL, so no render-time rebasing is required.

# ── Lagged agricultural-price controls ────────────────────────────────────────
# Following the price-control functional form used by Assuncao et al. (2023),
# interact lagged national real price LEVELS with fixed municipal agronomic
# suitability. The function stores the two raw lagged price series; the product
# with soy or pasture suitability is specified transparently with `:` in the
# regression formula. These controls vary by year and receive no extra year interaction.
add_lagged_price_controls = function(dat) {
  prices_lagged = readRDS(paste0(panel_dir, "cmdty_price_monthly.RDS")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(commodity %in% c("soy", "cattle")) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(commodity, year) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = commodity,
      values_from = price,
      names_prefix = ".price_"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      .price_year = as.integer(year) + 1L,
      .soy_price_lagged = .price_soy,
      .cattle_price_lagged = .price_cattle
    )

  out = dat %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.price_year = as.integer(as.character(year))) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(prices_lagged, by = ".price_year") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      soy_price_lagged_level = .soy_price_lagged,
      cattle_price_lagged_level = .cattle_price_lagged
    )

  stopifnot(!anyNA(out[c(
    "soy_price_lagged_level", "cattle_price_lagged_level"
  )]))

  out %>%
    dplyr::select(
      -.price_year, -.soy_price_lagged, -.cattle_price_lagged
    )
}

# Join the Copernicus ERA5-Drought SPEI-12 endpoint aligned to each outcome
# window. Calendar year t uses December t (January--December); PRODES year t
# uses July t (August t-1--July t). Only the endpoint used by that panel is
# required, avoiding irrelevant missing-value restrictions.
add_spei12_anchor = function(dat, panel = c("calendar", "prodes")) {
  panel = match.arg(panel)
  value_name = if (panel == "calendar") "spei12_dec" else "spei12_jul"
  if (value_name %in% names(dat) && all(is.finite(dat[[value_name]]))) {
    return(dat)
  }
  file_name = if (panel == "calendar") {
    "spei12_copernicus_era5_normalyr.RDS"
  } else {
    "spei12_copernicus_era5_prodesyr.RDS"
  }
  drought = readRDS(file.path(DATA_DIR, "processed", file_name)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      codmun = as.numeric(codmun),
      year = as.numeric(year)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(codmun, year, dplyr::all_of(value_name))
  stopifnot(
    !anyDuplicated(drought[c("codmun", "year")]),
    all(is.finite(drought[[value_name]]))
  )

  n_before = nrow(dat)
  out = dat %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("spei12_dec", "spei12_jul"))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      codmun = as.numeric(codmun),
      year = as.numeric(year)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(drought, by = c("codmun", "year"))
  stopifnot(
    nrow(out) == n_before,
    all(is.finite(out[[value_name]]))
  )
  out
}

# Predetermined fire susceptibility used in the selected specification. DETER
# fire-scar observations in the processed panel begin in August 2016. Accumulate
# their municipal area through December 2021 and scale by fixed 2021 forest area.
# Repeatedly burned land can contribute in more than one period, so this is an
# accumulated exposure measure rather than a unique-area share. Its level is
# absorbed by municipality fixed effects. The time-varying control below is its
# interaction with December SPEI-12 for calendar outcomes and July SPEI-12 for
# PRODES-year outcomes; SPEI-12 itself also remains in Model II.
add_pre2022_fire_scar_spei = function(dat) {
  spei12_var = intersect(c("spei12_dec", "spei12_jul"), names(dat))
  stopifnot(
    length(spei12_var) == 1L,
    "pre2022_fire_scar_intensity" %in% names(dat)
  )

  out = dat %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      spei12_fire_scar_interaction =
        .data[[spei12_var]] * pre2022_fire_scar_intensity
    )

  stopifnot(
    all(is.finite(out$pre2022_fire_scar_intensity)),
    all(out$pre2022_fire_scar_intensity >= 0),
    all(is.finite(out$spei12_fire_scar_interaction))
  )
  out
}

# ── Headline normalization denominator (v3) ───────────────────────────────────
# THE document-wide switch. v2 normalized every area/count outcome by municipal
# area; v3 normalizes by municipal FOREST area, because degradation can only
# occur where forest stands, so the denominator is the area at risk. Set here,
# ahead of the variable-label table, so labels and numbers are generated from the
# same source and cannot disagree. Applied in DataNormalization /
# DataNormalizationProdes; setting it back to "areamun" restores v2's headline
# exactly, without editing a single call site.
norm_denom = "area_forest" # "area_forest" = v3 headline | "areamun" = v2
stopifnot(norm_denom %in% c("area_forest", "areamun"))

# Printed units, derived from the switch. The var_names relabelling below and the
# Outcome-normalization robustness subsection both read these.
norm_area_unit = if (norm_denom == "area_forest") {
  "% forest area"
} else {
  "% munic. area"
}
# DETER/PRODES flags and fines are reported per count_scale km² of fixed 2021
# forest area. Ignitions use municipal area because they may originate outside
# the forest. v3 reports per 100 km²; set to 1000 to restore the earlier scale.
count_scale = 100
count_scale_label = format(count_scale, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)

norm_count_unit = if (norm_denom == "area_forest") {
  # Keep table cells and figure axes compact. Their notes state that the
  # denominator is each municipality's fixed 2021 forest area.
  sprintf("per %s km²", count_scale_label)
} else {
  sprintf("per %s km²", count_scale_label)
}

# Ignitions are observed across the whole municipality, including agricultural
# and other non-forest land. Their headline density therefore uses municipal
# area even though degradation flags and enforcement fines retain the fixed-2021
# forest denominator.
ignition_count_unit = sprintf("per %s km² munic. area", count_scale_label)

# ── Control set: THE single source of truth ───────────────────────────────────
# Add or remove a covariate by editing ONLY the vectors below. Everything else is
# derived from them:
#   * DataNormalization and DataNormalizationProdes build the year-interaction
#     columns via add_ctrl_interactions(), so both panels always carry the same
#     set;
#   * covlist's Model 2 is generated via ctrl_x_names(), so the formula can never
#     name a column that was not built.
# Keeping covlist in sync by hand is what left `x22_area_forest` in the formula
# after `area_forest` was dropped from the control list, and the render only
# discovered it 18 chunks in, inside feols.
#
# ctrl_interact    interacted with the year dummies in ctrl_interact_years. Any
#                  column on the panel works, including ones DataNormalization
#                  derives later (`r_way_road`): the names are resolved when the
#                  panel is built, not here.
# ctrl_uninteract  entered with their own main effects and no year interaction.
#                  These are the time-VARYING controls, which is exactly why they
#                  need a main effect (see the base-year note in
#                  DataNormalization).
# ── The control set ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Geography (density, coordinates, distance to the coast and to Brasilia) plus
# two transport-access terms: paved road density and operating railway density.
# Each is a fixed municipal characteristic interacted with the year dummies, so
# it enters as a differential trend rather than a level.
#
# Paved and unpaved road density are entered separately, following Pfaff (1999,
# JEEM 37:26-43), which covers the same region and the same outcome family.
# Roads are held at MUNICIPAL area because they mostly lie outside forest, so the
# forest denominator would be the wrong one for them.
#
# Time-varying controls (temperature, precipitation, GEO subscriptions, and the
# two price-suitability interactions) enter with their own main effects and no
# year interaction. SPEI-12 is also uninteracted, but its endpoint differs by
# panel and is therefore added to Model II separately below.
ctrl_interact = c(
  "dens", # population and area within the Legal Amazon panel boundary
  "lat",
  "lon",
  "dist_coast",
  "dist_brasilia",
  "r_way_road_pav",
  "r_way_rail_oper"
)
ctrl_uninteract = c(
  "tmax",
  "prcp",
  "geosat",
  # SPEI-12 remains in Model II separately; this term allows drought effects to
  # vary with predetermined accumulated fire-scar exposure.
  "spei12_fire_scar_interaction",
  "soyield_ful_mun_high:soy_price_lagged_level",
  "pasture_suit_mun:cattle_price_lagged_level"
)
ctrl_model_ii_extra_calendar = "spei12_dec"
ctrl_model_ii_extra_prodes = "spei12_jul"
# Raw columns required to evaluate the formula terms above. Keep this separate
# from ctrl_uninteract because interaction expressions are not data-frame names.
ctrl_uninteract_vars = unique(all.vars(stats::as.formula(paste(
  "~", paste(ctrl_uninteract, collapse = " + ")
))))

# ── Base year and the two interaction sets ────────────────────────────────────
# 2022 is the omitted base EVERYWHERE: the instrument set skips ca_2022, and the
# control-by-year interactions skip 2022 as well. One base year for both halves
# of the model, so a coefficient is always read against the same reference.
#
# Two sets, because the two panels have different year support:
#   ctrl_interact_years   2023, 2024              -- the 2SLS sample (2022-2024)
#   ctrl_placebo_years    2017-2021, 2023, 2024   -- the full panel behind the
#                                                    event-study placebo
# The placebo set is a superset, so it is also what gets BUILT on both panels;
# the 2SLS formula simply names the subset it can identify.
#
# WHY THE PLACEBO NEEDS ITS OWN SET (this is the v3 bug this replaces). Until
# now both halves used a fixed {2022, 2023}. On the 2SLS sample that is a
# harmless relabelling -- every interacted control is time-invariant, so the
# municipality FE absorbs its total and the omitted base is not identified. On
# the FULL panel it is not harmless: x22_/x23_ columns are identically zero on
# every 2017-2021 row, so the pre-period leads were estimated with no covariate
# conditioning at all. The placebo was therefore testing an UNCONDITIONAL
# pre-trend while the design's exogeneity claim is a CONDITIONAL one, and any
# specification ranked on that placebo was ranked on the wrong null.
ctrl_base_year = 2022
ctrl_interact_years = setdiff(2022:CAL_END_YEAR, ctrl_base_year)
ctrl_placebo_years = setdiff(2017:CAL_END_YEAR, ctrl_base_year)

# Identified calendar-year instruments. With municipality FE, the sum of all
# coverarea-by-year instruments is the time-invariant coverarea level, so one
# year must be omitted. Passing ca_2022 as well makes the OP covariance problem
# rank-deficient.
calendar_iv_names = paste0("ca_", ctrl_interact_years)

# Interaction columns needed by ROBUSTNESS models that are not in the headline
# set. Listed here only so the columns get built; they enter no model unless a
# covlist entry names them. Example: the cubic-geography Model 3 needs
# c("lat2", "lon2", "latlon", "lat3", "lon3", "lat2lon", "latlon2").
ctrl_interact_extra = character(0)

# Column names for the interactions: x23_<var>, x24_<var> on the 2SLS sample and
# x17_<var> ... x24_<var> on the placebo panel, grouped BY VARIABLE so the result
# table's covariate block reads in the order written above.
ctrl_x_names = function(vars, years = ctrl_interact_years) {
  yy = substr(as.character(years), 3, 4)
  unlist(lapply(vars, function(v) sprintf("x%s_%s", yy, v)), use.names = FALSE)
}

# Builds those columns on any panel. Called by both normalization chunks, so the
# PRODES panel cannot fall out of step with the calendar panel. Defaults to the
# PLACEBO year set (every non-base year), so the full-panel formulas always find
# their columns; the 2SLS formula names only the post-period subset.
add_ctrl_interactions = function(
  dat,
  vars = union(ctrl_interact, ctrl_interact_extra),
  years = ctrl_placebo_years
) {
  absent = setdiff(vars, names(dat))
  if (length(absent)) {
    stop(
      "ctrl_interact / ctrl_interact_extra name controls that are not on the ",
      "panel: ", paste(absent, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }
  for (v in vars) {
    for (yy in years) {
      dat[[sprintf("x%s_%s", substr(as.character(yy), 3, 4), v)]] =
        dat[[v]] * (as.character(dat$year) == as.character(yy))
    }
  }
  dat
}

# ---- run settings ------------------------------------------------------------
# Share of microregions sampled in the leave-one-microregion-out sweep; 1 = all.
loo_microregion_share = as.numeric(Sys.getenv(
  "STARLINK_LOO_MICROREGION_SHARE",
  unset = "1"
))

# Parallel workers for the leave-one-out and leave-one-state-out sweeps. This is
# the single largest cost in the document -- raise it on a machine with cores to
# spare.
robust_max_workers = as.integer(Sys.getenv(
  "STARLINK_ROBUST_MAX_WORKERS",
  unset = "3"
))

stopifnot(
  is.numeric(loo_microregion_share), length(loo_microregion_share) == 1,
  loo_microregion_share >= 0, loo_microregion_share <= 1,
  is.numeric(robust_max_workers), length(robust_max_workers) == 1,
  robust_max_workers >= 1
)
robust_max_workers = as.integer(robust_max_workers)
```

```{r Initialization, include=FALSE, dev="ragg_png"}
options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE, width = 200)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev = "ragg_png",
  eval = TRUE,
  echo = FALSE,
  results = "markup",
  fig.show = "asis"
)
try(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "pt_BR.UTF-8"), silent = TRUE) # for special chars

# Loading required R packages
library(fixest)
# fixest's default OpenMP multithreading segfaults (Windows access violation,
# exit code 0xC0000005) inside the headline `feols` loop. Force single-threaded
# estimation globally so every chunk matches the explicit `setFixest_nthreads(1)`
# calls already used in the later robustness sections.
fixest::setFixest_nthreads(1)

# Belt-and-suspenders for the 0xC0000005 segfault: run the single-thread +
# native-state reset before EVERY chunk via a knitr chunk hook, so the long
# unguarded feols sweeps (the Anderson-Rubin grid inversions, the share-balance
# wild-cluster bootstrap, the heterogeneity loops, the placebo loops) get the
# same protection as the chunks that already call setFixest_estimation(reset =
# TRUE) explicitly. Wrapped in try() so a hook failure can never abort the render.
knitr::knit_hooks$set(fixest_reset = function(before, ...) {
  if (isTRUE(before)) {
    try(
      {
        fixest::setFixest_nthreads(1)
        fixest::setFixest_estimation(reset = TRUE)
      },
      silent = TRUE
    )
  }
  invisible(NULL)
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fixest_reset = TRUE)

DETER_zip = "INPE/deter-amz-public-2026mar29.zip"

# Function for turning first character to upper case
first_upper = function(string) {
  substr(string, 1, 1) = toupper(substr(string, 1, 1))
  return(string)
}
```

```{r VariableNames, echo=F}
colnames(var_names) = c("var", "varname", "type")

# ── Units under the active normalization (v3) ─────────────────────────────────
# The labels above are written in v2's municipal-area units. Rather than editing
# ~90 label strings by hand (and risking one that disagrees with the number
# printed next to it), rewrite the unit text for exactly the rows the
# normalization switch touches: the `r_`-prefixed area and count outcomes.
#
# NOT touched, deliberately:
#   rt_*      tenure-area normalization, unchanged by the switch
#   sh_/shm_  cover transitions; both already carry their own correct base in the
#             label ("% prior-year forest" and "% munic. area" respectively), so
#             there is nothing to rewrite
#   het rows  covariate/heterogeneity labels, not outcomes
# The count-unit substitution must also run when the denominator is municipal
# area but count_scale has moved off 1,000; the area gsub is then a no-op.
if (norm_denom != "areamun" || count_scale != 1000) {
  .relab = startsWith(var_names$var, "r_") & var_names$type == "out"
  .lab = var_names$varname[.relab]
  .lab = gsub("% munic. area", norm_area_unit, .lab, fixed = TRUE)
  .lab = gsub("per 1,000 km²", norm_count_unit, .lab, fixed = TRUE)
  var_names$varname[.relab] = .lab
  rm(.lab)
  rm(.relab)
}

# The replication package carries only the seven forest-transition outcomes
# used in the calendar results. They are rebased below on the fixed 2021 forest
# stock. shm_agr_pec is retained separately for the municipal-area robustness
# row; no other municipal-denominator transition is estimated.
cover_outcomes = paste0(
  "sh21_",
  c("for2non", "veg", "agr_pec", "agr_agr")
)
```


---

# Normal Year

**Calendar-year panel: Jan 2022 to Dec `r CAL_END_YEAR`.**

```{r DataNormalization, echo=F}
# Dataset and normalization
# The compact calendar panel runs from 2017 through 2024. All non-PRODES
# outcomes use this basis; only the separate native-PRODES panel reaches 2025.
# Latitude, longitude, distance to Brasilia and distance to the coast now come
# directly from the panel, all measured from IBGE municipal-seat points.

# Operating railway now ships on the panel. work_dataframe.Rmd measures it once,
# after a single intersection with the municipal layer, so `way_rail` is the
# operating-network kilometre count (about 2,902 km inside the Legal Amazon) and
# is used directly as the eighth control's input.

# .RDS, not .dta. The RDS retains the full names of the 99 required columns;
# Stata's 32-character limit requires abbreviations in the companion export.
panel_path = paste0(panel_dir, "dataset_normalyr.RDS")
dta = readRDS(panel_path)
if (ncol(dta) != 99L) {
  stop("dataset_normalyr.RDS must follow the compact 99-column contract")
}
if (!identical(attr(dta, "coordinate_basis"), "ibge_municipal_seat")) {
  stop("Rebuild the v3 panel: its coordinates and distances are not marked as IBGE-seat based")
}
if (!identical(attr(dta, "faction_report_years"), c(2023L, 2024L)) ||
    !identical(attr(dta, "faction_time_varying"), FALSE)) {
  stop("Rebuild the panel with the time-invariant 2023--2024 faction definition")
}
dta = dta %>%
  filter(year >= 2017 & year <= CAL_END_YEAR & !is.na(coverarea)) %>%
  {
    stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(.$codmun) == 772)
    .
  } %>%
  # Road surfaces, coordinates, CHIRTS-ERA5 Tmax, CHIRPS precipitation, and
  # distances ship on the panel.
  add_lagged_price_controls() %>%
  add_spei12_anchor("calendar") %>%
  add_pre2022_fire_scar_spei() %>%
  mutate(year = factor(year, levels = as.character(CAL_END_YEAR:2017))) %>%
  fastDummies::dummy_cols("year") %>%
  mutate(
    # `way_`-prefixed so the normalization loop builds the r_/rm_ version per
    # municipal area x100 without a second convention being introduced here.
    # Operating railway; `way_rail` is measured on the panel.
    way_rail_oper = way_rail,
    ca_2017 = year_2017 * coverarea,
    ca_2018 = year_2018 * coverarea,
    ca_2019 = year_2019 * coverarea,
    ca_2020 = year_2020 * coverarea,
    ca_2021 = year_2021 * coverarea,
    ca_2022 = year_2022 * coverarea,
    ca_2023 = year_2023 * coverarea,
    ca_2024 = year_2024 * coverarea,
    sh_for2non = 1 - sh_flo,

    # ── Cover transitions rebased on the FIXED 2021 forest stock ──────────────
    # The pipeline writes sh_* over PRIOR-YEAR forest cells
    rebase21 = lag_areaforest / areaforest_2021,
    sh21_for2non = (1 - sh_flo) * rebase21,
    sh21_flo = sh_flo * rebase21,
    sh21_veg = sh_veg * rebase21,
    sh21_agr_pec = sh_agr_pec * rebase21,
    sh21_agr_agr = sh_agr_agr * rebase21,
    sh21_agr_out = sh_agr_out * rebase21,
    sh21_nvg_min = sh_nvg_min * rebase21,
    sh21_nvg_urb = sh_nvg_urb * rebase21,

    # lpop = log(pop),
    # r_degr_flag = area_mun_deter_degr / n_mun_deter_degr,
    # rf_n_igni_deter = (n_igni_deter / area_mun_deter_degr_fire) / 1000,
    uc_dummy = ifelse(areauc > 0, 1, 0),
    sett_dummy = ifelse(areasett > 0, 1, 0),
    ndpf_dummy = ifelse(areandpf > 0, 1, 0)
  ) %>%
  select(-starts_with("year_20"))


# ── Normalization denominators ────────────────────────────────────────────────
tenure_denom = c(
  ti = "areati",
  uc = "areauc",
  sett = "areasett",
  ndpf = "areandpf",
  # v2 SICAR: the outcome masks are NET of public land, so the denominator must
  # be the net area too. `areasicar21_large_g` / `_small_g` are the gross
  # versions and pairing them here would inflate the denominator by roughly a
  # third and deflate every rt_ rate.
  sicar21_large = "areasicar21_large",
  sicar21_small = "areasicar21_small",

  # Claims over public land BY CLAIM SIZE
  over_ndpf_large = "areaover_ndpf_large",
  over_ndpf_small = "areaover_ndpf_small"
)

# ── Zero tenure areas → NA in tenure-level outcomes ──────────────────────────
for (tag in names(tenure_denom)) {
  denom_col = tenure_denom[[tag]]
  tenure_vars = colnames(dta)[grepl(
    paste0("^(area|n)_", tag, "_"),
    colnames(dta)
  )]
  dta = dta %>%
    mutate(across(
      all_of(tenure_vars),
      ~ if_else(dta[[denom_col]] == 0, NA_real_, .)
    ))
}

# Returns the matching tenure area column, or NULL if none applies.
get_tenure_denom = function(varname, prefix) {
  remainder = sub(paste0("^", prefix), "", varname)
  for (tag in names(tenure_denom)) {
    if (startsWith(remainder, paste0(tag, "_"))) return(tenure_denom[[tag]])
  }
  return(NULL)
}

# ── Headline normalization denominator (v3 change) ────────────────────────────
# v2 normalized every area/count outcome by MUNICIPAL area. v3 normalizes by
# municipal FOREST area: degradation can only happen where forest stands, so the
# denominator is the area at risk rather than the whole municipality.
#
# `norm_denom` below is the ONLY place the headline denominator is set. Every
# `r_`-prefixed outcome in this document is built from it -- result tables,
# figures, event-study placebos, weak-IV diagnostics, LOO/LOSO robustness,
# heterogeneity, PRODES -- so setting norm_denom = "areamun" reproduces v2's
# headline exactly without editing a single call site.
#
# The municipal-area version is ALWAYS built in parallel under the `rm_` prefix.
# That is what the Outcome-normalization robustness subsection compares the
# headline against, so both conventions exist on the panel at once.
#
# Deliberately EXCLUDED from the switch:
#   way_*    road length is a CONTROL (`r_way_road`, entered as year
#            interactions), not an outcome. It stays on municipal area so v3's
#            control set differs from v2's only by `lpop`. An alternative variant instead
#            rebuilds road density as way_road / area_forest; that variant is
#            reported in the normalization robustness subsection rather than
#            adopted here, because changing a control and the outcome
#            denominator in the same step makes the two impossible to separate.
#   r_<norm_denom>  identically 100 under its own denominator, so it is dropped
#            below exactly as v2 dropped r_areamun.
stopifnot(exists("norm_denom"), norm_denom %in% names(dta))
stopifnot(all(dta[[norm_denom]] > 0, na.rm = TRUE))

# Whether the denominator is time-invariant decides whether "forest area" means
# contemporaneous or baseline forest. In this build it is a single
# cross-sectional value per municipality, so the two coincide and the
# normalization is a pure cross-sectional rescaling. Checked rather than
# assumed: if a later build makes forest extent time-varying, the
# prior-year-forest variant in the robustness subsection becomes the relevant
# comparison and this message flips.
norm_denom_time_invariant = dta %>%
  group_by(codmun) %>%
  summarise(sd_den = sd(.data[[norm_denom]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pull(sd_den) %>%
  {
    all(. < 1e-10, na.rm = TRUE)
  }

# ── Area outcomes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
area_list = colnames(dta)[
  startsWith(colnames(dta), "area") |
    startsWith(colnames(dta), "way")
]
for (y in area_list) {
  # rm_ = v2's municipal-area convention, always built (robustness subsection).
  dta[[paste0("rm_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[["areamun"]]) * 100 # % munic. area
  # r_ = the headline convention, on the active denominator. Road density is a
  # control and is held at municipal area (see the note above).
  dta[[paste0("r_", y)]] = if (startsWith(y, "way")) {
    dta[[paste0("rm_", y)]]
  } else {
    (dta[[y]] / dta[[norm_denom]]) * 100 # norm_area_unit
  }

  td = if (startsWith(y, "area_")) get_tenure_denom(y, "area_") else NULL
  if (!is.null(td)) {
    dta[[paste0("rt_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[[td]]) * 100 # % tenure area
  }
}

# ── Count outcomes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_list = colnames(dta)[
  startsWith(colnames(dta), "n_") |
    startsWith(colnames(dta), "offend_")
]
for (y in n_list) {
  dta[[paste0("rm_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[["areamun"]]) * count_scale # per count_scale km² munic.
  dta[[paste0("r_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[[norm_denom]]) * count_scale # norm_count_unit

  td = get_tenure_denom(y, "n_")
  if (!is.null(td)) {
    dta[[paste0("rt_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[[td]]) * count_scale # per count_scale km² tenure
  }
}

# Level / log / IHS of the RAW ignition count (non-area-normalized).
# THE CONSTANT IN THE LOG IS 1, and it is not innocuous. log1p(x) = log(x + 1), so the
# estimand depends on that choice: Chen & Roth (2024) show log(y + c) has no
# scale-invariant interpretation when many observations are zero, and the coefficient can
# be moved arbitrarily by moving c. IHS (asinh) has the same problem in units rather than
# in a chosen constant. Both are reported because Fabio asked for them; neither is a
# candidate for the headline, and fepois with the log-area offset remains the count model.
for (v in intersect(c("n_igni"), names(dta))) {
  dta[[paste0("log_", v)]] = log1p(dta[[v]])
  dta[[paste0("ihs_", v)]] = asinh(dta[[v]])
}

# # ── Share outcomes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Both families are forest-ORIGIN transitions; they differ only in the base
# (work_dataframe.Rmd, raster_trans):
#   sh_*  = transition cells / prior-year FOREST-origin cells  -> forest-normalized
#   sh21_*  = transition cells / 2021 FOREST-origin cells  -> forest-normalized
#   shm_* = transition cells / prior-year total MUNICIPAL cells
sh_list = colnames(dta)[grepl("^sh(m|21)?_", colnames(dta))]
for (y in sh_list) {
  dta[[y]] = dta[[y]] * 100
}


dta = dta %>%
  mutate(
    areamun = areamun / 1000,
    area_forest = area_forest / 1000,
    dist_coast = dist_coast / 1000,
    dist_brasilia = dist_brasilia / 1000,
  ) %>%
  # Degenerate normalizations: a denominator divided by itself is identically
  # 100. v2 dropped r_areamun; under a forest denominator r_area_forest is the
  # same degenerate column. Drop whichever applies, plus the rm_ twin.
  select(-any_of(c("r_areamun", "rm_areamun", paste0("r_", norm_denom))))

# ── Control-by-year interactions: every non-base year, 2022 omitted ───────────
# The controls are written out explicitly (rather than v2's `year:x`, which let
# fixest drop whichever term the codmun FE rendered collinear) for EVERY year
# except 2022. 2022 is the base for the instrument too, so both halves of the
# model are read against the same reference year.
#
# What this does and does not change:
#
#   * On the 2SLS estimation sample (2022-2024) it changes NOTHING relative to
#     any other base-year choice. Every interacted control here is time-invariant
#     within municipality (verified below), so the codmun FE absorbs its total
#     and any two of the three year interactions span the same space. First
#     stage and 2SLS coefficients are identical to v2's to machine precision, on
#     this build and on the 2026-07-31 export. The omitted base year
#     is not identified, which is why "reference 2022" and "reference 2024"
#     cannot differ here.
#
#   * On the FULL 2017-2024 panel used by the event-study placebo it is the
#     whole point. The earlier {2022, 2023} restriction left every x-column
#     identically zero on the pre-period rows, so the leads were estimated
#     unconditionally -- a pre-trend test of a null the design does not claim.
#     With every non-base year interacted, the pre-period gets the same
#     covariate flexibility as the post-period and the placebo finally tests
#     conditional parallel trends.
#
# The control set itself is defined ONCE in the first setup chunk
# (`ctrl_interact` / `ctrl_uninteract` / `ctrl_interact_years`), and covlist's
# Model 2 is generated from it, so adding or removing a covariate is a one-line
# edit there. Naming follows the v4 replication file (`x22_lat`, `x23_lat`, ...),
# so a coefficient can be traced between the two documents by name.
# Checked here, before anything is estimated: every control the models name must
# be present on the panel and complete. An incomplete control is not an error
# feols reports -- it silently drops the rows.
stopifnot(
  all(ctrl_interact %in% names(dta)),
  all(ctrl_uninteract_vars %in% names(dta)),
  all(is.finite(dta$spei12_dec)),
  !anyNA(dta$r_way_road_pav),
  !anyNA(dta$r_way_rail_oper),
  # The operating network inside the Legal Amazon is about 2,902 km. A total
  # near 3,886 means the railway double-count is back in the panel.
  abs(sum(dta$way_rail[dta$year == CAL_END_YEAR]) - 2902) < 50
)

# Retained ONLY for the interaction-structure comparison in the diagnostics
# section, which reconstructs the superseded hand-built {2022, 2023} columns to show
# what they did to the pre-period. No model in this document uses these columns any
# more -- covlist and the placebo both use `year:x`, which fixest expands from the
# year levels present in whichever sample it is given.
dta = add_ctrl_interactions(dta)

# The no-op claim above is only true for time-invariant controls, so it is
# asserted rather than trusted. Any control that varies within municipality
# would make the omitted base year identified, and moving the base to 2022 would
# then change the 2SLS as well -- in which case the choice needs its own
# justification instead of being a relabelling.
ctrl_interact_tv = vapply(
  ctrl_interact,
  function(v) {
    s = tapply(dta[[v]], dta$codmun, function(z) sd(z, na.rm = TRUE))
    any(s > 1e-10, na.rm = TRUE)
  },
  logical(1)
)
if (any(ctrl_interact_tv)) {
  warning(
    "Time-VARYING interacted controls present (",
    paste(names(ctrl_interact_tv)[ctrl_interact_tv], collapse = ", "),
    "): the omitted base year is now identified, so the choice of 2022 as the ",
    "base is no longer a relabelling of the 2SLS."
  )
}

dta_normal = dta
```

```{r ClusterSchemeSwitch, echo=F}
# ============================================================================
# MAIN STANDARD-ERROR CLUSTERING SCHEME -- microregion (IBGE 2017 RGI) cluster
# ============================================================================
# Every headline / result-table / figure / robustness / weak-IV estimate
# clusters on `main_cluster_form`; printed scheme labels read `main_cluster_label`
# and `main_cluster_note`. The headline inference is
# fixed at microregion clustering -- there is no longer a document-wide switch.
#
# Microregion-only (IBGE 2017 RGI) single cluster. Municipalities nest within
# RGIs, so this allows arbitrary error correlation among municipalities within a
# microregion across all years and absorbs within-municipality serial correlation
# (Cameron-Gelbach-Miller 2011).
main_cluster_form = ~microreg
main_cluster_chars = "microreg"
main_cluster_scheme = "micro" # key into se_summary()
main_cluster_label = "microregion"
main_cluster_note = paste0(
  "microregion (RGI) clustering allows arbitrary error correlation among ",
  "municipalities within a microregion across all years (single-cluster scheme)"
)

```

```{r DescriptiveStatistics, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F}
# function to format mean ± sd
fmt = function(x, digits = 2) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  m = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  s = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f ± %.", digits, "f"), m, s)
}


for (period in list(2017:2021, 2022:CAL_END_YEAR)) {
  # create empty tab with names in first column and NA for groups
  tab = data.frame(
    Name = var_names$varname[match(vars, var_names$var)],
    MeanSD = NA_character_,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE

    dplyr::mutate(desc_year = as.integer(as.character(year))) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(desc_prices, by = "desc_year") %>%
    dplyr::filter(desc_year %in% period) %>%

      pop = pop / 1000,
      # FGGD stores the official 0--100 Pasture Suitability Index with
      # two implied decimal places, so native raster values are divided by 100.
      pasture_suit_desc = pasture_suit_mun / 100,
      N = 1
    )
  stopifnot(!anyNA(dta2[c("soy_price_current", "cattle_price_current")]))
  i = 1
  # fill tab by looping over vars
  for (var in vars) {
    colvals = dta2[[var]]
    # compute per-group formatted strings
    tab$MeanSD[i] = fmt(colvals)
    i = i + 1
  }

  tab = rbind(colnames(tab), c("N", nrow(dta2) / length(period)), tab)
  colnames(tab) = NULL

  assign(
    paste0("tab_stat_", first(period), "_", last(period)),
    format(tab, justify = "left")
  )
}
```

```{r FigureAXDroughtFireMap, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=8.5, dpi=150}
figure_ax_years = 2021:2024

# Use the panel-matched 772-unit municipal geometry and its Albers equal-area
# projection. SPEI-12 is already joined to the analysis panel, so the map and
# the regression use the same coverage-area-weighted municipal values.
figure_ax_mun = readRDS(mun_legal_amazon_geometry) %>%
  sf::st_make_valid() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(codmun = as.numeric(codmun)) %>%
  dplyr::select(codmun)
figure_ax_crs = sf::st_crs(figure_ax_mun)$wkt

figure_ax_metadata = dta %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    codmun = as.numeric(codmun),
    uf
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

figure_ax_states = figure_ax_mun %>%
  dplyr::left_join(figure_ax_metadata, by = "codmun") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(uf) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(.groups = "drop") %>%
  sf::st_make_valid()

figure_ax_spei = dta %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    codmun = as.numeric(codmun),
    year = as.integer(as.character(year)),
    spei12_dec
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year %in% figure_ax_years) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()
stopifnot(
  nrow(figure_ax_spei) == 772L * length(figure_ax_years),
  !anyDuplicated(figure_ax_spei[c("codmun", "year")]),
  all(is.finite(figure_ax_spei$spei12_dec))
)

figure_ax_drought = figure_ax_mun %>%
  dplyr::left_join(figure_ax_spei, by = "codmun") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    spei12_display = pmax(pmin(spei12_dec, 0), -6),
    panel = factor(year, levels = figure_ax_years)
  )

# Compact submission-local inputs reproduce the fixed 2021 coverage layer and
# the 2021--2024 DETER fire-scar polygons without relying on external paths.
figure_ax_mobile = readRDS(file.path(
  DATA_DIR,
  "processed",
  "figure1_mobile_coverage.RDS"
)) %>%
  sf::st_make_valid() %>%
  sf::st_transform(figure_ax_crs)
figure_ax_fire = readRDS(file.path(
  DATA_DIR,
  "processed",
  "figure_ax_deter_fire_2021_2024.RDS"
)) %>%
  sf::st_transform(figure_ax_crs) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(panel = factor(year, levels = figure_ax_years))
stopifnot(setequal(sort(unique(figure_ax_fire$year)), figure_ax_years))

# Rasterization is for legibility only. The outcome construction continues to
# use the original DETER polygons.
figure_ax_template = terra::rast(
  terra::ext(terra::vect(figure_ax_mun)),
  resolution = 2000,
  crs = figure_ax_crs
)
figure_ax_mobile_raster = terra::rasterize(
  terra::vect(figure_ax_mobile),
  figure_ax_template,
  field = 1,
  background = NA,
  touches = TRUE
)
figure_ax_mobile_cells = terra::as.data.frame(
  figure_ax_mobile_raster,
  xy = TRUE,
  na.rm = TRUE
) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(x, y)

figure_ax_fire_cells = lapply(figure_ax_years, function(year_i) {
  year_raster = terra::rasterize(
    terra::vect(figure_ax_fire %>% dplyr::filter(year == year_i)),
    figure_ax_template,

    background = NA,
    touches = TRUE

    dplyr::transmute(
      x,
      y,
      panel = factor(year_i, levels = figure_ax_years)
    )
}) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows()
```

```{r Covariates, echo=F}
covlist = list(
  # Model 1 - No covariates
  c("1"),

  # Model 2 - Full covariates with GEO subscriptions and Copernicus SPEI-12
  #
  # GENERATED from the control set in the first setup chunk. Add or drop a
  # covariate there and this model, the placebo list, and the covariate block of
  # every result table all follow.
  #
  # BACK TO `year:x` (Fabio, 2026-08-11), reverting the hand-built x22_/x23_
  # columns. Writing the interactions out manually was a mistake, and the placebo
  # is where it bit: a hand-written list has to name the pre-period years too, and
  # the first version named only {2022, 2023}. Those columns are identically ZERO
  # on every 2017-2021 row, so the pre-period was left UNCONDITIONED and the
  # pre-trend test was silently an unconditional one. Nothing errored -- the
  # formula was valid, the columns existed, the numbers looked plausible.
  #
  # `year:x` cannot make that mistake: fixest generates one term per year level
  # PRESENT IN THE SAMPLE, so the 2SLS support gets 2023-2024 and the full placebo
  # panel gets 2017-2021 plus 2023-2024, automatically and with no year list to
  # keep in sync. It also removes the need for a separate `covs_placebo`.
  #
  # Verified equivalent where both are correct:
  # on the 2SLS sample b = 0.26604162 either way, identical to 1e-10, and every
  # placebo lead and lag matches to 1e-9. `year:` keeps one more interaction level
  # (67 coefficients against 66) because it drops a different collinear term, which
  # moves the joint pre-trend p only in the fifth decimal (0.107813 vs 0.107833).
  # The equivalence holds because every interacted control is time-INVARIANT within
  # municipality: the FE absorbs its total, so any n-1 of n year interactions span
  # the same space and the choice of dropped level is a relabelling.
  #
  # ctrl_uninteract stays uninteracted: weather, satellite coverage, and the
  # lagged-price-by-suitability controls already vary over time and therefore
  # carry their own main effects.
  # To add soy-yield potential: put "soyield_ful_mun_high" in ctrl_interact.
  c(
    paste0("year:", ctrl_interact),
    ctrl_uninteract,
    ctrl_model_ii_extra_calendar
  )#,

  # Model 3 - Model 2 with geography as a THIRD-DEGREE bivariate polynomial in
  # latitude and longitude instead of the linear pair, each term interacted with
  # year dummies. Follows Araujo et al. (2025, transportation), the closest
  # comparison paper and one already cited in the exclusion-restriction
  # discussion, which controls for "third-degree polynomials of latitude and
  # longitude interacted with time dummies". The polynomial terms themselves
  # (lat2, lon2, latlon, ...) are built in DataNormalization; the municipality FE
  # absorbs every time-invariant spatial term, so they do work only through the
  # year interaction.
  #
  # To enable: uncomment the entry below. Under `year:x` the polynomial terms need
  # only exist as plain columns on the panel (DataNormalization builds lat2, lon2,
  # latlon, ... from the raw coordinates); no interaction columns have to be
  # pre-built and no year list has to be maintained.
  # Priced on the N03 base before being left disabled: the SQUARES are the
  # problem, not the curvature as such. lon2 correlates -0.663 with lon, so
  # adding it contributes collinearity rather than shape, and OP F falls from
  # 15.2 to 11.9-13.3 -- at or below the MOP13 threshold of 12.17 -- while UPF
  # loses 5%. The lat*lon INTERACTION alone is the one curvature term that
  # survives (UPF p = .049, PM1 p = .0023, OP F 14.4). Every curvature variant
  # strengthens PM1 to 0.53-0.62, so this is the lever if PM1 ever needs
  # defending on its own; it just costs the UPF result.
  # c(
  #   paste0("year:", c(
  #     "lat", "lon", "lat2", "lon2", "latlon", "lat3", "lon3", "lat2lon",
  #     "latlon2", "dens", "dist_coast", "dist_brasilia",
  #     "r_way_road_pav", "r_way_road_unpav_c", "r_way_rail_oper"
  #   )),
  #   ctrl_uninteract
  # )
)

covs = unique(unlist(covlist))[unique(unlist(covlist)) != "1"]

# Fail fast on a covariate that is not on the panel. Without this, a covlist term
# naming a column that was never built survives until the first feols call --
# which is how a dropped `area_forest` still produced `x22_area_forest` in the
# formula and killed a render 18 chunks in. Terms containing an operator (`:`,
# `^`, `(`) are formula expressions that fixest resolves itself, so they are

cov_terms_check = setdiff(unique(unlist(covlist)), "1")

# message(
```

```{r EstimationsSetupSE, message=F, warning=F, echo=F}
# Standard-error infrastructure shared by the per-scheme Estimations subsections
# below and by the `## Standard Errors` comparison table further down. The
# inference schemes shown as subsections share ONE point estimate (the choice of
# variance estimator never moves the coefficient), so the headline 2SLS is fit
# once per (model, outcome) on `d_se` (see the Estimations engine chunk) and each
# scheme's SE / stars / CI / t / p is read off that fit via summary(est, ...).

# Headline (full) covariate set = the last model in covlist. Defined here because
# the diagnostics and heterogeneity chunks below reuse it (they guard on
# exists("covs_full")).
covs_full = covlist[[covs_headline_idx]]

# Estimation data for every model. microreg / microreg_year feed the cluster
# schemes. microreg (IBGE 2017 RGI, the official successor to the microrregiao)
# ships on dta from work_dataframe.Rmd section 1; municipalities nest within
# RGIs, so clustering by microregion already absorbs within-municipality serial
# correlation (Cameron-Gelbach-Miller 2011).
d_se = dta %>%
  filter(reg_sample == 1) %>%
  mutate(microreg_year = paste(microreg, year, sep = "_"))

# Count-conditional permutation-null EXCESS outcomes = observed index - permutation
# mean (the conc_*_*_cnull columns from build_cnull_panel in work_dataframe.Rmd).
# The primary count-robust test; created only when the _cnull columns exist (post
# .dta rebuild), so the document stays knittable against the current .dta.
add_cnull_excess = function(dat) {
  pairs = c("conc_igni_hhiunb", "conc_igni_max3",
            "conc_hot_hhiunb",  "conc_hot_max3",  "conc_hot_gini")
  for (v in pairs) {
    cn = paste0(v, "_cnull")
    if (all(c(v, cn) %in% names(dat))) dat[[paste0(v, "_excess")]] = dat[[v]] - dat[[cn]]
  }
  dat
}
d_se = add_cnull_excess(d_se)

# `lat`/`lon` must never enter a covariate list as bare columns: the geography
# controls enter as PRE-BUILT interaction columns (x22_lat / x23_lat, built in
# DataNormalization). Asserted rather than assumed.
stopifnot(!any(c("lat", "lon") %in% unlist(covlist)))

# The inference schemes consumed by the per-scheme Estimations subsections and
# the Standard-Errors comparison table. The fit is identical across schemes;
# only the variance estimator differs.
#   micro           = microregion (RGI) cluster -- headline / main specification.
#                     Municipalities nest within RGIs, so this allows arbitrary
#                     error correlation among municipalities within a microregion
#                     across all years and absorbs within-municipality serial
#                     correlation (Cameron-Gelbach-Miller 2011).
#   munic_microyear = two-way {municipality, microregion x year} cluster --
#                     comparator only, shown side by side in the Standard-Errors
#                     table (Assuncao et al. 2023 annual-panel benchmark).
#                     Municipality clustering absorbs within-municipality serial
#                     correlation; microregion-year clustering absorbs within-
#                     microregion spatial correlation in a given year.
se_summary = function(est, scheme) {
  switch(
    scheme,
    micro = summary(est, cluster = ~microreg),
    munic_microyear = summary(est, cluster = ~ codmun + microreg_year),
    stop("unknown SE scheme: ", scheme)
  )
}

# Olea-Pflueger simplified test under one-way clustering via
# momentfit::MOPtest(). This follows the paper's computational steps: partial out
# the included regressors and fixed effects, orthonormalize the excluded
# instruments, estimate clustered W2, then compute F_eff, K_eff, and the Patnaik
# critical value. momentfit's clustered default is HC0 with cadjust = TRUE.
op_mop_momentfit = function(
  data,
  yvar,
  controls,
  iv,
  fe_str = "codmun + interaction(uf, year)",
  cluster_col = "microreg",
  endog = "starlink",
  taus = c(0.30, 0.20, 0.10, 0.05),
  size = 0.05
) {
  empty = data.frame(
    tau = taus,
    Feff = NA_real_,
    Keff = NA_real_,
    x = NA_real_,
    critValue = NA_real_,
    pvalue = NA_real_
  )
  if (!requireNamespace("momentfit", quietly = TRUE)) {
    return(empty)
  }

  control_vars = if (length(controls)) {
    all.vars(stats::as.formula(paste("~", paste(controls, collapse = " + "))))
  } else {
    character(0)
  }
  fe_vars = all.vars(stats::as.formula(paste("~", fe_str)))
  required = unique(c(yvar, endog, iv, control_vars, fe_vars, cluster_col))
  if (length(setdiff(required, names(data)))) {
    return(empty)
  }

  data_use = droplevels(as.data.frame(data[stats::complete.cases(data[required]), ]))
  if (!nrow(data_use)) {
    return(empty)
  }
  controls_rhs = if (length(controls)) paste(controls, collapse = " + ") else "1"

  # Match fixest's estimation sample exactly. Outcome-specific panels can leave
  # municipalities with only one usable observation, which fixest removes.
  sample_fit = fixest::feols(
    stats::as.formula(paste0(yvar, " ~ ", controls_rhs, " | ", fe_str)),
    data = data_use,
    notes = FALSE,
    nthreads = 1
  )
  kept_obs = fixest::obs(sample_fit)
  if (length(kept_obs) != nrow(data_use)) {
    data_use = droplevels(data_use[kept_obs, , drop = FALSE])
  }

  partial_out = function(variable) {
    fit = fixest::feols(
      stats::as.formula(paste0(
        variable, " ~ ", controls_rhs, " | ", fe_str
      )),
      data = data_use,
      notes = FALSE,
      nthreads = 1
    )
    as.numeric(stats::residuals(fit))
  }

  z_names = paste0("z", seq_along(iv))
  mop_data = data.frame(
    mop_y = partial_out(yvar),
    mop_d = partial_out(endog),
    stats::setNames(lapply(iv, partial_out), z_names),
    cluster = data_use[[cluster_col]],
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  mop_model = momentfit::momentModel(
    stats::reformulate("mop_d", response = "mop_y", intercept = FALSE),
    stats::reformulate(z_names, intercept = FALSE),
    data = mop_data,
    vcov = "CL",
    vcovOptions = list(cluster = ~cluster)
  )

  out = lapply(taus, function(tau) {
    ans = momentfit::MOPtest(
      mop_model,
      tau = tau,
      size = size,
      estMethod = "TSLS",
      simplified = TRUE,
      print = FALSE
    )
    data.frame(tau = tau, t(ans), check.names = FALSE)
  })
  do.call(rbind, out)
}

# Outcome-specific effective F for the calendar estimation table.
op_F_calendar_outcome = function(data, yvar, controls) {
  tryCatch(
    op_mop_momentfit(
      data = data,
      yvar = yvar,
      controls = controls,
      iv = calendar_iv_names
    )$Feff[1],
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )
}
```


- Model `r as.character(as.roman(1))`: no covariates
- Model `r as.character(as.roman(length(covlist)))`: all covariates

```{r Estimations, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F}
# Single-thread fixest and reset its native estimation state before the headline
# feols sweep — the same Windows ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xC0000005) guard the
# robustness chunks use (e.g. RobustTrim). The global setFixest_nthreads(1) in
# Initialization is not always enough on this loop; the reset clears stale
# native state that otherwise segfaults partway through the sweep.
fixest::setFixest_nthreads(1)
fixest::setFixest_estimation(reset = TRUE)

# ── Fit-once engine ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Fit the headline 2SLS once per (model, outcome) on d_se. The default cluster is microregion (~microreg),
# the main-specification inference for this paper: microregion (RGI) clustering
# allows arbitrary error correlation among municipalities within a microregion
# across all years and absorbs within-municipality serial correlation (Cameron-
# Gelbach-Miller 2011). The fitted objects are kept in est_fits so each
# per-scheme subsection can read off its SE via summary(est, ...) without re-
# fitting (the SE choice never moves the point estimate). bd_fig (full model,
# microregion cluster) is built here and feeds the Result tables and Fig 2-Fig 6
# downstream.
n_models = length(covlist)
est_fits = vector("list", n_models)

# ── The two estimation frames, as STABLE named objects ────────────────────────
# THE ONE THING NOT TO REFACTOR HERE. feols stores its `data` argument as an
# EXPRESSION, not a copy, and summary(est, cluster = ~microreg) re-evaluates that
# expression later to fetch the cluster variable. So the frame must still be
# reachable under the same name, with the same rows, when print_se_result_table
# runs -- which is long after this loop ends.
#
# Writing this as a per-iteration `d_y = igni_sample(d_se, y)` and fitting on
# `d_y` LOOKS equivalent and is not: every fit then records the name `d_y`, and
# by print time `d_y` holds whatever the last iteration left in it. Every fit
# whose row count disagrees with that leftover frame fails inside summary() with
# "Index out of bounds", and the table prints "---" for the entire half of the
# outcome list that does not match -- silently, since the failure is caught and
# rendered as a dash. Which half breaks depends only on which outcome happens to
# be last in varlist, so reordering the rows moves the damage around.
#
# Two frames are all that is needed: the ignition outcomes drop 2025, everything
# else does not. Both are bound once, here, and never reassigned. The branch is
# on the OUTSIDE of the feols call so each fit records a literal name.
#
# THE SECOND FRAME IS KEPT AS SMALL AS THE CONTRACT ALLOWS, and that is not
# fastidiousness. Because feols re-evaluates the name later, this object has to
# stay alive for the whole document -- which puts it in the environment that
# `future` walks when the leave-one-out chunks export their globals. A full copy
# of d_se pushed that estimate over the 4 GiB future.globals.maxSize cap and the
# render died in RobustOneOut / RobustOneOutProdes with "Will not launch future
# due to the size of the globals". Two things keep it cheap:
#   * it is only built when there is actually a 2025 to drop (on the <= 2024
#     build the ignition outcomes use d_se directly and no copy exists at all);
#   * it carries only the columns the ignition models read, not the several
#     hundred columns of the full panel.
# Anything the fits or their later summaries need must be in igni_model_cols --
# outcome, instrument, treatment, FE keys, every cluster variable and every
# control. A missing column errors at fit time rather than silently.
igni_needs_2025_drop = any(as.character(d_se$year) == "2025")
if (igni_needs_2025_drop) {
  igni_model_cols = intersect(
    unique(c(
      igni_outcomes,
      "starlink", "coverarea", "codmun", "uf", "year",
      "microreg", "microreg_year", # cluster schemes
      # bare column names behind the covariate formulas ("year:x" -> "x")
      unique(unlist(lapply(covlist, function(cv) {
        unlist(strsplit(gsub("year:", "", cv), ":"))
      })))
    )),
    names(d_se)
  )
  d_se_ign = dplyr::filter(
    d_se[, igni_model_cols, drop = FALSE],
    as.character(year) != "2025"
  )
}
stopifnot(
  # d_se must stay reachable and unchanged for the rest of the document.
  is.data.frame(d_se),
  !igni_needs_2025_drop ||
    (is.data.frame(d_se_ign) && nrow(d_se_ign) < nrow(d_se))
)

bd_fig = data.frame() # Store results to create figures
for (m in seq_len(n_models)) {
  cv = covlist[[m]]
  est_fits[[m]] = list()
  for (y in varlist) {
    is_ign = y %in% igni_outcomes

    model = paste0(
      y,
      " ~ ",
      # Covariates
      paste0(cv, collapse = " + "),
      " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)", # fixed-effects
      " | starlink ~ coverarea:year"
    ) %>%
      as.formula()

    # Branch outside the call, so the fit records `d_se_ign` or `d_se` by name.
    # On a build with no 2025 there is nothing to drop and no second frame, so
    # the ignition outcomes take the d_se branch like everything else.
    use_ign_frame = is_ign && igni_needs_2025_drop
    est = if (use_ign_frame) {
      feols(model, data = d_se_ign, cluster = main_cluster_form, notes = FALSE)
    } else {
      feols(model, data = d_se, cluster = main_cluster_form, notes = FALSE)
    }
    est_fits[[m]][[y]] = est

    # The frame this outcome was actually fitted on, for the dep-var mean and the
    # cluster/municipality counts below. Read-only: never fit on this.
    d_y = if (use_ign_frame) d_se_ign else d_se

    # First-stage and figure data come from the full model (last in covlist),
    # microregion-clustered (~microreg) (the main-specification inference).
    if (m == n_models) {
      if (y == varlist[1]) {
        # 1st stage results
        tab_1st = round(summary(est, stage = 1)$coeftable, 4)
        tab_1stA = fitstat(est, ~ cd + ivwald)
        tab_1stB = paste0(
          "R² = ",
          sprintf("%.4f", r2(summary(est, stage = 1))["r2"])
        )
      }

      # First-stage strength (Kleibergen--Paap rk Wald F). Identical across outcomes
      # sharing the same first-stage sample/instruments, but captured per outcome so
      # reduced-sample outcomes (e.g., the PRODES reference-year panel) carry their own.
      fstat_kp = tryCatch(
        fitstat(est, ~ivwald, simplify = FALSE)$ivwald1$stat,
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      d_op = dplyr::filter(d_y, !is.na(.data[[y]]))
      op_F_y = op_F_calendar_outcome(d_op, y, cv)

      aux = broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>%
        rename(conf.low95 = conf.low, conf.high95 = conf.high) %>%
        left_join(
          broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>%
            select(term, conf.low, conf.high) %>%
            rename(conf.low90 = conf.low, conf.high90 = conf.high),
          by = "term"
        ) %>%
        filter(term == "fit_starlink") %>%
        mutate(
          term = y,
          N = nobs(est),
          fstat_kp = fstat_kp,
          op_F = op_F_y,
          # Dep-var mean and microregion cluster count for the new table footer
          # rows. n_micro is restricted to the estimation sample (non-NA outcome
          # rows) so it is correct for outcomes that drop rows (e.g. mortality).
          ymean = mean(d_y[[y]], na.rm = TRUE),
          n_micro = dplyr::n_distinct(d_y$microreg[!is.na(d_y[[y]])]),
          n_munic = dplyr::n_distinct(d_y$codmun[!is.na(d_y[[y]])])
        )

      # Saving results for figures
      bd_fig = bind_rows(bd_fig, aux)
    }
  }
}

# Restore the global `covs` to the full covariate set, reproducing the side
# effect the legacy `for (covs in covlist)` loop left behind: downstream chunks
# read this global without redefining it first.
covs = covlist[[covs_headline_idx]]

print(paste0("Covariates (full model): ", paste(covs, collapse = ", ")))

# ── Per-scheme model-comparison table ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds and prints the Estimations model-comparison table: one column per model
# in covlist (labeled by Roman numeral, so the table widens automatically if
# models are added or removed), outcomes as rows, plus 95% CI / t / p / N for
# the full (last-in-covlist) model. The point estimate is identical across
# inference schemes; only the SE, significance stars, CI, t and p change.
# Called by the three per-scheme subsections below.
print_se_result_table = function(scheme) {
  # Scaffolding identical to the legacy single-scheme result table.
  # THE COVARIATE BLOCK IS NOT PRINTED (Fabio, 2026-08-12). It used to list every
  # control on its own row with an X per model, which on this document is ~11 rows
  # of X repeated identically in every table, on both panels, pushing the numbers
  # off the screen. The control set is stated once in the section prose and in
  # `covs` itself; the table keeps only the closing rule. Observation counts are
  # unaffected -- this table already carries N as a per-outcome COLUMN, which is
  # the right place for it here, since N varies by row (tenure-restricted
  # outcomes, mortality, the ignition rows) and a single figure at the foot would
  # be wrong for most of them.
  result = data.frame(matrix(
    ncol = 1 + length(covlist),
    nrow = 2 + 2 * length(varlist) + 1,
    data = ""
  ))
  result[1, 1 + ceiling(length(covlist) / 2)] = "Starlink"
  result[2, 1] = "Outcomes"
  result[2, 2:ncol(result)] = paste0("  (", as.roman(1:length(covlist)), ")")

  result = cbind(
    result,
    data.frame(ci95 = "", t = "", p = "", N = "", opF = "")
  )
  result[2, (ncol(result) - 4):ncol(result)] = c(
    "95% CI",
    "t-stat",
    "p-val",
    "N",
    "OP F"
  )

  # Closing rule under the last outcome.
  result[3 + 2 * length(varlist), ] = "-------"

  i = 3
  for (vardep in varlist) {
    rownames(result)[i] = paste0(vardep, "_est")
    rownames(result)[i + 1] = paste0(vardep, "_se")
    result[i, 1] = var_names$varname[which(vardep == var_names$var)]
    i = i + 2
  }

  # Fill the coefficient (scheme-invariant) and the chosen scheme's SE / stars /
  # CI / t / p / N from the pre-fitted models. CI / t / p / N are shown only for
  # the full model (last column), matching the legacy table.
  j = 2
  for (m in seq_len(n_models)) {
    for (y in varlist) {
      est = est_fits[[m]][[y]]
      s = tryCatch(se_summary(est, scheme), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(s) || !("fit_starlink" %in% rownames(s$coeftable))) {
        result[paste0(y, "_est"), j] = "---"
        next
      }
      ct = s$coeftable
      b = ct["fit_starlink", 1]
      se = ct["fit_starlink", 2]
      tval = ct["fit_starlink", 3]
      p = ct["fit_starlink", 4]

      result[paste0(y, "_est"), j] = paste0(
        sprintf("%.3f", b),
        case_when(
          p <= .01 ~ "***",
          p <= .05 ~ "**",
          p <= .10 ~ "*",
          TRUE ~ ""
        )
      )
      result[paste0(y, "_se"), j] = paste0("(", sprintf("%.3f", se), ")")

      if (m == n_models) {
        ci = tryCatch(
          as.numeric(confint(s, "fit_starlink", level = 0.95)[1, ]),
          error = function(e) c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
        )
        result[paste0(y, "_est"), "ci95"] = paste0(
          "[",
          sprintf("%.3f", ci[1]),
          ", ",
          sprintf("%.3f", ci[2]),
          "]"
        )
        result[paste0(y, "_est"), "t"] = sprintf("%.3f", tval)
        result[paste0(y, "_est"), "p"] = sprintf("%.3f", p)
        result[paste0(y, "_est"), "N"] = formatC(
          nobs(est),
          format = "d",
          big.mark = ","
        )
        op_f = bd_fig$op_F[match(y, bd_fig$term)]
        result[paste0(y, "_est"), "opF"] = if (is.na(op_f)) {
          "."
        } else {
          sprintf("%.1f", op_f)
        }
      }
    }
    j = j + 1
  }
  rownames(result) = 1:nrow(result)
  colnames(result) = NULL

  print(format(
    result[, -c((ncol(result) - 4):(ncol(result) - 3))],
    justify = "left"
  ))
}

# Display the model comparison in the HTML.
print_se_result_table(main_cluster_scheme)
cat(
  "\nRead OP F against the momentfit Patnaik critical value based on the ",
  "sample-specific clustered K_eff, not a raw-instrument-count table.\n",
  sep = ""
)
```




-->

This chunk defines the shared scaffolding used by the assumption-grouped diagnostics below and by the PRODES section: the single-thread `fixest` guard, `robust_covs`, the label/format helpers, the `estimate_starlink()` 2SLS wrapper, and the `robust_full` full-sample baseline. (The coverage-tail trim is disabled — `if (FALSE)` — so this chunk produces no visible output.) -->

```{r RobustTrim, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F, fig.height=15, fig.width=8, results = "asis"}
# Diagnostic: single-thread fixest and reset its native estimation state to
# avoid Windows ACCESS_VIOLATION crashes (0xC0000005) seen partway through the
# sequential 2SLS sweep below.
fixest::setFixest_nthreads(1)
fixest::setFixest_estimation(reset = TRUE)

robust_outcomes = headline_outcomes

dta_robust = if (exists("dta_normal")) dta_normal else dta

missing_robust = setdiff(robust_outcomes, names(dta_robust))
if (length(missing_robust) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing robustness outcomes in dta_robust: ",
    paste(missing_robust, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

robust_covs = covlist[[covs_headline_idx]]
robust_label = function(x) {
  label = var_names$varname[match(x, var_names$var)]
  ifelse(is.na(label), x, label)
}
robust_plot_label = function(x) {
  label = robust_label(x) %>%
    str_replace(" \\(", "\n(")

  indent = str_extract(label, "^ +")
  indent[is.na(indent)] = ""
  indent_n = nchar(indent)

  paste0(
    vapply(indent_n, function(n) strrep("\u00A0", n), character(1)),
    str_sub(label, indent_n + 1)
  )
}

# Shared outcome set for the two manuscript influence checks: leave one state
# out and trim municipalities with the largest first-stage variance shares.
# The aggregate-UPF outcome replaces the narrower UPF-large-claim overlap in
# diagnostics while the tenure results table continues to report both measures.
# Ignitions use total municipal area because they can originate outside forest.
# Ignition spatial HHI and PM1 remain in their original municipality-level units.
appendix_stability_outcomes = c(
  "r_n_mun_deter_degr",
  "r_area_mun_deter_degr",

fmt_num = function(x, digits = 3) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
}
fmt_pct = function(x, digits = 1) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), 100 * x))
}

estimate_starlink = function(data, outcome, iv_rhs = "coverarea:year") {
  on.exit(gc(verbose = FALSE), add = TRUE)
  data_reg = dplyr::filter(igni_sample(data, outcome), reg_sample == 1)
  model = paste0(
    outcome,
    " ~ ",
    paste0(robust_covs, collapse = " + "),
    " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)",
    " | starlink ~ ",
    iv_rhs
  ) %>%
    as.formula()

  tryCatch(
    {
      est = fixest::feols(
        model,
        data = data_reg,
        cluster = main_cluster_form,
        notes = FALSE
      )

      tab95 = broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>%
        filter(term == "fit_starlink")
      tab90 = broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>%
        filter(term == "fit_starlink")

      tibble(
        outcome = outcome,
        estimate = tab95$estimate[1],
        std.error = tab95$std.error[1],
        statistic = tab95$statistic[1],
        p.value = tab95$p.value[1],
        conf.low95 = tab95$conf.low[1],
        conf.high95 = tab95$conf.high[1],
        conf.low90 = tab90$conf.low[1],
        conf.high90 = tab90$conf.high[1],
        N = stats::nobs(est),
        n_mun = n_distinct(data_reg$codmun),
        error = NA_character_
      )
    },
    error = function(e) {
      tibble(
        outcome = outcome,
        estimate = NA_real_,
        std.error = NA_real_,
        statistic = NA_real_,
        p.value = NA_real_,
        conf.low95 = NA_real_,
        conf.high95 = NA_real_,
        conf.low90 = NA_real_,
        conf.high90 = NA_real_,
        N = nrow(data_reg),
        n_mun = n_distinct(data_reg$codmun),
        error = conditionMessage(e)
      )
    }
  )
}

# Municipalities that actually enter an outcome's 2SLS estimation sample, taken
# from the fitted model's codmun fixed-effect levels (so it accounts for NA rows
# AND feols's singleton/collinear-FE removal — matching the "Municipalities"
# count in the first-stage-by-tenure table). Tenure-disaggregated outcomes
# (r_area_ti_*, r_area_uc_*, ...) are NA for municipalities lacking the tenure,
# so feols estimates them on a tenure-restricted subsample, not the full
# 772-municipality panel. This is the correct leave-one-out universe: dropping a
# municipality outside this set is a no-op (feols already excludes it), which
# would otherwise reproduce the full-sample estimate and inflate the LOO
# significant-share denominator. Falls back to complete cases if the fit fails.
estimation_municipalities = function(data, outcome, iv_rhs = "coverarea:year") {
  data_reg = dplyr::filter(igni_sample(data, outcome), reg_sample == 1)
  model = paste0(
    outcome,
    " ~ ",
    paste0(robust_covs, collapse = " + "),
    " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)",
    " | starlink ~ ", iv_rhs
  ) %>%
    as.formula()
  tryCatch(
    {
      est = fixest::feols(
        model,
        data = data_reg,
        cluster = main_cluster_form,
        notes = FALSE,
        nthreads = 1
      )
      # codmun fixed-effect levels retained by feols = exact estimation sample.
      mun = as.integer(names(fixest::fixef(est, notes = FALSE)$codmun))
      sort(mun[!is.na(mun)])
    },
    error = function(e) {
      model_vars = c(
        outcome,
        robust_covs,
        "starlink",
        "coverarea",
        "codmun",
        "uf",
        "year"
      )
      cc = stats::complete.cases(data_reg[, model_vars, drop = FALSE])
      sort(unique(as.integer(data_reg$codmun[cc])))
    }
  )
}

robust_full = map_dfr(robust_outcomes, ~ estimate_starlink(dta_robust, .x)) %>%
  mutate(sample = "Full")

# ---- Per-municipality first-stage variance share for an arbitrary panel -----
# Faithful copy of the RobustACRMass machinery: residualize starlink and each
# ca_<year> instrument on covariates + FE, form D-hat^Z = sum(coef * resid),
# then sum (D-hat^Z)^2 within municipality and normalize to a share.
muni_var_share = function(panel, covs) {
  req = c(
    "starlink",
    "codmun",
    "uf",
    "year",
    "coverarea",
    all.vars(stats::as.formula(paste0("~", paste(covs, collapse = "+"))))
  )
  d = panel %>%
    dplyr::filter(reg_sample == 1) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na(dplyr::any_of(req))

  # Active ca_YYYY instrument columns (the coverarea:year interaction terms).
  instr = grep("^ca_\\d+$", names(d), value = TRUE)
  instr = instr[vapply(
    instr,
    function(v) {
      !all(is.na(d[[v]])) && stats::sd(d[[v]], na.rm = TRUE) > 0
    },
    logical(1)
  )]
  d = d %>% tidyr::drop_na(dplyr::any_of(instr))

  fs = fixest::feols(
    stats::as.formula(paste0(
      "starlink ~ ",
      paste(c(instr, covs), collapse = " + "),
      " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)"
    )),
    data = d,
    cluster = main_cluster_form,
    notes = FALSE
  )
  b = stats::coef(fs)[instr]
  instr = instr[!is.na(b)] # fixest drops instruments collinear with FE
  b = b[!is.na(b)]

  res_fit = function(lhs) {
    fixest::feols(
      stats::as.formula(paste0(
        lhs,
        " ~ ",
        paste(covs, collapse = " + "),
        " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)"
      )),
      data = d,
      cluster = main_cluster_form,
      notes = FALSE
    )
  }
  dhatZ = rep(0, nrow(d))
  for (v in instr) {
    dhatZ = dhatZ + b[[v]] * stats::residuals(res_fit(v))
  }
  d$mass_iv = dhatZ^2 # (D-hat^Z)^2, per-observation variance mass

  d %>%
    dplyr::group_by(codmun) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(mass_iv = sum(mass_iv, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(share_var = mass_iv / sum(mass_iv))
}


# Coverage-tail trim test disabled for now (kept for easy re-enable: flip to
# `if (TRUE)`). The shared robustness infrastructure above this block stays live.
if (FALSE) {
  # Trimmed-share robustness ------------------------------------------------
  coverage_mun = dta_robust %>%
    filter(reg_sample == 1) %>%
    distinct(codmun, coverarea)

  trim_defs = tibble(
    sample = c("Full", "1%", "2.5%", "5%"),
    tail = c(0, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05)
  )

  make_trim_data = function(tail) {
    if (tail == 0) {
      return(dta_robust)
    }

    cuts = quantile(
      coverage_mun$coverarea,
      probs = c(tail, 1 - tail),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
    keep_mun = coverage_mun %>%
      filter(coverarea >= cuts[[1]], coverarea <= cuts[[2]]) %>%
      pull(codmun)

    dta_robust %>% filter(codmun %in% keep_mun)
  }

  trim_est = map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(trim_defs)), function(i) {
    data_i = make_trim_data(trim_defs$tail[i])
    map_dfr(robust_outcomes, ~ estimate_starlink(data_i, .x)) %>%
      mutate(sample = trim_defs$sample[i], tail = trim_defs$tail[i])
  }) %>%

      sample = factor(sample, levels = trim_defs$sample),
      outcome_id = factor(outcome, levels = robust_outcomes),
      outcome_label = robust_plot_label(outcome)

      N = formatC(N, format = "d", big.mark = ",")

      Outcome = outcome_label,

    )

  # cat(knitr::kable(as.data.frame(trim_table),
  #                  align = "l", format = "html",

  # cat("\n\n")

  fig_trim_robust = ggplot(

      alpha = 0.45

    geom_segment(
      aes(x = conf.low90, xend = conf.high90, yend = sample),
```
