```{r RobustTrim, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F, fig.height=15, fig.width=8, results = "asis"}
      alpha = 0.45
    ) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(
      ~outcome_id,
      scales = "free_x",
      ncol = 1,
      strip.position = "left",
      labeller = as_labeller(robust_outcome_labs)
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        "Full" = "red",
        "1%" = "grey20",
        "2.5%" = "grey45",
        "5%" = "grey65"
      )
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Estimate",
      y = NULL,
      color = "Two-sided trim",
      caption = "Bars: 95% CI (light); 90% CI (darker)."
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.placement = "outside",
      strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      text = element_text(size = 14)
    )

  print(fig_trim_robust)
} # end if (FALSE) — coverage-tail trim test
```


```{r WeakIVSetup, message=F, warning=F, echo=F}
# Shared cluster spec + OP effective F helpers for ALL weak-IV diagnostics
# below (RobustFirstStageTenure, WeakIVDiagnostics, NEW_WeakIV_AR_OlaePflueger).
# The weak-IV diagnostics inherit the document-wide microregion clustering scheme
# set once in the `ClusterSchemeSwitch` chunk (main_cluster_form = ~microreg).
# Single source of truth -- there is NO separate cluster spec here.
weakiv_cluster_form = main_cluster_form
weakiv_cluster_chars = main_cluster_chars
weakiv_cluster_label = main_cluster_label

# Helper: split a controls vector into bare column names vs formula-syntax
# interaction terms (anything containing `:`, e.g. "year:lat"). Still needed
# by ivDiag::AR_test(), which does `data[, controls]` and rejects formula syntax.
split_controls_for_ivdiag = function(controls, data) {
  is_bare = controls %in% names(data)
  list(formula = controls[!is_bare], bare = controls[is_bare])
}

# Olea-Pflueger effective F under MULTI-WAY-cluster SE via fixest.
# ivDiag::eff_F() only supports single-cluster (cl is a scalar column name), so
# for two-way clustering on {codmun + microreg:year} we extract the first-stage
# Z-coefficient VCV from a fixest fit with cluster = cluster_form. fixest
# applies Cameron-Gelbach-Miller (2011) add-and-subtract internally and its own
# G/(G-1), (N-1)/(N-K) small-sample corrections (consistent with the lfe path
# to within ~5%). Algebra: V(pi_hat) = (Z'Z)^{-1} S (Z'Z)^{-1} from the
# doubly-partialled (controls + FE) Z design, so tr(Sigma %*% Q_zz) =
# tr((Z'Z)^{-1} S) is the OP F denominator.
op_F_twoway = function(
  data,
  controls,
  fe_str,
  iv,
  cluster_form,
  endog = "starlink",
  nthreads = 1
) {
  controls_rhs = if (length(controls) > 0) {
    paste(controls, collapse = " + ")
  } else {
    "1"
  }
  fs_form = stats::as.formula(paste0(
    endog,
    " ~ ",
    paste(iv, collapse = " + "),
    " + ",
    controls_rhs,
    " | ",
    fe_str
  ))
  fs = tryCatch(
    fixest::feols(
      fs_form,
      data = data,
      cluster = cluster_form,
      notes = FALSE,
      nthreads = nthreads
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(fs)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  iv_pos = match(iv, names(stats::coef(fs)))
  if (any(is.na(iv_pos))) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  Sigma = stats::vcov(fs)[iv_pos, iv_pos, drop = FALSE]
  pi_hat = matrix(stats::coef(fs)[iv_pos], ncol = 1)
  # Q_zz on the doubly-partialled (controls + FE) Z design.
  partial = function(yvar) {
    f_p = stats::as.formula(paste0(
      yvar,
      " ~ ",
      controls_rhs,
      " | ",
      fe_str
    ))
    as.numeric(stats::residuals(
      fixest::feols(f_p, data = data, notes = FALSE, nthreads = nthreads)
    ))
  }
  rZ = vapply(iv, partial, numeric(nrow(data)))
  if (is.null(dim(rZ))) {
    rZ = matrix(rZ, ncol = length(iv))
  }
  Q_zz = crossprod(rZ)
  drop(
    crossprod(pi_hat, Q_zz %*% pi_hat) / sum(diag(Sigma %*% Q_zz))
  )
}

# Dispatch wrapper: the one-way path uses momentfit's complete MOP
# implementation. The legacy multi-way path retains the fixest calculation
# because the paper's specification clusters by microregion only.
op_F_clustered = function(
  data,
  yvar,
  formula_controls,
  bare_controls,
  iv,
  cluster_chars = weakiv_cluster_chars,
  cluster_form = weakiv_cluster_form,
  fe_cols = c("codmun", "uf_year"),
  fe_str = "codmun + interaction(uf, year)",
  endog = "starlink"
) {
  if (length(cluster_chars) == 1L) {
    mop = op_mop_momentfit(
      data = data,
      yvar = yvar,
      controls = c(formula_controls, bare_controls),
      iv = iv,
      fe_str = fe_str,
      cluster_col = cluster_chars,
      endog = endog
    )
    mop$Feff[1]
  } else {
    op_F_twoway(
      data = data,
      controls = c(formula_controls, bare_controls),
      fe_str = fe_str,
      iv = iv,
      cluster_form = cluster_form,
      endog = endog
    )
  }
}
```

```{r RobustFirstStageTenure, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F, include=FALSE}
# First stage by land tenure ----------------------------------------------
# Tenure-specific degradation outcomes are NA for municipalities lacking that
# tenure type, so feols estimates each tenure 2SLS — and therefore its first
# stage — on a tenure-restricted subsample. This table re-runs the headline
# 2SLS per tenure outcome and reports first-stage strength (Cragg-Donald F,
# Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F, and Olea-Pflueger effective F) and fit on that
# subsample; r_area_mun_deter_degr is the full-panel benchmark. Reuses
# dta_robust, robust_covs, robust_plot_label, robust_outcomes, fmt_num defined
# in the RobustTrim chunk above. Cluster scheme is controlled by the
# weakiv_cluster_* config in the WeakIVSetup chunk above.

first_stage_tenure = function(data, outcome, iv_rhs = "coverarea:year") {
  data_reg = dplyr::filter(data, reg_sample == 1)
  model = paste0(
    outcome,
    " ~ ",
    paste0(robust_covs, collapse = " + "),
    " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)",
    " | starlink ~ ",
    iv_rhs
  ) %>%
    as.formula()

  tryCatch(
    {
      # Single-thread fixest (same Windows ACCESS_VIOLATION guard as RobustTrim).
      # Cluster scheme from WeakIVSetup (the paper default is microregion).
      est = fixest::feols(
        model,
        data = data_reg,
        cluster = weakiv_cluster_form,
        notes = FALSE,
        nthreads = 1
      )
      fs = summary(est, stage = 1) # stage-1 (first-stage) fit
      fe = est$fixef_sizes
      # First-stage strength: Cragg-Donald F (homoskedastic), Kleibergen-Paap
      # rk Wald F (cluster-robust analog of CD under the configured scheme),
      # and Olea-Pflueger effective F (principled weak-IV statistic under
      # non-iid errors with k > 1 instruments; Montiel Olea & Pflueger 2013,
      # JBES 31(3), 358-369). Its clustered K_eff and Patnaik critical values
      # are sample-specific, so do not substitute the raw instrument count.
      sf = tryCatch(
        fixest::fitstat(est, ~ cd + ivwald, simplify = FALSE),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      cd_stat = tryCatch(
        {
          v = sf$cd
          if (is.list(v)) v$stat else as.numeric(v)
        },
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      wald = if (!is.null(sf)) sf$ivwald1 else NULL
      # momentfit diagnostics on the paper's microregion-clustered
      # specification. NA-outcome rows are dropped first to match the 2SLS
      # estimation sample.
      d_op = dplyr::filter(data_reg, !is.na(.data[[outcome]]))
      op_mop = op_mop_momentfit(
        data = d_op,
        yvar = outcome,
        controls = robust_covs,
        iv = calendar_iv_names
      )
      op_row_10 = op_mop[match(0.10, op_mop$tau), ]
      tibble(
        outcome = outcome,
        n_mun = unname(fe[if ("codmun" %in% names(fe)) "codmun" else 1L]),
        N = stats::nobs(est),
        cd_F = cd_stat,
        wald_F = if (!is.null(wald)) wald$stat else NA_real_,
        wald_p = if (!is.null(wald)) wald$p else NA_real_,
        op_F = op_mop$Feff[1],
        op_Keff_10 = op_row_10$Keff,
        op_cv_10 = op_row_10$critValue,
        fs_r2 = unname(fixest::r2(fs)["r2"]),
        error = NA_character_
      )
    },
    error = function(e) {
      tibble(
        outcome = outcome,
        n_mun = NA_integer_,
        N = NA_integer_,
        cd_F = NA_real_,
        wald_F = NA_real_,
        wald_p = NA_real_,
        op_F = NA_real_,
        op_Keff_10 = NA_real_,
        op_cv_10 = NA_real_,
        fs_r2 = NA_real_,
        error = conditionMessage(e)
      )
    }
  )
}

# Full sample (municipal aggregate) + 7 tenure-restricted subsamples — the
# first 8 entries of headline_outcomes. Other headline outcomes (forest-cover
# transitions, fines, PM2.5) are reported in the WeakIVDiagnostics chunk
# below, not here.
tenure_fs_outcomes = intersect(
  unique(
    # 1:9, not 1:8 -- the tenure block gained a row when the single pooled
    # claims-over-public-land outcome was replaced by its two size components
    # (large / small, each nested under its property class). The pooled TI, UC
    # and settlement overlaps and the cancelled-claims row used to be appended
    # here; all four were dropped as null rows, TI on 624 observations with an SE
    # four times its estimate.
    headline_outcomes[1:9]
  ),
  names(dta_robust)
)

# Row labels for the first-stage tables (Fabio, 2026-08-12). These rows do not
# vary by OUTCOME, they vary by SAMPLE: every one of them is the same 2SLS, run
# on the municipalities that have the tenure in question. Labelling them with the
# outcome name ("in indigenous lands (% forest area)") repeated a unit that is
# identical down the column and buried the thing that actually differs. So the
# column carries the tenure name alone, and the full-panel row reads "Full".
#
# Keyed on the tenure token in the variable name, so it works for the degradation
# outcomes here and the PRODES deforestation outcomes in the PRODES Relevance
# section (r_area_<tenure>_deter_degr / r_area_<tenure>_prodes_defo). Anything
# that is not a municipal-total or tenure outcome -- PM1, fines -- falls through
# to its ordinary label rather than being forced into a tenure name it does not
# have.
fs_tenure_names = c(
  ti = "Indigenous lands",
  uc = "Conservation units",
  sett = "Settlements",
  ndpf = "Undesignated forests",
  sicar21_large = "Large properties",
  sicar21_small = "Small properties",
  sicar21_ca = "Cancelled claims",
  over_ndpf = "Claims over undesignated forest",
  over_ti = "Claims over indigenous lands",
  over_uc = "Claims over conservation units",
  over_sett = "Claims over settlements",
  over_ndpf_large = "Large ∩ undesignated forest",
  over_ndpf_small = "Small ∩ undesignated forest",
  over_ti_large = "Large ∩ indigenous lands",
  over_ti_small = "Small ∩ indigenous lands",
  over_uc_large = "Large ∩ conservation units",
  over_uc_small = "Small ∩ conservation units",
  over_sett_large = "Large ∩ settlements",
  over_sett_small = "Small ∩ settlements"
)
# `full_var` names the municipal-total outcome the tenure rows partition, and it
# is a REQUIRED argument rather than a "mun" pattern match. Matching on the token
# alone labelled every municipal total "Full", which on the PRODES table -- where
# the tenure rows split PRODES deforestation but degradation, PM1 and fines are
# also reported -- produced the row "Full" twice, for two different outcomes.
# Only the total the tenure rows actually decompose gets that label; every other
# outcome keeps its ordinary name.
fs_tenure_label = function(v, full_var) {
  # Matches the area and the flags spelling of each tenure outcome, so the row
  # shows "Indigenous lands" rather than falling through to the full label with
  # its unit suffix in parentheses.
  # [A-Za-z0-9_]+, not [A-Za-z]+. The original class matched no digit and no
  # underscore, so it only ever resolved the four single-word tenures
  # (ti/uc/sett/ndpf): every multi-token name -- sicar21_large, over_ndpf, and now
  # the by-size overlaps -- failed to match and fell through to the verbose
  # outcome label, silently making those fs_tenure_names entries dead. The class
  # is greedy and the suffix is anchored, so "over_ndpf_large_deter_degr" yields
  # "over_ndpf_large" rather than a shorter prefix.
  tok = sub(
    "^r_(?:area|n)_([A-Za-z0-9_]+)_(deter_degr|prodes_defo)$",
    "\\1",
    v,
    perl = TRUE
  )
  out = unname(fs_tenure_names[tok])
  # Fall back to the ordinary label wherever the pattern does not match or the
  # token is unknown, so a new outcome shows a real name instead of NA.
  fallback = trimws(robust_plot_label(v))
  ifelse(v == full_var, "Full", ifelse(is.na(out), fallback, out))
}

fs_tenure = map_dfr(
  tenure_fs_outcomes,
  ~ first_stage_tenure(dta_robust, .x)
) %>%
  arrange(match(outcome, robust_outcomes)) %>%
  # headline_outcomes[1] is the municipal aggregate (flags in v3), so the "Full"
  # row keeps its label whichever outcome family the headline uses.
  mutate(outcome_label = fs_tenure_label(outcome, headline_outcomes[1]))

fs_tenure_table = fs_tenure %>%
  mutate(
    cd_cell = fmt_num(cd_F, 1),
    wald_cell = fmt_num(wald_F, 1),
    op_cell = fmt_num(op_F, 1),
    r2_cell = fmt_num(fs_r2, 3),
    N_cell = ifelse(is.na(N), "", formatC(N, format = "d", big.mark = ",")),
    mun_cell = ifelse(
      is.na(n_mun),
      "",
      formatC(n_mun, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    `Land tenure` = outcome_label,
    Municipalities = mun_cell,
    N = N_cell,
    `Cragg-Donald F` = cd_cell,
    `Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F` = wald_cell,
    `Olea-Pflueger effective F` = op_cell,
    `First-stage R²` = r2_cell
  )

cat(
  knitr::kable(
    as.data.frame(fs_tenure_table),
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    format = "html",
    caption = "First stage by land tenure"
  ) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "bordered", "hover", "condensed"),
      full_width = FALSE,
      position = "left"
    ) #%>%
    # kableExtra::footnote(
    #   general_title = "Notes:",
    #   general = paste0(
    #     "Each row re-estimates the headline 2SLS for one degradation ",
    #     "outcome (endogenous variable: Starlink; instruments: the ",
    #     "coverarea:year interactions). Tenure-specific outcomes are missing ",
    #     "for municipalities without that tenure type, so each first stage ",
    #     "is estimated on a tenure-restricted subsample; Municipalities and ",
    #     "N report that subsample. r_area_mun_deter_degr (degradation, % ",
    #     "munic. area) is the full-panel benchmark. Cragg-Donald F is the ",
    #     "homoskedastic first-stage statistic; the Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald ",
    #     "F and Olea-Pflueger effective F are computed under ",
    #     weakiv_cluster_label,
    #     " clustering (configured in the WeakIVSetup chunk; revert to ",
    #     "microregion-only via the three weakiv_cluster_* lines there). ",
    #     "The Olea-Pflueger effective F (Montiel Olea & Pflueger 2013, ",
    #     "JBES 31(3), 358-369) is the principled weak-IV statistic under ",
    #     "non-iid errors with k > 1 instruments — read it against the ",
    #     "MOP21 critical values (~19-20 for 10% worst-case bias, ~13 for ",
    #     "20%, ~10 for 30% with 2 instruments), not the homoskedastic ",
    #     "Stock-Yogo F > 10 rule of thumb. For single-cluster runs the OP ",
    #     "F, K_eff, and Patnaik critical values are from momentfit::MOPtest() ",
    #     "with its default clustered HC0 covariance and cluster adjustment. ",
    #     "First-stage R² ",
    #     "is from the stage-1 regression."
    #   ),
    #   footnote_as_chunk = TRUE,
    #   escape = FALSE,
    #   threeparttable = TRUE
    # )
    ,
  sep = "\n"
)
cat("\n\n")

# Knit-time one-line summary: weakest tenure subsample (excludes the benchmark).
# Rank by Olea-Pflueger effective F when available (the principled weak-IV
# statistic under cluster-robust SE); fall back to KP rk Wald F if OP is NA
# for all rows (e.g., the MOP calculation failed on every subsample).
weakest_rank_col = if (any(!is.na(fs_tenure$op_F))) "op_F" else "wald_F"
weakest = fs_tenure %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    outcome != headline_outcomes[1],
    !is.na(.data[[weakest_rank_col]])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::slice_min(.data[[weakest_rank_col]], n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
if (nrow(weakest) == 1) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "*Weakest tenure first stage: %s — Olea-Pflueger effective F = %s, K_eff = %s, and the 10%% maximal-bias critical value = %s; Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F = %s. The conventional Stock-Yogo F > 10 rule is derived for the homoskedastic case only.*\n\n",
    trimws(weakest$outcome_label),
    fmt_num(weakest$op_F, 1),
    fmt_num(weakest$op_Keff_10, 2),
    fmt_num(weakest$op_cv_10, 1),
    fmt_num(weakest$wald_F, 1)
  ))
}
```


<!-- **Reading the result.** Read the `Olea-Pflueger effective F` as primary and `Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F` as a cluster-robust cross-check, each against its critical value (MOP21 ~16–20 for OP at 10% bias) and the full-panel municipal-aggregate row. Subsamples with OP F comfortably above the MOP21 threshold carry essentially the headline first-stage strength, so their degradation estimates are not weak-instrument artifacts. Watch the smallest subsamples — indigenous territories (≈287 municipalities) and conservation units (≈371) — where N and first-stage strength shrink; the indigenous-territory estimate is already flagged weak-IV. Any tenure OP F near/below the critical value should be read as weak-IV-fragile, caveated, and complemented with the Anderson–Rubin CI (Inference). Source for the appendix first-stage-by-tenure table. -->


### Exogeneity


#### Event-study placebo

The event studies use 2022 as the omitted year. The table reports joint Wald
p-values for all pre-2022 coefficients: 2017--2021 for most outcomes and
2019--2021 for ignitions and ignition spatial HHI, whose consistent series begin in 2019.

<!-- > Calendar-year event-study placebo (2022 base) for the four headline outcomes, with **`r main_cluster_label`** clustered SEs — the main-specification inference (`r main_cluster_note`). -->

```{r PlaceboTestMicroreg, message=F, warning=F, fig.height=8, fig.width=10, echo=F}
# Main-specification calendar-year event-study placebo with microregion-clustered
# SEs (cluster = main_cluster_form = ~microreg) -- the headline inference for the
# placebo. No coordinate swap is needed: clustering never changes the point
# estimate, and the covariates keep the original lat/lon.

# Single-thread fixest + reset native state (Windows ACCESS_VIOLATION guard).
fixest::setFixest_nthreads(1)
fixest::setFixest_estimation(reset = TRUE)

# Estimate the same eight main-form outcomes used in the influence checks plus
# the requested IHS transformation of ignition counts. IHS is plotted separately
# below and does not alter the established eight-panel figure.
placebo_outcomes_requested = c(appendix_stability_outcomes, "ihs_n_igni")
placebo_outcomes = intersect(placebo_outcomes_requested, names(dta))
stopifnot(identical(placebo_outcomes, placebo_outcomes_requested))

placebo_pretrend_test = function(model, years = 2017:2021) {
  keep_regex = paste0("^ca_(", paste(years, collapse = "|"), ")$")
  test = tryCatch(
    fixest::wald(model, keep = keep_regex, print = FALSE),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(test)) {
    return(tibble(pretrend_F = NA_real_, pretrend_p = NA_real_))
  }
  tibble(
    pretrend_F = as.numeric(test$stat),
    pretrend_p = as.numeric(test$p)
  )
}

pick_best_pretrend = function(options, tests) {
  ranked = tests %>%
    filter(outcome %in% options) %>%
    mutate(option_order = match(outcome, options)) %>%
    arrange(desc(pretrend_p), option_order)
  if (!nrow(ranked) || all(is.na(ranked$pretrend_p))) return(options[1])
  ranked$outcome[which.max(replace(ranked$pretrend_p, is.na(ranked$pretrend_p), -Inf))]
}

placebo_pretrend_calendar = tibble()

# Headline controls interacted with EVERY non-base year (covs_placebo), not the
# 2SLS set: on the full panel the 2SLS interactions are identically zero across
# the whole pre-period, which would leave these leads unconditioned. See the
# covs_placebo note in the covlist chunk.
covs_plm = covs_placebo
ca_terms = paste(paste0("ca_", setdiff(2017:CAL_END_YEAR, ctrl_base_year)), collapse = " + ")

# Placebo panel: full dta (needs pre-period leads). microreg / microreg_year
# (IBGE 2017 RGI and its year interaction) ship on dta from work_dataframe.Rmd
# section 1, feeding the main-specification cluster (see ClusterSchemeSwitch).
d_plm = dta %>% mutate(codmun = as.numeric(codmun))

for (var in placebo_outcomes) {
  # Both ignition quantity and ignition spatial HHI come from the current clustered-VIIRS
  # series, which begins in 2019. The balanced ignition-count panel contains
  # constructed zeros in 2017--2018, not observed zeros, so exclude those years
  # from both the plot and the joint pretrend test.
  placebo_start_year = if (
    var %in% c('rm_n_igni', 'ihs_n_igni', 'disp_shhiunb')
  ) 2019L else 2017L
  placebo_years = placebo_start_year:CAL_END_YEAR
  ca_terms_var = paste(
    paste0('ca_', setdiff(placebo_years, ctrl_base_year)),
    collapse = ' + '
  )
  est_data = d_plm %>% filter(year %in% placebo_years)

  model = paste0(
    var,
    " ~ ",
    ca_terms_var,
    " + ",
    paste(covs_plm, collapse = " + "),
    " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)"
  ) %>%
    as.formula()

  # Main-specification cluster scheme (see ClusterSchemeSwitch). The point
  # estimate is unchanged from the figures above, only the vcov (hence the CI
  # width) differs.
  est = feols(model, data = est_data, cluster = main_cluster_form, notes = FALSE)

  placebo_pretrend_calendar = bind_rows(
    placebo_pretrend_calendar,
    bind_cols(
      tibble(outcome = var),
      placebo_pretrend_test(est, years = placebo_start_year:2021)
    )
  )

  ct = est$coeftable
  trm = rownames(ct)
  ci95 = confint(est, level = 0.95)
  ci90 = confint(est, level = 0.90)

  tab = tibble(
    term = trm,
    estimate = ct[, 1],
    conf.low95 = ci95[trm, 1],
    conf.high95 = ci95[trm, 2],
    conf.low90 = ci90[trm, 1],
    conf.high90 = ci90[trm, 2]
  ) %>%
    filter(grepl("^ca_", term)) %>%
    mutate(year = as.numeric(gsub("ca_", "", term))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(year)) %>%
    select(-term) %>%
    bind_rows(tibble(
      year = 2022,
      estimate = 0,
      conf.low95 = 0,
      conf.high95 = 0,
      conf.low90 = 0,
      conf.high90 = 0
    )) %>%
    arrange(year)

  var_name = trimws(var_names$varname[which(var == var_names$var)])

  assign(
    paste0("es_", var, "_mun_microreg"),
    ggplot(tab, aes(x = year, y = estimate)) +
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = 0,
        color = "black",
        size = 0.5,
        linetype = "dashed"
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = 2022,
        color = "black",
        size = 0.5,
        linetype = "dashed"
      ) +
      geom_linerange(
        aes(ymin = conf.low95, ymax = conf.high95, colour = "95% CI"),
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
        size = 2,
        show.legend = TRUE,
        key_glyph = "vline"
      ) +
      scale_colour_manual(
        name = NULL,
        breaks = "95% CI",
        values = c("95% CI" = "grey80"),
        guide = guide_legend(
          order = 2,
          keyheight = grid::unit(0.9, "cm"),
          override.aes = list(shape = NA, linetype = 1, linewidth = 3)
        )
      ) +
      ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +
      geom_point(
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
        size = 1.5,
        color = "red"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = var_name,
        x = "Year",
        y = "Estimate",
        color = "Group"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        text = element_text(size = 10),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11.25),
        panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
        legend.key.height = grid::unit(0.5, "cm"),
        legend.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.1, "cm")
      )
  )

}
```

<!-- **Reading the result.** Under two-way {codmun + microreg:year} clustering, OP effective F ≈ **11.5** and KP rk F ≈ **8.9** (shared across outcomes — first-stage only). Against the MOP13 k = 2 critical values (19.29 / 12.17 / 9.57 for 10/20/30% bias, in the verdict table above), F = 11.5 **clears the 30% but not the 20% band**: moderate-to-weak, not "strong." So we don't lean on an "F > 10" claim and lead with the weak-IV-robust Anderson-Rubin test, valid regardless of first-stage strength.

For the two headline positive outcomes — DETER degradation (% municipal area) and PM2.5 — the AR 95% CIs exclude zero ([0.040, 0.367] and [0.062, 1.017]), rejecting the no-effect null at 5% under identification-robust inference, and the rejection survives the cluster-scheme change — so the headline is not a weak-instrument artifact. Enforcement fines is the informative non-rejection: AR CI bounded but wide (upper ≈ 2.4× the mean fine rate), i.e. "no *detectable* enforcement response, imprecisely estimated" (reference note [weak_iv_tests.md](../notes/weak_iv_tests.md) §10). Aggregate forest-replaced has an unbounded AR CI — β not bounded for that outcome; its 2SLS point estimate is not headlined.

*(Numbers reflect the two-way-clustered default recorded in the reference note §9; re-knit and confirm against the printed `ar_results` and effective-F tables above.)*


**Standard-error structure.** Identification runs through the *share-exogeneity* route, under which conventional cluster-robust SEs are appropriate (Borusyak, Hull & Jaravel 2025); exposure-robust (Adão–Kolesár–Morales) SEs address the *shock* route, not this design. The live SE concern is **spatial dependence** (identification is a contiguous frontier block), addressed here by clustering on microregion (IBGE 2017 RGI), within which municipalities nest. -->

## Robustness

### Inference

<!-- **What this reports.** The headline 2SLS estimate, its `r main_cluster_label`-clustered standard error and p-value, next to identification-robust Anderson-Rubin inference for the same specification: the AR p-value at $H_0:\beta = 0$ and the AR 95% confidence set obtained by test inversion. AR is valid whatever the strength of the first stage, so it is the honest check on the conventional Wald inference when the Olea-Pflueger effective F sits in the moderate range. An **unbounded** AR set is not a failure of the code: under weak identification any valid confidence set must be unbounded with positive probability (Dufour 1997), and the `bounded` column flags it. Computed with `ivDiag::AR_test()` (Lal, Lockwood, Xu & Shen), which takes the fixed effects and the cluster directly. -->

```{r InferenceAR, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F}
# Anderson-Rubin test + inverted 95% confidence set via ivDiag::AR_test().
# ivDiag indexes controls with data[, controls], so year:X interaction terms must
# be materialized as bare columns and the state-by-year FE must exist as a single
# factor column.
ar_ci_ivdiag = function(
  data,
  yvar,
  formula_controls,
  bare_controls,
  iv,
  fe_cols = c("codmun", "uf_year"),
  cluster_col = "microreg",
  endog = "starlink",
  alpha = 0.05
) {
  if (!requireNamespace("ivDiag", quietly = TRUE)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  data_aug = as.data.frame(data)
  if ("uf_year" %in% fe_cols && !"uf_year" %in% names(data_aug)) {
    data_aug$uf_year = interaction(data_aug$uf, data_aug$year, drop = TRUE)
  }
  mm_cols = character(0)
  if (length(formula_controls) > 0) {
    mm_form = stats::as.formula(paste(
      "~ -1 +",
      paste(formula_controls, collapse = " + ")
    ))
    mm = stats::model.matrix(
      mm_form,
      data = data_aug,
      na.action = stats::na.pass
    )
    colnames(mm) = make.names(colnames(mm), unique = TRUE)
    mm_cols = colnames(mm)
    data_aug = cbind(data_aug, as.data.frame(mm))
  }
  suppressWarnings(tryCatch(
    ivDiag::AR_test(
      data = data_aug,
      Y = yvar,
      D = endog,
      Z = iv,
      controls = c(bare_controls, mm_cols),
      FE = fe_cols,
      cl = cluster_col,
      CI = TRUE,
      alpha = alpha,
      prec = 6
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  ))
}

# One row per outcome: 2SLS estimate / SE / p (estimate_starlink, the same
# wrapper the other robustness checks use) alongside AR p and the AR 95% set.
inference_table = function(
  data,
  outcomes,
  iv = calendar_iv_names,
  iv_rhs = paste(iv, collapse = " + ")
) {
  purrr::map_dfr(outcomes, function(y) {
    # Match estimate_starlink() exactly, including the reduced ignition window.
    # Instruments with no within-sample variation are removed outcome by outcome;
    # this matters in the 2025 PRODES-year panel because PM and ignition outcomes
    # can end before 2025 even while the panel-wide IV basis includes caP_2025.
    d_y = igni_sample(data, y) %>%
      dplyr::filter(reg_sample == 1, !is.na(.data[[y]]))
    iv_y = intersect(iv, names(d_y))
    iv_y = iv_y[vapply(iv_y, function(z) {
      vz = d_y[[z]]
      any(is.finite(vz)) && stats::sd(vz, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
    }, logical(1))]
    if (!length(iv_y)) {
      return(tibble::tibble(
        Outcome = robust_label(y), Estimate = NA_real_, SE = NA_real_,
        p = NA_real_, `AR F` = NA_real_, `AR p` = NA_real_,
        `OP F` = NA_real_, `AR 95% CI` = NA_character_, Bounded = NA,
        N = nrow(d_y)
      ))
    }
    iv_rhs_y = paste(iv_y, collapse = " + ")
    est = estimate_starlink(data, y, iv_rhs = iv_rhs_y)
    ivd_split = split_controls_for_ivdiag(robust_covs, d_y)
    op_F = tryCatch(
      op_F_clustered(
        data = d_y,
        yvar = y,
        formula_controls = ivd_split$formula,
        bare_controls = ivd_split$bare,
        iv = iv_y
      ),
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    )
    ar = ar_ci_ivdiag(
      data = d_y,
      yvar = y,
      formula_controls = ivd_split$formula,
      bare_controls = ivd_split$bare,
      iv = iv_y
    )
    # AR_test returns Fstat = c(F, df1, df2, p) and ci.print as ONE formatted
    # string, which already carries the union / infinite-bound cases.
    ar_p = if (!is.null(ar)) unname(ar$Fstat["p"]) else NA_real_
    ar_F = if (!is.null(ar)) unname(ar$Fstat["F"]) else NA_real_
    tibble::tibble(
      Outcome = robust_label(y),
      Estimate = est$estimate,
      SE = est$std.error,
      p = est$p.value,
      `AR F` = ar_F,
      `AR p` = ar_p,
      `OP F` = op_F,
      `AR 95% CI` = if (is.null(ar)) NA_character_ else ar$ci.print,
      Bounded = if (is.null(ar)) NA else isTRUE(ar$bounded),
      N = est$N
    )
  })
}
# The same nine outcomes are used in the AR and outcome-normalization checks.
inference_specs = tibble::tribble(
  ~outcome,                                  ~label,
  "r_n_mun_deter_degr",                     "Degradation (flags per 100 km2)",
  "r_area_mun_deter_degr",                  "Degradation area",
  "r_area_ndpf_deter_degr",                 "  UPF",
  "r_area_over_ndpf_large_deter_degr",      "    with large-property claims",
  "rm_n_igni",                               "Ignitions (per 100 km2 munic. area)",
  "disp_shhiunb",                            "Ignition spatial HHI",
  "sh21_agr_pec",                            "Forest transition to pasture",
  "pm1mun",                                  "PM1",
  "r_n_mun_police",                         "Enforcement fines (per 100 km2)"
)
inference_outcomes = inference_specs$outcome
missing_inference = setdiff(inference_outcomes, names(dta_robust))
if (length(missing_inference)) {
  stop("Missing requested AR outcomes: ", paste(missing_inference, collapse = ", "))
}

inference_normal = inference_table(dta_robust, inference_outcomes)

cat(sprintf(
  "Inference: 2SLS vs Anderson-Rubin, calendar year (%s cluster)\n\n",
  main_cluster_label
))
inference_normal = inference_normal %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Outcome = inference_specs$label[match(Outcome, robust_label(inference_specs$outcome))]
  )
print(
  as.data.frame(
    dplyr::select(
      inference_normal,
      Outcome, Estimate, SE, p, "AR p", "AR 95% CI", "OP F", N
    )
  ),
  row.names = FALSE,
  digits = 4
)
```

### Outcome normalization

<!-- **What this tests.** v3 reports degradation, enforcement and the other area/count outcomes normalized by municipal **forest** area. That denominator is a choice, and the whole point of choosing it is that it changes results — so it has to be shown against the alternatives rather than asserted. Each form below is estimated with the headline covariates, fixed effects, instrument and `r main_cluster_label` cluster, and each gets **its own event-study placebo**: -->

<!-- | Form | Definition | What it assumes |
|---|---|---|
| forest area, fixed 2021 | $y / \text{forest km}^2_{2021}$ | the exposed area is the 2021 forest stock (v3 headline) |
| forest area, prior year | $y / \text{forest km}^2_{t-1}$ | the exposed area is last year's remaining forest |
| municipal area | $y / \text{municipal km}^2$ | the exposed area is the whole municipality (v2 headline) |
| raw level | $y$ | no exposure adjustment; large municipalities dominate |
| $\log(y + c)$ | $\log(y + c)$ on the raw level | proportional effects, at a chosen $c$ |
| IHS | $\operatorname{asinh}(y)$ on the raw level | proportional effects without a chosen constant | -->

<!-- **On the prior-year denominator.** The headline `area_forest` is **frozen at 2021** — zero municipalities show any within-municipality variation in it — so the headline treats the area at risk as constant while the MapBiomas stock actually falls about 0.7% a year. The prior-year form divides by each municipality's forest stock in $t-1$, taken from `data/processed/mb_forest.RDS`, which covers 2016–2024 and reproduces both `shm_flo` and `area_forest` at $r = 0.9999$ — the same forest definition, not a different class grouping. Because 2016 is available, the lag is complete and **no pre-period lead is lost**: an earlier attempt that lagged after joining dropped 2017 and pushed the joint pre-trend from 0.076 to 0.046, and that loss was the missing lead rather than the denominator.

The trade-off is worth stating rather than burying. Prior-year is *predetermined with respect to the same year's outcome* but not with respect to treatment: in 2023 and 2024 the lagged stock already embodies Starlink's earlier effect, so part of the response sits in the denominator. That contamination is small — the stock moves 0.7% a year and the treatment-induced share of that is a fraction again — but it is the reason the fixed 2021 stock remains the headline. On the measured side, prior-year improves the negative-lead ratio from 0.928 to 0.855 and costs UPF degradation its 5% significance (0.0473\*\* → 0.0475\*, essentially the same coefficient with a slightly wider standard error).

**Removed: deviations from the historical mean.** $y_{it} - \bar y_i$ is an algebraic **no-op** — $\bar y_i$ is time-invariant, so the municipality fixed effect absorbs it exactly and the coefficient reproduced the raw-level one to every digit. It was kept for a while as a panel check; it never was a separate specification, and the prior-year denominator now occupies that column with something that genuinely differs. The ratio version $y_{it} / \bar y_i$ was dropped earlier for a substantive reason: it requires a strictly positive pre-period mean, so it silently ran on about 60% of the panel, and a coefficient estimated on a sample selected by pre-period activity is not comparable with the rows around it.

**On the log constant.** Because $\log(y+c)$ is scale-dependent when outcomes contain zeros, the constants follow fixed unit-based rules rather than sample minima. Raw integer counts use $c=1$, their smallest positive increment. Zero-inclusive continuous outcomes use $c=0.01$, while strictly positive PM$_1$ uses $c=0$. The continuous-outcome choice affects fewer than 1\% of positive observations except for the UPF--large-claim overlap, where it exceeds 12 of 397 positive observations (3\%), largely tiny polygon-clipping slivers. The sensitivity of the estimates to $c$ remains part of their interpretation.

**What to expect.** The forms answer slightly different questions and need not agree in magnitude, only in sign and in whether the pre-period is clean. Log and IHS will not track each other closely on an outcome that is 60% zeros no matter how $c$ is set — that is Chen & Roth's (2024) point, not a coding artifact — because $\operatorname{asinh}$ compresses toward the level near zero while $\log(y + c)$ places every zero at $\log c$. A form that rescues a coefficient while wrecking the pre-period is not a robustness result. -->

```{r NormalizationRobustness, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F}
# Outcome-normalization robustness: five forms x the main outcomes, each with a
# 2SLS estimate (headline specification, only the outcome's scaling changes) and
# its own calendar-year event-study placebo, summarized by a joint Wald test on
# the pre-period leads. Structure follows the archived v3
# (code/archive/starlink_results_v3.Rmd, NEW_RobustNormalization), rebuilt here
# against v3's forest-normalized headline and its x22_/x23_ control interactions.
fixest::setFixest_nthreads(1)
fixest::setFixest_estimation(reset = TRUE)

nz_dat = if (exists("dta_normal")) dta_normal else dta
# Raw pasture-transition area in km2. sh21_agr_pec is already a percentage of
# fixed 2021 forest area, while area_forest is stored in 1,000 km2 here.
nz_dat = nz_dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    nz_pasture_area = (sh21_agr_pec / 100) * area_forest * 1000
  )
# 2SLS uses the headline set; the full-panel placebo needs the pre-period
# interactions too (see covs_placebo).
nz_covs = covlist[[covs_headline_idx]]
nz_covs_plc = covs_placebo

# Numerators behind the headline outcomes. `denom = TRUE` marks the outcomes for
# which a per-area denominator is meaningful at all: PM1 is a concentration,
# so the two denominator rows are not applicable to it and print as an em dash
# instead of a number that would invite a comparison that does not exist.
# Labels are column HEADERS in the tables below, so they are written flat rather
# than indented the way var_names indents sub-rows.
nz_specs = tibble::tribble(
  ~outcome,                                  ~raw,                                ~forest,                                  ~municipal,                                  ~label,
  "r_n_mun_deter_degr",                     "n_mun_deter_degr",                 "r_n_mun_deter_degr",                     "rm_n_mun_deter_degr",                     "Degradation flags",
  "r_area_mun_deter_degr",                  "area_mun_deter_degr",              "r_area_mun_deter_degr",                  "rm_area_mun_deter_degr",                  "Degradation area",
  "r_area_ndpf_deter_degr",                 "area_ndpf_deter_degr",             "r_area_ndpf_deter_degr",                 "rm_area_ndpf_deter_degr",                 "  UPF",
  "r_area_over_ndpf_large_deter_degr",      "area_over_ndpf_large_deter_degr",  "r_area_over_ndpf_large_deter_degr",      "rm_area_over_ndpf_large_deter_degr",      "    with large-property claims",
  "rm_n_igni",                               "n_igni",                           "r_n_igni",                                "rm_n_igni",                                "Ignitions",
  "disp_shhiunb",                            "disp_shhiunb",                     NA_character_,                            NA_character_,                              "Ignition spatial HHI\u2020",
  "sh21_agr_pec",                            "nz_pasture_area",                  "sh21_agr_pec",                            "shm_agr_pec",                              "Forest transition to pasture",
  "pm1mun",                                  "pm1mun",                           NA_character_,                            NA_character_,                              "PM1\u2020",
  "r_n_mun_police",                         "n_mun_police",                     "r_n_mun_police",                          "rm_n_mun_police",                          "Enforcement fines"
)
stopifnot(identical(nz_specs$outcome, inference_outcomes))
missing_nz_raw = setdiff(nz_specs$raw, names(nz_dat))
if (length(missing_nz_raw)) {
  stop("Missing normalization outcomes: ", paste(missing_nz_raw, collapse = ", "))
}

# --- log constant, one per outcome -------------------------------------------
# log(y + c) is scale-dependent when y contains zeros, so use fixed unit-based
# rules rather than constants computed from sample minima. Raw integer counts
# use 1, their smallest positive increment and the value reported for Ignitions
# in Table 5. Zero-inclusive continuous outcomes use 0.01. In the 2022--2024
# panel, fewer than 1% of positive observations fall below 0.01 except for the
# UPF--large-claim overlap (12 of 397, 3%), largely polygon-clipping slivers.
# Strictly positive outcomes use c = 0. Written out so the specification cannot
# drift across tables or data builds.
nz_logc_default = c(
  n_mun_deter_degr = 1,
  area_mun_deter_degr = 0.01,
  area_over_ndpf_large_deter_degr = 0.01,
  n_igni = 1,
  disp_shhiunb = 0.01,
  nz_pasture_area = 0.01,
  n_mun_police = 1
)
nz_logc = vapply(
  nz_specs$raw,
  function(v) {
    y = nz_dat[[v]]
    pos = y[is.finite(y) & y > 0]
    if (!length(pos)) return(NA_real_)
    # No zeros -> no constant is needed at all and none is invented: log(y + 0)
    # is just log(y), which is what a strictly positive outcome (PM) should get.
    if (min(y, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) return(0)
    if (v %in% names(nz_logc_default)) return(nz_logc_default[[v]])
    # Fallback for an outcome with no entry above: largest power of 10 strictly
    # below the ROBUST floor (0.1th percentile of the positives, not the
    # minimum, for the reason spelled out above).
    fl = stats::quantile(pos, 0.001, names = FALSE)
    cc = 10^(ceiling(log10(fl)) - 1)
    if (cc >= fl) cc = cc / 10
    cc
  },
  numeric(1)
)
# Is the constant small enough? The interpretable test is not a percentile
# threshold but the SHARE of strictly positive observations that fall below c --
# those are the ones for which the constant, rather than the measurement,
# determines the transformed value. Anything under 1% is a handful of
# border-clipped slivers and is fine; more than that means c is doing real work
# and the row cannot be read as a semi-elasticity. Reported per outcome in the
# sensitivity table below, and warned about here.
nz_logc_share_below = vapply(
  nz_specs$raw,
  function(v) {
    y = nz_dat[[v]]
    pos = y[is.finite(y) & y > 0]
    if (!length(pos) || nz_logc[[v]] == 0) return(0)
    mean(pos < nz_logc[[v]])
  },
  numeric(1)
)
if (any(nz_logc_share_below > 0.01)) {
  bad = nz_specs$raw[nz_logc_share_below > 0.01]
  warning(
    "log constant exceeds 1% of the positive observations for: ",
    paste(sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", bad, 100 * nz_logc_share_below[bad]),
          collapse = ", "),
    ". Read those log rows as extensive-margin, not as semi-elasticities."
  )
}

# --- PRIOR-YEAR forest stock -------------------------------------------------
# `lag_areaforest` comes from the DATA, not from a join here. It is added to both v3
# panels, and work_dataframe.Rmd now emits it
# natively (alongside `areaforest_2021`), so this code is identical before and after
# the pipeline re-run -- no second edit, no chance of the two drifting.
#
# What the patch guarantees, all asserted there and re-checked below:
#   * areaforest_2021 reproduces area_forest exactly (the headline denominator has
#     always been the 2021 stock; the new name just says so)
#   * lag_areaforest is complete for 2017, because the lag is taken on mb_forest
#     where 2016 exists. Building it downstream instead loses 2017 and with it a
#     pre-period lead -- which by itself moved the joint pre-trend from 0.076 to
#     0.046 in testing, an artifact of the missing year rather than the denominator.
#   * lag_areaforest in 2022 equals the 2021 stock exactly, and the series declines
#     monotonically (3,822,343 km2 in 2017 to 3,708,810 in 2024)
#
# DataNormalization divided the area columns by 1,000 at the end of the chunk, so
# both forest columns arrive here in the same units as area_forest and need no
# rescaling -- which is the other reason to take them from the data rather than
# rebuild from a raw share.
stopifnot(
  "lag_areaforest" %in% names(nz_dat),
  !anyNA(nz_dat$lag_areaforest),
  all(nz_dat$lag_areaforest > 0)
)
nz_dat = nz_dat %>% dplyr::mutate(nz_forest_prior = lag_areaforest)

# --- build one outcome column per (form, numerator) --------------------------
.safe_div = function(num, den) {
  out = num / den
  out[!is.finite(out)] = NA_real_
  out
}
# `diff` (y - 2017-2021 municipal mean) was REMOVED (Fabio, 2026-08-11). It was an
# algebraic no-op kept as a panel check: the pre-period mean is time-invariant, so
# the codmun FE absorbs it exactly and the row reproduced `raw level` to every
# digit. It occupied a column without ever being a separate specification.
#
# `pri` (PRIOR-YEAR forest area) replaces it, and unlike `diff` it is a genuine
# alternative. The headline denominator `area_forest` is FIXED at 2021 -- 0% of
# municipalities show any within-municipality variation -- so the headline treats
# the area at risk as constant while the forest stock actually falls about 0.7% a
# year. The prior-year form uses each municipality's forest stock in t-1, which
# tracks the shrinking stock and stays predetermined with respect to the SAME
# year's outcome.
# The prior-year forest row was DROPPED (Fabio, 2026-08-15): the table reports
# the fixed 2021 stock only. It never was an independent alternative -- it moved
# every estimate by a few thousandths and its joint pre-trend tracked the
# headline's to the third decimal (0.098 against 0.099) -- while inviting the
# objection that the denominator itself responds to treatment, since the 2023 and
# 2024 lagged stocks already embody Starlink's earlier effect. The `pri` columns
# are still built below and lag_areaforest is still emitted by the pipeline, so
# re-adding the row is a one-line change here.
nz_forms = tibble::tribble(
  ~tag,     ~label,                                   ~needs_denom,
  "for",    "2021 forest area",                       TRUE,
  "mun",    "municipal area",                         TRUE,
  "lvl",    "raw level (no normalization)",           FALSE,
  "log",    "log(y + c)",                             FALSE,
  "ihs",    "IHS(y)",                                 FALSE
)

# The two denominator forms point at the columns DataNormalization already built
# (r_ = active denominator, rm_ = municipal area) rather than re-deriving them.
# That is not just tidier: for forest-risk outcomes, the forest-area row exactly
# reproduces the headline estimate; for ignitions, the municipal-area row does.
# A mismatch is therefore a real bug rather than a rescaling artifact. Re-deriving
# would also have to replicate
# the x100 / x1000 unit conventions and the areamun/area_forest division by
# 1,000 that happens at the end of DataNormalization.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(nz_specs))) {
  v = nz_specs$raw[i]
  lv = nz_dat[[v]]
  forest_v = nz_specs$forest[i]
  municipal_v = nz_specs$municipal[i]
  nz_dat[[paste0("nz_for_", v)]] = if (
    !is.na(forest_v) && forest_v %in% names(nz_dat)
  ) {
    nz_dat[[forest_v]]
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
  nz_dat[[paste0("nz_mun_", v)]] = if (
    !is.na(municipal_v) && municipal_v %in% names(nz_dat)
  ) {
    nz_dat[[municipal_v]]
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
  nz_dat[[paste0("nz_lvl_", v)]] = lv
  nz_dat[[paste0("nz_log_", v)]] = log(lv + nz_logc[[v]])
  nz_dat[[paste0("nz_ihs_", v)]] = asinh(lv)
  # PRIOR-YEAR forest denominator, built to the same x100 / x1000 unit conventions
  # DataNormalization uses so the row is comparable with the forest-area specification:
  # areas are % of the denominator, counts are per 1,000 km2.
  nz_dat[[paste0("nz_pri_", v)]] = if (!is.na(forest_v)) {
    .safe_div(lv, nz_dat$nz_forest_prior) * if (startsWith(v, "n_")) 1000 else 100
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
}

# --- 2SLS (headline spec) + placebo (reduced form, full panel) per cell ------
nz_ca = paste(paste0("ca_", setdiff(2017:CAL_END_YEAR, ctrl_base_year)), collapse = " + ")
nz_pre = paste0("ca_", 2017:2021)
# The estimation subset is taken from `dat` at CALL time, not from a snapshot
# made once. The log-constant sweep below adds its outcome columns to nz_dat
# after this function is defined, and a pre-filtered copy would not contain them
# -- every swept row silently returned NA before this was fixed.
nz_one = function(y, dat = nz_dat) {
  est_dat = dplyr::filter(dat, reg_sample == 1)
  stopifnot(y %in% names(dat))
  iv = tryCatch(
    fixest::feols(
      as.formula(paste0(
        y, " ~ ", paste(nz_covs, collapse = " + "),
        " | codmun + interaction(uf, year) | starlink ~ coverarea:year"
      )),
      data = est_dat, cluster = main_cluster_form, notes = FALSE
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  plc = tryCatch(
    fixest::feols(
      as.formula(paste0(
        y, " ~ ", nz_ca, " + ", paste(nz_covs_plc, collapse = " + "),
        " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)"
      )),
      data = dat, cluster = main_cluster_form, notes = FALSE
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  out = list(b = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, n = NA_integer_,
             pre_p = NA_real_, ev = NULL)
  if (!is.null(iv) && "fit_starlink" %in% rownames(fixest::coeftable(iv))) {
    # unname: coeftable carries "Estimate"/"Std. Error" names that data.frame()
    # would otherwise turn into row names in the assembled tables.
    ct = unname(fixest::coeftable(iv)["fit_starlink", ])
    out$b = ct[1]; out$se = ct[2]; out$p = ct[4]; out$n = stats::nobs(iv)
  }
  if (!is.null(plc)) {
    cc = as.data.frame(fixest::coeftable(plc))
    rn = intersect(rownames(cc), paste0("ca_", setdiff(2017:CAL_END_YEAR, ctrl_base_year)))
    have_pre = intersect(nz_pre, rn)
    if (length(have_pre) > 1) {
      w = tryCatch(
        fixest::wald(plc, keep = "^ca_20(17|18|19|20|21)$", print = FALSE),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      if (!is.null(w)) out$pre_p = w$p
    }
    if (length(rn)) {
      out$ev = data.frame(
        year = as.integer(sub("ca_", "", rn)),
        beta = cc[rn, 1], se = cc[rn, 2], row.names = NULL
      )
    }
  }
  out
}

nz_rows = list()
nz_ev = list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(nz_specs))) {
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(nz_forms))) {
    v = nz_specs$raw[i]
    y = sprintf("nz_%s_%s", nz_forms$tag[j], v)
    applicable = !(nz_forms$needs_denom[j] && is.na(nz_specs$forest[i]))
    if (!applicable || all(is.na(nz_dat[[y]]))) {
      nz_rows[[length(nz_rows) + 1]] = data.frame(
        outcome = nz_specs$label[i], outcome_key = nz_specs$outcome[i],
        form = nz_forms$label[j],
        estimate = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, cell = "\u2014", se = NA_real_,
        pre_p = NA_real_, n = NA_integer_
      )
      next
    }
    r = nz_one(y)
    nz_rows[[length(nz_rows) + 1]] = data.frame(
      outcome = nz_specs$label[i], outcome_key = nz_specs$outcome[i],
      form = nz_forms$label[j],
      estimate = r$b, p = r$p,
      cell = if (is.na(r$b)) "---" else sprintf(
        "%.4g%s", r$b,
        as.character(cut(r$p, c(-Inf, .01, .05, .1, Inf),
                         c("***", "**", "*", "")))
      ),
      se = r$se, pre_p = r$pre_p, n = r$n
    )
    if (!is.null(r$ev)) {
      nz_ev[[length(nz_ev) + 1]] = data.frame(
        outcome = nz_specs$label[i], form = nz_forms$label[j], r$ev
      )
    }
  }
}
NZ = dplyr::bind_rows(nz_rows)
NZE = dplyr::bind_rows(nz_ev)

# The 2021 forest area column uses that fixed denominator wherever meaningful.
# Ignition spatial HHI and PM1 instead appear under Municipal area because they are
# municipality-level outcomes, but the dagger marks that they remain in their
# original units and are not divided by municipal area.
nz_municipal_raw = c("disp_shhiunb", "pm1mun")
nz_display_forms = c("2021 forest area", "Municipal area", "IHS(y)", "log(y + c)")
NZ_display = dplyr::bind_rows(
  NZ %>%
    dplyr::filter(form == "2021 forest area"),
  NZ %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      (form == "municipal area" &
         !outcome_key %in% nz_municipal_raw) |
        (form == "raw level (no normalization)" &
           outcome_key %in% nz_municipal_raw)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(form = "Municipal area"),
  NZ %>%
    dplyr::filter(form %in% c("log(y + c)", "IHS(y)"))
)
stopifnot(
  nrow(NZ_display) == nrow(nz_specs) * length(nz_display_forms)
)

# --- wide layout: outcomes across the top, transformations down the side ------
# Same shape as the archived v3's normalization table, so the two can be read
# side by side. The estimate carries its own significance stars; SEs and N are
# not repeated in every cell (they are in the companion tables below), because
# the question this table answers is whether sign and significance survive the
# scaling, not how precise each cell is.
nz_wide = function(dat, value_col, digits = NULL) {
  dat %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      form = factor(form, levels = nz_forms$label),
      outcome = factor(outcome, levels = nz_specs$label),
      .val = if (is.null(digits)) {
        .data[[value_col]]
      } else {
        ifelse(is.na(.data[[value_col]]), "",
               sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), .data[[value_col]]))
      }
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(form, outcome) %>%
    dplyr::select(Transformation = form, outcome, .val) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = .val)
}

nz_wide_transposed = function(dat, value_col) {
  dat %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      outcome = factor(outcome, levels = nz_specs$label),
      form = factor(form, levels = nz_display_forms),
      .val = .data[[value_col]]
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(outcome, form) %>%
    dplyr::select(Outcome = outcome, Transformation = form, .val) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Transformation, values_from = .val)
}

knitr::kable(
  nz_wide_transposed(NZ_display, "cell"),
  align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(nz_display_forms)))#,
  # caption = paste0(
  #   "Outcome normalization: coefficient on instrumented Starlink. Stars are ",
  #   "*** p<0.01, ** p<0.05, * p<0.1 on ", main_cluster_label, "-clustered SEs. ",
  #   "Headline covariates, fixed effects and instrument throughout -- only the ",
  #   "outcome's scaling changes, so the columns are NOT on a common unit and only ",
  #   "sign and significance are comparable down a column. `y - 2017-2021 mean` is ",
  #   "an identity check, not a separate specification: the pre-period mean is ",
  #   "time-invariant, so the municipality FE absorbs it and the row must ",
  #   "reproduce `raw level` exactly. log constants: ",
  #   paste(sprintf(
  #     "%s c = %s", nz_specs$label,
  #     ifelse(nz_logc[nz_specs$raw] == 0, "0 (no zeros in the outcome)",
  #            format(nz_logc[nz_specs$raw], scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))
  #   ), collapse = "; "),
  #   ". An em dash means that a per-area denominator is not meaningful for a concentration."
  # )
  ,
  # THIS TABLE NEEDS A CAPTION even though the long one above stays disabled.
  # Pandoc attaches a trailing caption to the PRECEDING table, so when this table
  # had none and the pre-trend table below did, the pre-trend caption migrated up
  # and sat on the coefficients -- the numbers were right and the label was wrong,
  # which is worse than no label. One caption per table keeps them paired.
  caption = paste0(
    "Outcome normalization: coefficient on instrumented ",
    "Starlink, ", main_cluster_label, "-clustered. Transformations are not on a ",
    "common unit; compare sign and significance across each outcome row."
  )
)

# --- joint pre-trend test, one cell per outcome x form -----------------------
# pre_p is already computed for every cell above: a Wald test on the five
# pre-period leads (ca_2017..ca_2021) of that form's OWN reduced-form event
# study, on the full 2017-CAL_END_YEAR panel with the same covariates and cluster.
# This table only formats it.
#
# THE MARKER CONVENTION IS INVERTED relative to the estimate table above. There a
# star means the effect is detectable, which is the result. Here a low p means the
# PRE-PERIOD is detectable, which is a failure. Flagging with "!" rather than "*"
# keeps a reader scanning for stars from reading these as good news:
#   (blank) p >= 0.10  pre-period clean, the null of no pre-trend is not rejected
#   !       p <  0.10  pre-trend at 10%
#   !!      p <  0.05  pre-trend at 5% -- the form fails the placebo
#
# A high p is NOT proof the pre-period is clean, only a failure to reject; with
# five leads and municipality-by-state-year fixed effects the test has limited
# power. Read it as a screen, not a certificate.
NZ = NZ %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pre_cell = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(pre_p) ~ "n/a",
      pre_p < 0.05 ~ sprintf("%.3f !!", pre_p),
      pre_p < 0.10 ~ sprintf("%.3f !", pre_p),
      TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", pre_p)
    )
  )

# The pre-trend diagnostics remain available in NZ for internal checking, but
# the second normalization table is intentionally omitted from the output.
if (FALSE) knitr::kable(
  nz_wide(NZ, "pre_cell"),
  align = paste0("l", strrep("r", nrow(nz_specs))),
  caption = paste0(
    "Joint pre-trend test for each cell above: Wald p-value on the five ",
    "pre-period leads (2017-2021) of that form's own reduced-form event study, ",
    "full 2017-", CAL_END_YEAR, " panel, same covariates and ", main_cluster_label,
    " cluster. ! = p<0.10, !! = p<0.05, i.e. a DETECTED pre-trend; blank means ",
    "the pre-period is clean at 10%. A form that rescues a coefficient in the ",
    "table above while failing here is not a robustness result."
  )
)

#   caption = paste0(

#     "transformation is undefined for some rows."
#   )
```
