### Coefficient-leverage deletion


**Identifying-mass map.** Each municipality is shaded by quintile of its coefficient-leverage share in the instrument-predicted Starlink component.

```{r MapVarShareMass, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.3, dpi=150}
# === Identifying-mass map =====================================================
# Maps each municipality's IV identifying mass as quintiles of its
# per-municipality variance share (% of total identifying variance): OrRd
# quintile fill, state outlines in black, right-side legend, tight crop
# (coord_sf expand = FALSE), ~1.62:1 landscape.
#
# The quintile breaks are recomputed from the live data on every knit, so the
# legend tracks the current distribution -- the top bin's upper bound is the
# largest per-municipality variance share.
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(sf))

# Per-municipality Frisch-Waugh variance share (mirrors the VarShareHist chunk
# below; computed here too so the map runs first and stays self-contained).
muni_influence = muni_var_share(dta_robust, robust_covs)

# Panel-matched Legal Amazon municipality polygons.
iv_mass_poly = readRDS(mun_legal_amazon_geometry) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  st_transform(4674) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  mutate(codmun = as.numeric(codmun)) %>%
  select(codmun)

# Mojui dos Campos (1504752) was split off Santarem (1506807) in 2013 and is
# merged back into it in the panel (the minimum comparable area, 772 units), so
# the shapefile carries a polygon the estimation data has no row for. Left as
# is, it joins to NA and prints as a grey hole inside Santarem. Dissolve the two
# into the parent geometry before any share is joined, so both maps (calendar
# and PRODES) colour the merged unit as one.
iv_mass_poly = iv_mass_poly %>%
  mutate(codmun = ifelse(codmun == 1504752, 1506807, codmun)) %>%
  group_by(codmun) %>%
  summarise(.groups = "drop") %>%
  st_make_valid()

# ── Map builder, shared with the PRODES panel ─────────────────────────────────
# Factored out of this chunk (Fabio, 2026-08-12) so the PRODES variance-trim
# section can draw the same map from ITS own variance-share distribution. The
# polygons are read once above and passed in, rather than re-read per call.
#
# Everything below is the previous inline code verbatim, with `muni_influence`
# replaced by the `share_df` argument; the calendar call underneath therefore
# produces exactly the figure it did before.
make_iv_mass_map = function(share_df, poly = iv_mass_poly) {
  # Variance share as % of total identifying variance, joined onto the polygons.
  df = poly %>%
    left_join(
      share_df %>% transmute(codmun, var_share_pct = share_var * 100),
      by = "codmun"
    )

  # Quintile bins labeled "[lo - hi]" to three decimals.
  brks = quantile(df$var_share_pct, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2), na.rm = TRUE)
  # A concentrated distribution can put two quintile boundaries at the same
  # value, and cut() rejects non-unique breaks outright. Collapsing them yields
  # fewer, wider bins instead of an error that would take the whole chunk down.
  brks = unique(brks)
  if (length(brks) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  labs_q = sprintf("[%.3f - %.3f]", brks[-length(brks)], brks[-1])
  df = df %>%
    mutate(
      var_share_q = cut(
        var_share_pct,
        breaks = brks,
        labels = labs_q,
        include.lowest = TRUE
      )
    )

  # State (UF) outlines: dissolve the municipalities by their 2-digit IBGE prefix.
  states = df %>%
    mutate(uf = codmun %/% 100000L) %>%
    group_by(uf) %>%
    summarise(.groups = "drop")

  ggplot() +
    # Grey base layer for all municipalities, so any municipality outside the
    # estimation sample (NA variance share) is still drawn grey rather than left
    # as a hole -- and carries no "NA" key in the legend.
    geom_sf(data = df, fill = "grey90", color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.05) +
    # Quintile fill on top, NA dropped so the legend shows only the quintiles.
    geom_sf(
      data = dplyr::filter(df, !is.na(var_share_q)),
      aes(fill = var_share_q),
      color = "grey80",
      linewidth = 0.05
    ) +
    geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_brewer(
      palette = "OrRd",
      drop = FALSE,
      name = "Leverage-share quintile\n(% of total identifying variation)"
    ) +
    coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
    theme_void(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.key.size = unit(0.9, "lines"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
      plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
    )
}

fig_iv_mass = make_iv_mass_map(muni_influence)

print(fig_iv_mass)
```

*Quintiles of the municipality-level coefficient-leverage share across the Legal Amazon; darker shades supply more identifying variation. State boundaries in black.*


```{r VarShareHist, message=F, warning=F, echo=F, fig.height=3.6, fig.width=6.5, results="asis"}
# === Distribution of per-municipality variance share + trim cutoffs ==========
# Histogram of the per-municipality Frisch-Waugh variance share (share_var from
# muni_influence) and the upper-tail cutoffs used by the trim exercise below.
# The "max retained" variance share at trim level X is the (1 - X) quantile:
# trimming the top X% leaves that value as the largest in the kept sample. The
# same quantile() call drives make_var_trim_data() in the next chunk.

# The Monotonicity-section quintile/influence analysis was removed; recompute the per-municipality
# variance share here so this trim (Table A6) is self-contained.
muni_influence = muni_var_share(dta_robust, robust_covs)

# Variance share as a percentage of total identifying variance (map-legend unit).
var_share_pct = muni_influence$share_var * 100

# Diagnostic sweep: Full (0%) followed by 0.5-percentage-point upper-tail
# deletions through 2%. n_dropped and var_share_dropped_pct are read
# off the ACTUAL cutoff (share_var > the (1 - tail) quantile), matching
# make_var_trim_data().
var_trim_cuts = tibble(
  tail = seq(0, 0.02, by = 0.005),
  sample = c(
    "Full (0%)",
    paste0("Top ", 100 * seq(0.005, 0.02, by = 0.005), "%")
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    max_retained_pct = quantile(var_share_pct, probs = 1 - tail, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_dropped = vapply(
      tail,
      function(t) {
        if (t == 0) {
          0L
        } else {
          as.integer(sum(
            muni_influence$share_var >
              quantile(muni_influence$share_var, 1 - t, na.rm = TRUE),
            na.rm = TRUE
          ))
        }
      },
      integer(1)
    ),
    var_share_dropped_pct = vapply(
      tail,
      function(t) {
        if (t == 0) {
          0
        } else {
          sum(
            muni_influence$share_var[
              muni_influence$share_var >
                quantile(muni_influence$share_var, 1 - t, na.rm = TRUE)
            ],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ) *
            100
        }
      },
      numeric(1)
    )
  )

# Report the maximum variance share retained at each trim level.
cat(
  knitr::kable(
    var_trim_cuts %>%
      transmute(
        `Sample` = sample,
        `Municipalities dropped` = n_dropped,
        `Leverage share deleted (% of total)` = sprintf(
          "%.2f",
          var_share_dropped_pct
        ),
        `Max retained leverage share (% of total)` = sprintf(
          "%.3f",
          max_retained_pct
        )
      ),
    format = "html",
    align = "l",
    caption = sprintf(
      paste(
        "Coefficient-leverage deletion: municipalities deleted and the",
        "leverage share removed from 0%% through 2%% in 0.5-point steps,",
        "with the maximum leverage share retained",
        "(N = %d municipalities)."
      ),
      nrow(muni_influence)
    )
  ) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "bordered", "hover", "condensed"),
      full_width = FALSE,
      position = "left"
    ),
  sep = "\n"
)
cat("\n\n")

# Concentration ex ante: effective sample size = inverse Herfindahl of the
# per-municipality variance shares (share_var sums to 1). A small value means a
# few municipalities supply most identifying variation, so the trim below is
# load-bearing; a large value means concentration is not a first-order concern.
eff_n_varshare = 1 / sum(muni_influence$share_var^2, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf(
  paste0(
    "*Effective sample size (1/HHI of variance shares) = **%.1f** of %d ",
    "municipalities; largest single share = **%.2f%%**, top-5 combined = ",
    "**%.1f%%**.*\n\n"
  ),
  eff_n_varshare,
  nrow(muni_influence),
  max(var_share_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
  sum(sort(var_share_pct, decreasing = TRUE)[1:5], na.rm = TRUE)
))

# Histogram with all four requested upper-tail cutoffs marked, using the same
# colors as the trimmed-estimate panels. The per-municipality
# variance share spans several orders of magnitude (a long thin upper tail over
# a mass of near-zero shares), so the x-axis is shown on a log10 scale. Zero
# shares cannot be displayed on a logarithmic axis and are omitted.
hist_df = tibble(var_share_pct = var_share_pct) %>%
  dplyr::filter(var_share_pct > 0)

# Use preliminary equal-width log10 bins to detect an isolated sparse lower
# tail. Begin at the first run of three occupied bins; if no such run exists,
# retain the full positive support.
log_hist_breaks_all = 10^seq(
  log10(min(hist_df$var_share_pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
  log10(max(hist_df$var_share_pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
  length.out = 41
)
log_hist_counts_all = hist(
  hist_df$var_share_pct,
  breaks = log_hist_breaks_all,
  plot = FALSE
)$counts
occupied_run_start = which(
  head(log_hist_counts_all, -2) > 0 &
    log_hist_counts_all[2:(length(log_hist_counts_all) - 1)] > 0 &
    tail(log_hist_counts_all, -2) > 0
)
first_hist_bin = if (length(occupied_run_start) > 0) occupied_run_start[1] else 1L
hist_x_min = log_hist_breaks_all[first_hist_bin]
hist_df = hist_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(var_share_pct >= hist_x_min)

# Recompute 40 equal-width log10 bins over the displayed support.
log_hist_breaks = 10^seq(
  log10(hist_x_min),
  log10(max(hist_df$var_share_pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
  length.out = 41
)
# Shared row order and grayscale key for the manuscript composite figure. Full
# is red and appears first; increasingly stringent trims run downward in
# progressively darker gray. The same shades mark the histogram cutoffs.
trim_panel_levels = c("Full", "Top 0.5%", "Top 1%", "Top 1.5%", "Top 2%")
trim_panel_cols = c(
  "Full" = "#e41a1c",
  "Top 0.5%" = "grey72",
  "Top 1%" = "grey58",
  "Top 1.5%" = "grey44",
  "Top 2%" = "grey30"
)
fig_var_share_hist = ggplot(hist_df, aes(x = var_share_pct)) +
  geom_histogram(
    breaks = log_hist_breaks,
    fill = "red",
    alpha = 0.70,
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    data = dplyr::filter(var_trim_cuts, sample %in% trim_panel_levels[-1]),
    aes(xintercept = max_retained_pct, color = sample),
    linewidth = 0.35,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = trim_panel_cols[trim_panel_levels[-1]]) +
  scale_x_log10(
    limits = range(log_hist_breaks),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.005, 0.005)),
    breaks = c(0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10),
    labels = function(b) {
      sub(
        "^0\\.",
        ".",
        trimws(format(b, drop0trailing = TRUE, scientific = FALSE))
      )
    }
  ) +  labs(
    x = "Municipality leverage share (% of total, log scale)",
    y = NULL,
    color = "Deletion cutoff (max retained)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", text = element_text(size = 14))

print(fig_var_share_hist)
```

```{r RobustTrimVarShare, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F, fig.height=24, fig.width=8, results = "asis"}
# Variance-share trim sensitivity ------------------------------------------
# Mirrors the RobustTrim chunk above, but trims on the per-municipality
# Frisch-Waugh variance share (share_var, from muni_influence in
# NEW_InfluenceMuniState) instead of on the raw 2021 mobile-coverage tails.
# Reuses estimate_starlink(), robust_covs, and robust_plot_label from the
# RobustTrim chunk; this test uses the eight main-form outcomes shared with the
# leave-one-state-out exercise and Appendix Table A7.

# Single-thread fixest (same Windows ACCESS_VIOLATION guard as RobustTrim).
fixest::setFixest_nthreads(1)
fixest::setFixest_estimation(reset = TRUE)

# One-sided (upper-tail) trim: drop the municipalities supplying the most
# identifying mass. share_var is the per-municipality variance share.
var_trim_defs = var_trim_cuts %>%
  transmute(
    sample = if_else(tail == 0, "Full", sample),
    tail
  )

make_var_trim_data = function(tail) {
  if (tail == 0) {
    return(dta_robust)
  }

  cut_hi = quantile(muni_influence$share_var, probs = 1 - tail, na.rm = TRUE)
  keep_mun = muni_influence %>%
    filter(share_var <= cut_hi) %>%
    pull(codmun)

  dta_robust %>% filter(codmun %in% keep_mun)
}

# Use the same headline forms as the placebo and LOSO exercises, including
# ignitions per 100 km² of municipal area.
var_trim_outcomes = appendix_stability_outcomes
var_trim_outcome_labels = setNames(
  unname(appendix_stability_labels),
  var_trim_outcomes
)
var_trim_outcome_label = function(x) {
  out = unname(var_trim_outcome_labels[x])
  out[is.na(out)] = robust_plot_label(x[is.na(out)])
  out
}
var_trim_labs = setNames(
  var_trim_outcome_label(var_trim_outcomes),
  var_trim_outcomes
)

var_trim_est = map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(var_trim_defs)), function(i) {
  data_i = make_var_trim_data(var_trim_defs$tail[i])
  map_dfr(var_trim_outcomes, ~ estimate_starlink(data_i, .x)) %>%
    mutate(sample = var_trim_defs$sample[i], tail = var_trim_defs$tail[i])
}) %>%
  mutate(
    sample = factor(sample, levels = var_trim_defs$sample),
    outcome_id = factor(outcome, levels = var_trim_outcomes),
    outcome_label = var_trim_outcome_label(outcome)
  )

fig_var_trim_robust = ggplot(
  var_trim_est,
  aes(y = sample, x = estimate, color = sample)
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.35,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = conf.low95, xend = conf.high95, yend = sample),
    linewidth = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.45
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = conf.low90, xend = conf.high90, yend = sample),
    linewidth = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.45
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~outcome_id,
    scales = "free_x",
    ncol = 1,
    strip.position = "left",
    labeller = as_labeller(var_trim_labs)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Full" = "red",
      setNames(
        grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("grey75", "grey15"))(
          sum(var_trim_defs$tail > 0)
        ),
        var_trim_defs$sample[var_trim_defs$tail > 0]
      )
    )
  ) +
  # Discrete y limits run bottom-to-top. Reversing the diagnostic sequence
  # places Full (0%) at the top, followed downward by 0.5-point trim steps.
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(var_trim_defs$sample)) +
  labs(
    x = "Estimate",
    y = NULL,
    color = "Coefficient-leverage deletion (upper tail)",
    caption = "Whiskers: 95% CI (light); 90% CI (darker)."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    text = element_text(size = 14)
  )

print(fig_var_trim_robust)

# === Paper panel: 3x3 grid (8 outcomes + variance-share histogram) ===========
# The eight coefficient panels follow Appendix Table A7's row order, with the
# variance-share distribution last. Each panel is titled "(x) <label>" at the
# top-left; Full through Top 2% appear only on the left-most panel in each row.
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(patchwork))

# Trim colors and displayed levels are defined once as trim_panel_cols and
# trim_panel_levels in the histogram chunk above, so the coefficient panels
# and histogram use the same red-to-gray key.

# One coefficient panel per headline outcome, titled "(tag) <label>" top-left.
# The Full sample and all four requested deletions are shown.
make_trim_panel = function(oc, tag, show_y_labels) {
  d = var_trim_est %>%
    dplyr::filter(outcome == oc, sample %in% trim_panel_levels) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = trim_panel_levels))
  panel_title = if (identical(oc, "pm1mun")) {
    expression(paste("(g) ", PM[1]))
  } else {
    paste0(tag, " ", var_trim_outcome_label(oc))
  }
  ggplot(d, aes(y = sample, x = estimate, color = sample)) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.3,
      linetype = "dashed"
    ) +
    # The whole row follows the Full/red and trim/grayscale key. The 95% interval
    # is lighter and the nested 90% interval is darker.
    geom_segment(
      aes(x = conf.low95, xend = conf.high95, yend = sample),
      linewidth = 1.4,
      alpha = 0.28
    ) +
    geom_segment(
      aes(x = conf.low90, xend = conf.high90, yend = sample),
      linewidth = 1.4,
      alpha = 0.68
    ) +
    geom_point(size = 2.1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = trim_panel_cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(trim_panel_levels), drop = FALSE) +
    labs(
      title = panel_title,
      x = "Estimate",
      y = NULL,
      color = "Coefficient-leverage deletion (upper tail)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = if (show_y_labels) {
        element_text(color = "black", size = 7.5)
      } else {
        element_blank()
      },
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9.5),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
}

trim_coefficient_panels = Map(
  function(oc, tag, panel_index) {
    make_trim_panel(
      oc,
      tag,
      show_y_labels = panel_index %in% c(1, 4, 7)
    )
  },
  var_trim_outcomes,
  paste0("(", letters[seq_along(var_trim_outcomes)], ")"),
  seq_along(var_trim_outcomes)
)

# (i) variance-share histogram, titled top-left. Its cutoff colors need no
# legend because the trim levels are labeled on each coefficient panel.
p_i = fig_var_share_hist +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "(i) Leverage-share distribution",
    x = "Leverage share (% of total, log scale)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9.5),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# Three-column grid. Each coefficient panel carries the sample labels directly,
# so a separate color legend is unnecessary.
fig_var_trim_panel = patchwork::wrap_plots(
  c(trim_coefficient_panels, list(p_i)),
  ncol = 3
)
print(fig_var_trim_panel)
```


### Leave-one-microregion-out

Each red point comes from re-estimating the headline 2SLS after deleting one microregion. Dark- and light-gray bars are 90% and 95% confidence intervals, respectively. Microregions are ordered within the UF brackets shown below the x-axis.

<!-- Leave-one-microregion-out is computed in a hidden estimation chunk. It preserves
the former municipality-level figure layout while deleting the same geographic
unit used to cluster the headline standard errors. -->

```{r RobustOneOut, eval = T, include=FALSE, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F, results = "asis", fig.height=3.2, fig.width=13}
# Leave-one-microregion-out robustness -------------------------------------
# Per-outcome deletion universe: each microregion is deleted only when at least
# one of its municipalities belongs to that outcome's estimation sample. This
# preserves the restricted UPF and spatial-HHI samples without running refits
# for microregions that feols already excludes from those outcomes.
#
# LOO/LOSO share the same eight main-form outcomes and row order as the
# variance-share trim exercise and Appendix Table A7.
loo_loso_outcomes = appendix_stability_outcomes

outcome_microreg = setNames(
  lapply(loo_loso_outcomes, function(oc) {
    estimation_mun = estimation_municipalities(dta_robust, oc)
    dta_robust %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        reg_sample == 1,
        codmun %in% estimation_mun,
        !is.na(microreg)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::transmute(microreg = as.character(microreg)) %>%
      dplyr::distinct() %>%
      dplyr::pull(microreg) %>%
      sort()
  }),
  loo_loso_outcomes
)

# One UF per microregion, used only to reproduce the former UF-bracket layout.
microreg_uf_lookup = dta_robust %>%
  dplyr::filter(reg_sample == 1, !is.na(microreg), !is.na(uf)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    dropped_microreg = as.character(microreg),
    dropped_uf_code = as.character(uf)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(microreg_uf_lookup$dropped_microreg))

# Outer-loop pool = union of every outcome's microregion universe. The worker
# skips a microregion for outcomes whose own estimation sample does not use it.
loo_microregions_full = sort(unique(unlist(outcome_microreg)))

if (loo_microregion_share == 1) {
  loo_microregions = loo_microregions_full
} else if (loo_microregion_share == 0) {
  loo_microregions = loo_microregions_full[0]
} else {
  set.seed(20260429)
  n_loo = max(
    1,
    ceiling(length(loo_microregions_full) * loo_microregion_share)
  )
  loo_microregions = sort(sample(loo_microregions_full, n_loo))
}

cat(
  "**Leave-one-microregion-out pool:** ",
  length(loo_microregions),
  " / ",
  length(loo_microregions_full),
  " (full-panel outcomes); restricted outcomes delete only microregions ",
  "represented in their own estimation sample.\n\n",
  sep = ""
)

if (length(loo_microregions) == 0) {
  cat(
    "*Leave-one-microregion-out skipped because `loo_microregion_share = 0`.*\n\n"
  )
} else {
  # Keep the future worker independent of the Rmd's global environment. Functions
  # defined in that environment otherwise carry all previously created spatial
  # objects when future inspects them, making a small regression worker appear to
  # be several GiB. Every dependency needed below is passed explicitly, and the
  # worker's enclosing environment is reset to baseenv().
  loo_worker = function(
    drop_microreg,
    data_worker,
    outcomes_worker,
    outcome_microreg_worker,
    covariates_worker,
    cluster_chars_worker,
    ignition_outcomes_worker,
    library_paths_worker
  ) {
    .libPaths(library_paths_worker)
    fixest::setFixest_nthreads(1)

    data_i = dplyr::filter(
      data_worker,
      as.character(microreg) != drop_microreg
    )
    purrr::map_dfr(outcomes_worker, function(outcome_i) {
      if (!(drop_microreg %in% outcome_microreg_worker[[outcome_i]])) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      data_reg = dplyr::filter(data_i, reg_sample == 1)
      if (outcome_i %in% ignition_outcomes_worker) {
        data_reg = dplyr::filter(
          data_reg,
          as.character(year) != "2025"
        )
      }
      model = stats::as.formula(paste0(
        outcome_i,
        " ~ ",
        paste(covariates_worker, collapse = " + "),
        " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)",
        " | starlink ~ coverarea:year"
      ))
      cluster_formula = stats::as.formula(paste0(
        "~", paste(cluster_chars_worker, collapse = " + ")
      ))

      result = tryCatch(
        {
          est = fixest::feols(
            model,
            data = data_reg,
            cluster = cluster_formula,
            notes = FALSE,
            nthreads = 1
          )
          tab95 = broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
          tab90 = broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90)
          tab95 = dplyr::filter(tab95, term == "fit_starlink")
          tab90 = dplyr::filter(tab90, term == "fit_starlink")
          tibble::tibble(
            outcome = outcome_i,
            estimate = tab95$estimate[1],
            std.error = tab95$std.error[1],
            statistic = tab95$statistic[1],
            p.value = tab95$p.value[1],
            conf.low95 = tab95$conf.low[1],
            conf.high95 = tab95$conf.high[1],
            conf.low90 = tab90$conf.low[1],
            conf.high90 = tab90$conf.high[1],
            N = stats::nobs(est),
            n_mun = dplyr::n_distinct(data_reg$codmun),
            error = NA_character_
          )
        },
        error = function(e) {
          tibble::tibble(
            outcome = outcome_i,
            estimate = NA_real_,
            std.error = NA_real_,
            statistic = NA_real_,
            p.value = NA_real_,
            conf.low95 = NA_real_,
            conf.high95 = NA_real_,
            conf.low90 = NA_real_,
            conf.high90 = NA_real_,
            N = nrow(data_reg),
            n_mun = dplyr::n_distinct(data_reg$codmun),
            error = conditionMessage(e)
          )
        }
      )
      dplyr::mutate(result, dropped_microreg = drop_microreg)
    })
  }
  environment(loo_worker) = baseenv()

  # This sweep is the single largest cost in the document: every microregion is
  # dropped in turn and every outcome re-estimated on the remainder. It runs in
  # batches so a batch's worker memory is released before the next one starts.
  loo_est = local({
    future::plan(
      future::multisession,
      # robust_max_workers is the worker count DIRECTLY: one number, one meaning.
      workers = min(robust_max_workers, length(loo_microregions))
    )
    on.exit(future::plan(future::sequential), add = TRUE)
    # Capture the main-session library paths so each fresh multisession worker
    # can be repointed at them below (see .libPaths() inside the worker).
    loo_worker_libpaths = .libPaths()

    batch_size = max(6L, 2L * robust_max_workers)
    loo_batches = split(
      loo_microregions,
      ceiling(seq_along(loo_microregions) / batch_size)
    )
    loo_parts = vector("list", length(loo_batches))

    for (batch_i in seq_along(loo_batches)) {
      loo_parts[[batch_i]] = dplyr::bind_rows(future_lapply(
        X = loo_batches[[batch_i]],
        FUN = loo_worker,
        data_worker = dta_robust,
        outcomes_worker = loo_loso_outcomes,
        outcome_microreg_worker = outcome_microreg,
        covariates_worker = robust_covs,
        cluster_chars_worker = main_cluster_chars,
        ignition_outcomes_worker = igni_outcomes,
        library_paths_worker = loo_worker_libpaths,
        future.seed = TRUE,
        future.globals = FALSE
      ))
      message(sprintf(
        "calendar LOMO: batch %s/%s complete (%s of %s microregions)",
        batch_i, length(loo_batches),
        sum(lengths(loo_batches[seq_len(batch_i)])), length(loo_microregions)
      ))
    }
    dplyr::bind_rows(loo_parts)
  })

  full_for_loo = robust_full %>%
    dplyr::select(
      outcome,
      full_estimate = estimate,
      full_p = p.value,
      full_conf.low95 = conf.low95,
      full_conf.high95 = conf.high95
    )

  loo_aug = loo_est %>%
    dplyr::left_join(microreg_uf_lookup, by = "dropped_microreg") %>%
    dplyr::left_join(full_for_loo, by = "outcome") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      abs_change = abs(estimate - full_estimate),
      same_sign = sign(estimate) == sign(full_estimate),
      sig10 = p.value <= 0.10,
      sig05 = p.value <= 0.05
    )

  # Coefficient-stability plots (Derenoncourt Fig. C5 style): ONE SEPARATE figure
  # per outcome (no faceting). Each drops one microregion at a time; points are
  # ordered by UF and microregion so same-state microregions are contiguous. A
  # UF "bracket" axis is drawn at the bottom as continuous horizontal lines
  # (one segment per state, end caps at boundaries, sigla centered). The point
  # and nested 90%/95% intervals use the same red-and-gray hierarchy as LOSO.

  # IBGE 2-digit prefix of codmun -> Legal-Amazon UF sigla.
  uf_code_to_sigla = c(
    "11" = "RO",
    "12" = "AC",
    "13" = "AM",
    "14" = "RR",
    "15" = "PA",
    "16" = "AP",
    "17" = "TO",
    "21" = "MA",
    "51" = "MT"
  )

  # `dat` and `label_fn` are arguments purely so the PRODES deletion section
  # can reuse this panel builder on its own augmented frame. Both default to the
  # calendar-panel objects, so every existing call is unchanged.
  make_loo_fig = function(oc, dat = loo_aug, label_fn = robust_label) {
    # Per-outcome panel: rank only microregions in THIS outcome's estimation
    # sample. Ordering by UF and microregion retains the dense-CI layout and the
    # UF bracket axis used by the former municipality-level diagnostic.
    d = dat %>%
      dplyr::filter(outcome == oc, !is.na(estimate)) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dropped_uf_code, dropped_microreg) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        x = dplyr::row_number(),
        uf_code = as.character(dropped_uf_code),
        uf = dplyr::coalesce(unname(uf_code_to_sigla[uf_code]), uf_code)
      )
    if (nrow(d) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    # UF "bracket" axis: one continuous horizontal segment per state (start->end),
    # vertical end caps at the boundaries, and the sigla centered under each block.
    # Drawn as data layers below the points (using this outcome's own y-range),
    # so it reads like a ruler rather than grid lines through the panel.
    uf_axis = d %>%
      dplyr::group_by(uf) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(start = min(x), end = max(x), .groups = "drop") %>%
      dplyr::arrange(start) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(mid = (start + end) / 2)
    uf_bound_df = tibble::tibble(
      b = sort(unique(c(uf_axis$start - 0.5, uf_axis$end + 0.5)))
    )

    # y-range from the CIs (and zero), to place the bracket below the data.
    y_lo = min(c(d$conf.low95, 0), na.rm = TRUE)
    y_hi = max(c(d$conf.high95, 0), na.rm = TRUE)
    rng = y_hi - y_lo
    if (!is.finite(rng) || rng <= 0) {
      rng = 1
    }
    y_br = y_lo - 0.12 * rng # bracket baseline
    cap = 0.04 * rng # half-height of the end caps

    ggplot(d, aes(x = x, y = estimate)) +
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = 0,
        color = "black",
        linewidth = 0.4,
        linetype = "dashed"
      ) +
      # 95% outer interval (light gray), with the 90% interval overlaid in
      # darker gray, matching the leave-one-state-out figures.
      geom_linerange(
        aes(ymin = conf.low95, ymax = conf.high95),
        color = "grey80",
        linewidth = 1.2,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) +
      geom_linerange(
        aes(ymin = conf.low90, ymax = conf.high90),
        color = "grey40",
        linewidth = 1.2,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) +
      geom_point(color = "red", size = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
      # continuous horizontal line, one segment per state ...
      geom_segment(
        data = uf_axis,
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        aes(x = start - 0.5, xend = end + 0.5, y = y_br, yend = y_br),
        linewidth = 0.4
      ) +
      # ... vertical end caps at every block boundary ...
      geom_segment(
        data = uf_bound_df,
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        aes(x = b, xend = b, y = y_br - cap, yend = y_br + cap),
        linewidth = 0.4
      ) +
      # ... and the UF sigla centered under each block.
      geom_text(
        data = uf_axis,
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        aes(x = mid, y = y_br - 2.4 * cap, label = uf),
        size = 3,
        vjust = 1
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
      scale_y_continuous(
        breaks = pretty(c(y_lo, y_hi), n = 5),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.16, 0.05))
      ) +
      coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
      labs(
        title = trimws(label_fn(oc)),
        x = NULL,
        y = "2SLS coefficient"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5),
        plot.margin = margin(6, 10, 8, 10),
        legend.position = "none",
        text = element_text(size = 11)
      )
  }

  # Print one figure per outcome and collect the panels into one diagnostic.
  loo_panels = list()
  for (oc in loo_loso_outcomes) {
    p_oc = make_loo_fig(oc)
    if (is.null(p_oc)) {
      next
    }
    loo_panels[[oc]] = p_oc
    print(p_oc)
    cat("\n\n")
  }

  # Combined manuscript diagnostic. Match the LOSO exhibit's 10 x 8 inch,
  # two-column by four-row page geometry. Horizontal titles cost little height
  # and preserve the scarce plotting width needed for 99 microregion estimates;
  # rotating them into a left strip would narrow every panel.
  loo_fig_titles = appendix_stability_titles
  loo_panel_order = appendix_stability_outcomes
  if (all(loo_panel_order %in% names(loo_panels))) {
    loo_panels_lettered = lapply(seq_along(loo_panel_order), function(i) {
      oc = loo_panel_order[i]
      panel_title = if (identical(oc, "pm1mun")) {
        bquote(paste("(", .(letters[i]), ") ", PM[1]))
      } else {
        loo_fig_titles[[oc]]
      }
      loo_panels[[oc]] +
        labs(title = panel_title, y = appendix_stability_ylabs[[oc]]) +
        theme(
          plot.title = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
          plot.margin = margin(4, 5, 6, 5),
          text = element_text(size = 8)
        )
    })
    fig_lomro_8 = ggpubr::ggarrange(
      plotlist = loo_panels_lettered,
      ncol = 2,
      nrow = 4,
      align = "hv"
    )
  }
}
```

```{r LooFigInline, include=TRUE, message=F, warning=F, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, echo=F}
# Guarded because the object only exists when the LOO block above ran.
if (exists("fig_lomro_8")) print(fig_lomro_8) else
  cat("_(leave-one-microregion-out figure not produced in this run)_\n")
```

<!-- **Reading the result.** Each interval is the 95% confidence interval after
deleting one microregion. The UF brackets group the deleted microregions by
state. This diagnostic remains hidden until its results are incorporated into
the manuscript. -->


### Leave-one-state-out


- Drop each of the 9 Legal-Amazon states (UF) in turn and re-estimate.


```{r RobustOneStateOut, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F, results = "asis", fig.height=3.2, fig.width=6}
# Leave-one-STATE-out robustness ------------------------------------------
# Drop each UF (the 9 Legal-Amazon states) in turn and re-estimate the headline
# 2SLS on the remaining 8 states. Dropping a whole state removes ~1/9 of the
# panel, so unlike leave-one-microregion-out this can move the estimate; each
# whole-state drop is an exact cluster-level DFBETA on beta-hat. Reuses
# estimate_starlink(), robust_outcomes, robust_full, robust_plot_label, and
# fmt_num/fmt_pct from the RobustTrim chunk.
fixest::setFixest_nthreads(1)
fixest::setFixest_estimation(reset = TRUE)

loso_states = sort(unique(dta_robust$uf[dta_robust$reg_sample == 1]))

# Match the eight selected headline outcomes, including ignitions per 100 km²
# of municipal area.
loo_loso_outcomes = appendix_stability_outcomes

loso_outcome_labels = setNames(
  unname(appendix_stability_labels),
  loo_loso_outcomes
)
loso_outcome_titles = setNames(
  paste0("(", letters[seq_along(loo_loso_outcomes)], ") ",
         unname(loso_outcome_labels)),
  loo_loso_outcomes
)
loso_outcome_ylabs = setNames(
  unname(appendix_stability_ylabs),
  loo_loso_outcomes
)
loso_outcome_ylabs[["rm_n_igni"]] = paste("ignitions", ignition_count_unit)
loso_outcome_label = function(x) {
  out = unname(loso_outcome_labels[x])
  out[is.na(out)] = robust_plot_label(x[is.na(out)])
  out
}

# 9 states x 8 outcomes is light enough to run sequentially.
loso_est = purrr::map_dfr(loso_states, function(drop_uf) {
  data_i = dplyr::filter(dta_robust, uf != drop_uf)
  purrr::map_dfr(loo_loso_outcomes, function(outcome_i) {
    estimate_starlink(data_i, outcome_i) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(dropped_uf = drop_uf)
  })
})

# Full-sample estimates for exactly the LOSO outcomes, computed here so the
# table's "Full estimate" column and the figure's "Full" entry are always
# present even when an outcome falls outside robust_outcomes (which drives
# robust_full). Same estimate_starlink() call as robust_full, so the numbers
# match the headline full-sample estimates.
loso_full = purrr::map_dfr(
  loo_loso_outcomes,
  function(oc) estimate_starlink(dta_robust, oc)
)

full_for_loso = loso_full %>%
  dplyr::select(outcome, full_estimate = estimate, full_p = p.value)

loso_aug = loso_est %>%
  dplyr::left_join(full_for_loso, by = "outcome") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    same_sign = sign(estimate) == sign(full_estimate),
    sig05 = p.value <= 0.05,
    sig10 = p.value <= 0.10
  )

loso_summary = loso_aug %>%
  dplyr::group_by(outcome) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    full_estimate = dplyr::first(full_estimate),
    full_p = dplyr::first(full_p),
    min = min(estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_sign_flip = sum(!same_sign, na.rm = TRUE),
    sig05_share = mean(sig05, na.rm = TRUE),
    sig10_share = mean(sig10, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_runs = sum(!is.na(estimate)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(outcome_label = loso_outcome_label(outcome)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(match(outcome, loo_loso_outcomes))

# Most influential state per outcome: the dropped UF that moves beta the most.
loso_worst = loso_aug %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(estimate), !is.na(full_estimate)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(outcome) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(abs(estimate - full_estimate), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    worst_uf = dropped_uf,
    worst_estimate = estimate,
    worst_p = p.value
  )

loso_table = loso_summary %>%
  dplyr::left_join(loso_worst, by = "outcome") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(match(outcome, loo_loso_outcomes)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    full = paste0(fmt_num(full_estimate), " (p = ", fmt_num(full_p), ")"),
    losomin = fmt_num(min),
    losomax = fmt_num(max),
    flips = as.character(n_sign_flip),
    s05 = fmt_pct(sig05_share),
    worst = ifelse(
      is.na(worst_uf),
      "",
      paste0(
        worst_uf,
        " (",
        fmt_num(worst_estimate),
        ", p = ",
        fmt_num(worst_p),
        ")"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Outcome = outcome_label,
    `Full estimate` = full,
    `LOSO min` = losomin,
    `LOSO max` = losomax,
    `Sign flips (/9)` = flips,
    `% LOSO sig. (5%)` = s05,
    `Most influential state dropped` = worst
  )

# cat(
#   knitr::kable(
#     as.data.frame(loso_table),
#     align = "l",
#     format = "html",
#     caption = "Leave-one-state-out robustness (each of the 9 Legal-Amazon UFs dropped in turn)"
#   ) %>%
#     kableExtra::kable_styling(
#       bootstrap_options = c("striped", "bordered", "hover", "condensed"),
#       full_width = FALSE,
#       position = "left"
#     ) %>%
#     kableExtra::footnote(
#       general_title = "Notes:",
#       general = paste(
#         "Each of the 9 Legal-Amazon states (UF) is dropped in turn and the",
#         "headline 2SLS re-estimated on the remaining 8. LOSO min/max give the",
#         "coefficient range across the 9 drops; Sign flips counts how many of",
#         "the 9 drops reverse the full-sample sign; % LOSO sig. is the share",
#         "significant at 5%; the last column reports the single most influential",
#         "state (largest absolute change in the coefficient) with its",
#         "re-estimated coefficient and p-value. Standard errors use the headline",
#         main_cluster_label,
#         "clustering scheme."
#       ),
#       footnote_as_chunk = TRUE,
#       escape = FALSE,
#       threeparttable = TRUE
#     ),
#   sep = "\n"
# )
cat("\n\n")

# Per-outcome LOSO coefficient-stability figure ---------------------------
# Matches the LOO-municipality panel layout but with the 95% (light) /
# 90% (darker overlay) double-segment whisker style used by the headline
# results figures (e.g. RobustTrim), and a plain discrete UF-sigla x-axis
# (no bracketed second axis). UFs ordered by IBGE code so the panel reads
# RO -> MT, the same geographic order as the LOO figures above. The full-
# sample estimate appears as the leftmost "Full" entry on the x-axis (rather
# than as a horizontal reference line), so the reader compares each
# leave-one-state-out point directly against it.
uf_code_to_sigla = c(
  "11" = "RO",
  "12" = "AC",
  "13" = "AM",
  "14" = "RR",
  "15" = "PA",
  "16" = "AP",
  "17" = "TO",
  "21" = "MA",
  "51" = "MT"
)
uf_levels = c("RO", "AC", "AM", "RR", "PA", "AP", "TO", "MA", "MT")

loso_plot_df = loso_aug %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    uf_code = as.character(dropped_uf),
    uf = dplyr::coalesce(unname(uf_code_to_sigla[uf_code]), uf_code)
  )

# Prepend the full-sample estimate (with its own 90/95% CIs) as the "Full"
# entry. robust_full covers all robust_outcomes; we keep only the outcomes
# LOSO actually iterated over.
loso_full_row = loso_full %>%
  dplyr::filter(outcome %in% unique(loso_plot_df$outcome)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    outcome = outcome,
    estimate = estimate,
    conf.low95 = conf.low95,
    conf.high95 = conf.high95,
    conf.low90 = conf.low90,
    conf.high90 = conf.high90,
    uf = "Full"
  )

loso_plot_df = dplyr::bind_rows(loso_full_row, loso_plot_df) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(uf = factor(uf, levels = c("Full", uf_levels)))

# The number below each state abbreviation is the number of municipalities that
# state drop excludes from the outcome's own estimation sample. The number below
# Full is that outcome's full-sample municipality count. These labels must be
# outcome-specific because the UPF-overlap and Spatial-HHI samples are smaller.
loso_state_counts = purrr::map_dfr(loo_loso_outcomes, function(oc) {
  dplyr::filter(
    dta_robust,
    reg_sample == 1,
    !is.na(.data[[oc]])
  ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(codmun, uf) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      uf_code = as.character(uf),
      uf_sigla = dplyr::coalesce(
        unname(uf_code_to_sigla[uf_code]),
        uf_code
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::count(uf_sigla, name = "n_mun") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(outcome = oc)
})

loso_x_labels = setNames(
  lapply(loo_loso_outcomes, function(oc) {
    counts = dplyr::filter(loso_state_counts, outcome == oc)
    n_by_uf = setNames(counts$n_mun, counts$uf_sigla)[uf_levels]
    n_by_uf[is.na(n_by_uf)] = 0
    c(
      Full = paste0("Full\n(", sum(n_by_uf), ")"),
      setNames(paste0(uf_levels, "\n(", n_by_uf, ")"), uf_levels)
    )
  }),
  loo_loso_outcomes
)

# `dat`, `x_labels` and `label_fn` are arguments purely so the PRODES
# leave-one-state-out section can reuse this panel builder on its own augmented
# frame. All three default to the calendar-panel objects, so every existing call
# is unchanged.
make_loso_fig = function(oc,
                         dat = loso_plot_df,
                         x_labels = loso_x_labels,
                         label_fn = loso_outcome_label) {
  d = dplyr::filter(dat, outcome == oc)
  if (nrow(d) == 0 || all(is.na(d$estimate))) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  panel_x_labels = if (is.list(x_labels)) x_labels[[oc]] else x_labels

  ggplot(d, aes(x = uf, y = estimate)) +
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = 0,
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.4,
      linetype = "dashed"
    ) +
    # 95% outer whisker (light grey) with 90% inner overlay (darker grey),
    # matching the placebo / trim figures' grey-and-red palette.
    geom_linerange(
      aes(ymin = conf.low95, ymax = conf.high95),
      color = "grey80",
      linewidth = 2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    geom_linerange(
      aes(ymin = conf.low90, ymax = conf.high90),
      color = "grey40",
      linewidth = 2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    geom_point(color = "red", size = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, labels = panel_x_labels) +
    labs(
      title = trimws(label_fn(oc)),
      x = NULL,
      y = "2SLS coefficient"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12),
      plot.margin = margin(6, 10, 8, 10),
      legend.position = "none",
      text = element_text(size = 10)
    )
}

# Build one panel per outcome, print each, and collect them into a combined view.
loso_panels = list()
for (oc in loo_loso_outcomes) {
  p_oc = make_loso_fig(oc)
  if (is.null(p_oc)) {
    next
  }
  loso_panels[[oc]] = p_oc
  print(p_oc)
  cat("\n\n")
}

# Combined 8-panel view: a two-column by four-row grid
# with letter-prefixed panel titles ("(a) ... " on the same line as the name)
# and short outcome-unit y labels. The per-panel "leave-one-state-out" subtitle
# is dropped here because it repeats identically across panels.
loso_fig_titles = loso_outcome_titles
loso_fig_ylabs = loso_outcome_ylabs
loso_panel_order = loo_loso_outcomes
if (all(loso_panel_order %in% names(loso_panels))) {
  loso_panels_lettered = lapply(seq_along(loso_panel_order), function(i) {
    oc = loso_panel_order[i]
    panel_title = if (identical(oc, "pm1mun")) {
      bquote(paste("(", .(letters[i]), ") ", PM[1]))
    } else {
      loso_fig_titles[[oc]]
    }
    loso_panels[[oc]] +
      labs(title = panel_title, y = loso_fig_ylabs[[oc]])
  })
  fig_loso_4 = ggpubr::ggarrange(
    plotlist = loso_panels_lettered,
    ncol = 2,
    nrow = 4,
    common.legend = TRUE,
    legend = "none",
    align = "hv"
  )
}
```

if (exists("fig_loso_4")) print(fig_loso_4) else
  cat("_(leave-one-state-out figure not produced in this run)_\n")
```


```{r FigureHelpers, echo=F}
# Axis-truncation helpers. They used to live inside the Fig4 chunk, but the
# Heterogeneity and HeterogeneityProdes chunks call them too, so they have to stay
# alive while the Figures sections below are commented out.
add_trunc = function(df, ylim) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      trunc_label = case_when(
        estimate > ylim[2] ~ paste0("► ", sprintf("%.1f", estimate)),
        estimate < ylim[1] ~ paste0(sprintf("%.1f", estimate), " ◄"),
        TRUE ~ ""
      ),
      trunc_hjust = case_when(
        estimate > ylim[2] ~ 1,
        estimate < ylim[1] ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ 0.5
      ),
      estimate_vis = pmin(pmax(estimate, ylim[1]), ylim[2])
    )
}

auto_ylim = function(x, probs = c(0.05, 0.95)) {
  q = quantile(x, probs = probs, na.rm = TRUE)
  pad = 0 #diff(q) * 0.2
  c(min(0, q[1] - pad), max(0, q[2] + pad))
}

Municipalities are split at the median soy yield potential (1.99) into high and low groups. Horizontal bars indicate 90% and 95% confidence intervals (CI), while the red circles represent point estimates. Results obtained from fixed-effects regressions using shift-share instruments and control variables on a panel dataset of 772 municipalities from 2022 to `r CAL_END_YEAR` (n = `r 772*(CAL_END_YEAR-2021)`).*

## Heterogeneity

```{r Heterogeneity, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F, fig.height=9, fig.width=10}
# The panel now carries a clean 0/1, time-invariant indicator pooled across the
# 2023 and 2024 Cartografias editions. Keep this coercion as a defensive check
# against legacy panels in which the Santarem--Mojui merge area-weighted the
# presence dummy to 0.7833.
dta = dta %>% mutate(faction = as.numeric(faction >= 0.5))

groups = c(
  "faction",
  "uc_dummy",
  "sett_dummy",
  "ndpf_dummy"
)

# Outcomes used in the appendix heterogeneity tables.
varlist = heterogeneity_outcomes

for (group in groups) {
  bd_fig = data.frame()

  # Every split reports the eight outcomes from the main results table.
  varlist = heterogeneity_outcomes

  # ── Detect variable type and define groups ──
  gvar = dta[[group]]

  # Continuous groups recompute the High/Low split separately for each outcome
  # (see the continuous branch and assign_groups() below). Dummy and categorical
  # groups keep one global assignment, so the flag defaults to FALSE.
  per_row_median = FALSE

  if (is.character(gvar) | is.factor(gvar)) {
    all_levels = sort(unique(na.omit(as.character(gvar))))
    freq = table(gvar) / sum(!is.na(gvar))
    levels_vec = all_levels[all_levels %in% names(freq[freq > 0.15])]
    removed_vec = all_levels[!all_levels %in% levels_vec]
    labels_vec = substr(levels_vec, 1, 7)
    dta2 = dta %>%
      mutate(group_var = as.character(.data[[group]])) %>%
      filter(group_var %in% levels_vec)
  } else if (all(na.omit(gvar) %in% c(0, 1))) {
    # Dummy: split by Yes/No
    med = median(gvar, na.rm = TRUE)
    # if (med == min(gvar, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    #   # More than 50% are zeros — use mean as threshold
    #   levels_vec = c("High", "Low")
    #   labels_vec = c("High", "Low")
    #   threshold = mean(gvar, na.rm = TRUE)
    #   dta2 = dta %>%
    #     mutate(group_var = ifelse(.data[[group]] > threshold, "High", "Low"))
    # } else {
    levels_vec = c("1", "0")
    labels_vec = c("Yes", "No")
    dta2 = dta %>% mutate(group_var = as.character(.data[[group]]))
    # }
  } else {
    # Continuous: per-outcome median split. A single global median sends almost
    # every tenure-holding municipality to one side once the outcome is limited
    # to municipalities that contain the tenure (e.g. indigenous lands land at
    # 156/705 under the road-density split, because indigenous-land
    # municipalities are overwhelmingly low-road). Splitting each outcome at the
    # median grouping value among the municipalities that actually enter its
    # regression (see assign_groups() below) keeps the High/Low cells balanced
    # within every row. The aggregate and by-category outcomes are non-missing
    # everywhere, so their per-row median equals the full-sample median and their
    # split is unchanged.
    levels_vec = c("High", "Low")
    labels_vec = c("High", "Low")
    per_row_median = TRUE
    med = median(gvar, na.rm = TRUE) # full-sample median: console + table note
    dta2 = dta %>%
      mutate(group_var = ifelse(.data[[group]] > med, "High", "Low"))
  }

  # Per-outcome High/Low assignment. For continuous groups the median is
  # recomputed within each outcome's estimation sample (reg_sample == 1 and the
  # outcome non-missing), so each land-tenure row splits at the median among the
  # municipalities that hold that tenure rather than at the full-sample median.
  # Dummy/categorical groups return the single global assignment in dta2.
  assign_groups = function(y) {
    if (!isTRUE(per_row_median)) {
      return(dta2)
    }
    med_y = median(
      dta[[group]][dta$reg_sample == 1 & !is.na(dta[[y]])],
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
    dplyr::mutate(
      dta,
      group_var = ifelse(.data[[group]] > med_y, "High", "Low")
    )
  }

  # ── High-Low difference test via a single fully-interacted ("saturated") IV ──
  # The displayed High/Low columns are split-sample IV fits, but the Diff column's
  # significance is read off ONE pooled regression in which the endogenous
  # Starlink rate, every covariate, and both fixed effects are interacted with the
  # group indicator (grp = 1 for the first displayed level, High/Yes), with both
  # the Starlink rate and its interaction instrumented (coverarea:year and
  # coverarea:year:grp). The coefficient on fit_starlink:grp is exactly the
  # High-Low difference (Frisch-Waugh equivalent to the split-sample point
  # estimate), and its cluster-robust SE comes from the joint vcov -- so it stays
  # correct even though microregion clusters span both halves of the split, where
  # the Paternoster split-sample z is only an approximation. grp follows the SAME
  # per-outcome split as assign_groups(), so the saturated difference matches
  # (High column - Low column) exactly.
  saturated_iv_diff = function(y) {
    d = assign_groups(y) %>%
      dplyr::filter(reg_sample == 1, group_var %in% levels_vec) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(grp = as.numeric(group_var == levels_vec[1]))
    sat_covs = c(covs_full, paste0(covs_full, ":grp"))
    f = as.formula(paste0(
      y,
      " ~ ",
      paste(sat_covs, collapse = " + "),
      " | interaction(codmun, grp) + interaction(uf, year, grp)",
      " | starlink + starlink:grp ~ coverarea:year + coverarea:year:grp"
    ))
    est = tryCatch(
      feols(f, data = d, cluster = main_cluster_form, notes = FALSE),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (is.null(est)) {
      return(list(diff = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
    }
    ct = est$coeftable
    nm = rownames(ct)[rownames(ct) == "fit_starlink:grp"]
    if (length(nm) != 1) {
      return(list(diff = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
    }
    list(
      diff = unname(ct[nm, 1]),
      se = unname(ct[nm, 2]),
      p = unname(ct[nm, 4])
    )
  }

  n_levels = length(levels_vec)

  # ── ONLY THE FULL MODEL (Fabio, 2026-08-12) ───────────────────────────────
  # These tables used to print every covlist model per split half -- Yes (I),
  # Yes (II), No (I), No (II), Diff -- which doubled the width for a
  # no-covariate column nobody reads the heterogeneity off. Only the headline
  # specification is shown now. het_covlist is a ONE-ELEMENT list, so every
  # seq_along / length below follows automatically, and the estimation loop runs
  # half as many fits. The column keeps its TRUE Roman numeral rather than being
  # renumbered to (I), so it still names the same model as the main table.
  het_covlist = covlist[covs_headline_idx]
  het_model_numeral = as.roman(covs_headline_idx)
  n_cov = length(het_covlist)

  # ── Build result table ──
  n_cols = 1 + n_levels * n_cov
  if (n_levels == 2) {
    n_cols <- n_cols + 1
  }

  # No covariate block: outcome rows, a rule, then N (see the note in
  # print_se_result_table). Here N genuinely belongs at the foot -- one figure
  # per split half, constant down the column.
  n_rows = 3 + 2 * length(varlist) + 2
  result = data.frame(matrix(ncol = n_cols, nrow = n_rows, data = ""))

  if (n_levels == 2) {
    result[1, n_cols] <- ""
    result[2, n_cols] <- "Diff."
  }

  # Row 1: group label over first column of each block
  for (lv in seq_along(levels_vec)) {
    j_start = 1 + (lv - 1) * n_cov + 1
    result[1, j_start] = labels_vec[lv]
  }

  # Row 2: specification number of the single model shown.
  result[2, 1] = ""
  for (lv in seq_along(levels_vec)) {
    for (cv in seq_along(het_covlist)) {
      j_col = 1 + (lv - 1) * n_cov + cv
      result[2, j_col] = paste0("(", het_model_numeral, ")")
    }
  }

  # Row 3: "Outcomes"
  result[3, 1] = "Outcomes"

  # Outcome rows
  i = 4
  for (vardep in varlist) {
    rownames(result)[i] = paste0(vardep, "_est")
    rownames(result)[i + 1] = paste0(vardep, "_se")
    result[i, 1] = heterogeneity_label(vardep)
    i = i + 2
  }

  # Closing rule under the last outcome; the N row is filled in below.
  result[4 + 2 * length(varlist), ] = "-------"

  # ── Estimation loop ──
  for (cv in seq_along(het_covlist)) {
    for (y in varlist) {
      model = paste0(
        y,
        " ~ ",
        paste0(het_covlist[[cv]], collapse = " + "),
        " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)",
        " | starlink ~ coverarea:year"
      ) %>%
        as.formula()

      # Per-outcome High/Low split (continuous groups recenter the median on the
      # municipalities that enter THIS outcome's regression; see assign_groups()).
      dta2 = assign_groups(y)

      est_store <- list() # ← ADD THIS

      for (lv in seq_along(levels_vec)) {
        j_col = 1 + (lv - 1) * n_cov + cv

        est = tryCatch(
          feols(
            model,
            data = dta2 %>%
              filter(reg_sample == 1 & group_var == levels_vec[lv]),
            cluster = main_cluster_form,
            notes = FALSE
          ),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
        # Degenerate (outcome x split-half) cells -- e.g. a tenure-specific
        # outcome that vanishes in the complementary tenure half (no tenure area
        # -> NA), or a constant DV -- blank the cell and carry NA into the diff
        # test instead of crashing the whole chunk.
        if (is.null(est) || !("fit_starlink" %in% rownames(est$coeftable))) {
          result[paste0(y, "_est"), j_col] <- "---"
          result[paste0(y, "_se"), j_col] <- ""
          est_store[[lv]] <- list(beta = NA_real_, se = NA_real_)
          next
        }
        tab = broom::tidy(est)

        result[paste0(y, "_est"), j_col] <-
          paste0(
            sprintf("%.3f", tab$estimate[1]),
            case_when(
              tab$p.value[1] <= .01 ~ "***",
              tab$p.value[1] <= .05 ~ "**",
              tab$p.value[1] <= .10 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ ""
            )
          )
        result[paste0(y, "_se"), j_col] <-
          paste0("(", sprintf("%.3f", tab$std.error[1]), ")")

        # Store for diff test
        est_store[[lv]] <- list(beta = tab$estimate[1], se = tab$std.error[1])

        # Store figure data for fullest specification
        if (cv == length(het_covlist)) {
          aux = broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>%
            rename(conf.low95 = conf.low, conf.high95 = conf.high) %>%
            left_join(
              broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>%
                select(term, conf.low, conf.high) %>%
                rename(conf.low90 = conf.low, conf.high90 = conf.high),
              by = "term"
            ) %>%
            filter(term == "fit_starlink") %>%
            mutate(term = y, group = group, half = labels_vec[lv])
          bd_fig = bind_rows(bd_fig, aux)
        }
      } # ← end of lv loop

      # Difference test AFTER both levels estimated ← MOVED HERE
      if (n_levels == 2 & cv == length(het_covlist)) {
        b1 <- est_store[[1]]$beta
        b2 <- est_store[[2]]$beta

        # High-Low difference significance from the fully-interacted ("saturated")
        # IV (see saturated_iv_diff() above), NOT the Paternoster split-sample z:
        # microregion clusters span both halves of every split, so
        # Cov(beta_high, beta_low) != 0 and the split-sample z would only be an
        # approximation. The saturated coefficient on fit_starlink:grp IS the
        # High-Low difference, with its cluster-robust SE from the joint vcov; its
        # point estimate equals b1 - b2 by Frisch-Waugh, so the displayed diff
        # still reconciles exactly with (High column - Low column).
        sat <- saturated_iv_diff(y)
        p_diff <- sat$p

        result[paste0(y, "_est"), n_cols] <-
          if (is.na(b1) || is.na(b2)) {
            "---"   # one split half was degenerate (blanked above)
          } else {
            # Difference and its significance stars only. The explicit
            # "[p=0.103]" suffix was dropped (Fabio, 2026-08-12): it repeated in
            # every row of the column and, at ~11 characters, was the widest
            # thing in the table. The stars carry the same test -- p_diff comes
            # from the saturated IV below, not from the two half-sample fits.
            paste0(
              sprintf("%.3f", b1 - b2),
              case_when(
                is.na(p_diff) ~ "",
                p_diff <= .01 ~ "***",
                p_diff <= .05 ~ "**",
                p_diff <= .10 ~ "*",
                TRUE ~ ""
              )
            )
          }

      }
    } # end y loop
  } # end cv loop

  rownames(result) = 1:nrow(result)
  colnames(result) = NULL

  # ── N row ──
  n_row = nrow(result)
  result[n_row - 1, 1] = "-------"
  result[n_row, 1] = "N"
  for (lv in seq_along(levels_vec)) {
    n_obs = dta2 %>%
      filter(reg_sample == 1 & group_var == levels_vec[lv]) %>%
      nrow()
    for (cv in seq_along(het_covlist)) {
      j_col = 1 + (lv - 1) * n_cov + cv
      result[n_row, j_col] = format(n_obs, big.mark = ",")
    }
  }

  print(paste(rep("=", 40), collapse = " "))
  print(paste0(
    "## Heterogeneity by ",
    var_names$varname[match(group, var_names$var)]
  ))
  if (is.numeric(gvar) & !(all(na.omit(gvar) %in% c(0, 1)))) {
    print(summary(gvar))
    # if (median(gvar, na.rm = TRUE) == min(gvar, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    #   print(paste0("Threshold: mean = ", round(mean(gvar, na.rm = TRUE), 4)))
    # } else {
    print(paste0("Threshold: median = ", round(median(gvar, na.rm = TRUE), 4)))
    # }
  } else if (all(na.omit(gvar) %in% c(0, 1))) {
    print(summary(gvar))
    # if (median(gvar, na.rm = TRUE) == min(gvar, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    #   print(paste0("Threshold: mean = ", round(mean(gvar, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    #                " (dummy with median = min)"))
    # } else {
    print(paste0("Split: dummy (Yes = 1, No = 0)"))
    # }
  } else {
    print(paste0(
      "Split: categorical (levels: ",
      paste(labels_vec, collapse = ", "),
      ")"
    ))
    if (length(removed_vec) > 0) {
      print(paste0(
        "Removed (< 15% of obs): ",
        paste(removed_vec, collapse = ", ")
      ))
    }
  }
  # # #
  print(format(result, justify = "left"))
  # print(" ")

  # The group-specific result matrix above is the HTML output for this split.
  # The formatted result matrix above is the displayed heterogeneity output.
  next

  # ── Figures: all outcome variables ──
  clean_het_label = function(x) {
    # Replace leading regular spaces with non-breaking spaces so ggplot preserves indentation
    leading = regmatches(x, regexpr("^ *", x))
    paste0(strrep("\u00a0", nchar(leading)), sub("^ *", "", x))
  }

  # Use term (unique) as factor; map to pretty labels via scale_x_discrete
  fig_term_levels = rev(varlist[varlist %in% bd_fig$term])
  term_labels = setNames(
    clean_het_label(var_names$varname[match(fig_term_levels, var_names$var)]),
    fig_term_levels
  )

  aux_het = bd_fig %>%
    mutate(
      name = factor(term, levels = fig_term_levels),
      half = factor(half, levels = labels_vec)
    )

  if (n_levels <= 2) {
    half_colors = setNames(c("red", "black")[1:n_levels], labels_vec)
  } else {
    half_colors = setNames(scales::hue_pal()(n_levels), labels_vec)
  }

  ylim_het = auto_ylim(
    c(aux_het$conf.low95, aux_het$conf.high95),
    probs = c(0.065, 0.90)
  )
  aux_het = add_trunc(aux_het, ylim_het)

  assign(
    paste0("fig_het_", group),
    ggplot(aux_het, aes(x = name, y = estimate)) +
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = 0,
        color = "black",
        size = 0.5,
        linetype = "dashed"
      ) +
      geom_linerange(
        aes(
          ymin = conf.low95,
          ymax = conf.high95,
          colour = "95% CI",
          group = half
        ),
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
        size = 2,
        show.legend = TRUE,
        key_glyph = "path"
      ) +
      geom_linerange(
        aes(
          ymin = conf.low90,
          ymax = conf.high90,
          colour = "90% CI",
          group = half
        ),
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
        size = 2,
        show.legend = TRUE,
        key_glyph = "path"
      ) +
      scale_colour_manual(
        name = NULL,
        breaks = c("90% CI", "95% CI"),
        values = c("90% CI" = "grey60", "95% CI" = "grey80"),
        guide = guide_legend(
          order = 2,
          override.aes = list(shape = NA, linetype = 1, size = 3)
        )
      ) +
      ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +
      geom_point(
        aes(color = half),
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
        size = 2,
        key_glyph = "point"
      ) +
      geom_text(
        aes(
          y = estimate_vis,
          label = trunc_label,
          color = half,
          hjust = trunc_hjust
        ),
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
        size = 3.5,
        vjust = 0.5,
        show.legend = FALSE
      ) +
      scale_color_manual(
        name = NULL,
        values = half_colors,
        guide = guide_legend(
          order = 1,
          override.aes = list(linetype = 0, shape = 16, size = 2)
        )
      ) +
      scale_x_discrete(labels = term_labels) +
      labs(
        x = NULL,
        y = "Estimate",
        title = paste0(
          "Heterogeneity by ",
          var_names$varname[match(group, var_names$var)]
        )
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        text = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0)
      ) +
      coord_flip(ylim = ylim_het) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  )

  print(eval(parse(text = paste0("fig_het_", group))))
}
