# PRODES Year

**Not part of the current 2022--2024 manuscript. Retained for a possible
referee-requested extension through official PRODES 2025 (August 2024--July
2025).**

```{r DataNormalizationProdes, echo=F}
# Dataset and normalization
# The PRODES estimation window begins in reference year 2023 (Aug 2022-Jul
# 2023). The IV columns are built explicitly below so 2023 is omitted by
# construction rather than left to factor ordering and collinearity removal.
prodes_iv_base_year = 2023L
normal_year_headline_covs = covlist[[covs_headline_idx]]
normal_year_covlist = covlist

# Same planned/under-construction road join as the calendar panel. It has to be
# repeated here rather than inherited: add_ctrl_interactions() runs on this panel
# too and stops if a control column is missing, which is the guard that caught
# x22_area_forest last time.

# .RDS for the same reason as the calendar panel above: the .dta names are
# abbreviated to fit Stata's 32-character cap and would not match this file.
prodes_source_marker = paste0(panel_dir, "prodes_source.txt")
stopifnot(
  file.exists(prodes_source_marker),
  identical(
    trimws(readLines(prodes_source_marker, warn = FALSE)[1]),
    "yearly_deforestation_amazonia_legal"
  )
)
panel_path = paste0(panel_dir, "dataset_prodesyr.RDS")
dta = readRDS(panel_path)
if (!identical(attr(dta, "coordinate_basis"), "ibge_municipal_seat")) {
  stop("Rebuild the v3 panel: its coordinates and distances are not marked as IBGE-seat based")
}
if (!identical(attr(dta, "faction_report_years"), c(2023L, 2024L)) ||
    !identical(attr(dta, "faction_time_varying"), FALSE)) {
  stop("Rebuild the panel with the time-invariant 2023--2024 faction definition")
}
dta = dta %>%
  filter(year >= 2017 & year <= PRODES_END_YEAR & !is.na(coverarea)) %>%
  {
    stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(.$codmun) == 772)
    .
  } %>%
  # Road surfaces, coordinates, CHIRTS-ERA5 Tmax, CHIRPS precipitation, and
  # distances ship on the panel.
  add_lagged_price_controls() %>%
  add_spei12_anchor("prodes") %>%
  add_pre2022_fire_scar_spei() %>%
  mutate(year = factor(year, levels = as.character(PRODES_END_YEAR:2017))) %>%
  fastDummies::dummy_cols("year") %>%
  mutate(
    # `way_`-prefixed so the normalization loop divides it by MUNICIPAL area
    # x100, the definition the control was selected on.
    way_rail_oper = way_rail,
    # The compact panel carries six native municipal PRODES concepts, each as
    # a polygon count and mapped area.
    ca_2017 = year_2017 * coverarea,
    ca_2018 = year_2018 * coverarea,
    ca_2019 = year_2019 * coverarea,
    ca_2020 = year_2020 * coverarea,
    ca_2021 = year_2021 * coverarea,
    ca_2022 = year_2022 * coverarea,
    ca_2023 = year_2023 * coverarea,
    ca_2024 = year_2024 * coverarea,
    # Third-degree bivariate polynomial in latitude and longitude, entered
    # interacted with year dummies in covlist. Follows Araujo et al. (2025,
    # transportation) -- the closest comparison paper, already cited in the
    # exclusion-restriction discussion -- which controls for "third-degree
    # polynomials of latitude and longitude interacted with time dummies".
    # The municipality FE absorbs every time-INVARIANT spatial term, so these
    # do work only through the year interaction: they absorb spatial trends
    # that shift over time, not fixed geography.
    lat2 = lat^2,
    lon2 = lon^2,
    latlon = lat * lon,
    lat3 = lat^3,
    lon3 = lon^3,
    lat2lon = lat^2 * lon,
    latlon2 = lat * lon^2,
    #  r_degr_flag = area_mun_deter_degr / n_mun_deter_degr,
    # rf_n_igni_deter = (n_igni_deter / area_mun_deter_degr_fire) / 1000,
  ) %>%
  mutate(ca_2025 = year_2025 * coverarea) %>%
  select(-starts_with("year_20"))

# Explicit PRODES-year IV basis: 2023 is the reference, so the 2024 build uses
# caP_2024 and the 2025 build uses caP_2024 + caP_2025.
prodes_iv_names = paste0(
  "caP_",
  setdiff(2023:PRODES_END_YEAR, prodes_iv_base_year)
)
for (yy in setdiff(2023:PRODES_END_YEAR, prodes_iv_base_year)) {
  dta[[paste0("caP_", yy)]] = dta$coverarea *
    (as.integer(as.character(dta$year)) == yy)
}
stopifnot(length(prodes_iv_names) > 0, all(prodes_iv_names %in% names(dta)))
prodes_iv_rhs = paste(prodes_iv_names, collapse = " + ")


# # Creating new variables / Normalizing by area
# area_list = colnames(dta)[startsWith(colnames(dta),"area") | startsWith(colnames(dta),"way")]
# n_list = colnames(dta)[startsWith(colnames(dta),"n_")]
# sh_list = colnames(dta)[startsWith(colnames(dta),"sh_")]

# for (y in area_list) {
#   dta[[paste0("r_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[["areamun"]]) * 100
# }

# for (y in n_list) {
#   dta[[paste0("r_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[["areamun"]]) * 1000
#   }

# for (y in sh_list) {
#   dta[[y]] = dta[[y]] * 100
# }

# ── Area outcomes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
area_list = colnames(dta)[
  startsWith(colnames(dta), "area") |
    startsWith(colnames(dta), "way")
]
# Same headline denominator as the calendar panel (see DataNormalization): the
# switch is read from there, so the two panels can never disagree. PRODES
# deforestation is forest clearing, so the forest denominator applies for the
# same reason it applies to degradation.
stopifnot(exists("norm_denom"), all(dta[[norm_denom]] > 0, na.rm = TRUE))
for (y in area_list) {
  dta[[paste0("rm_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[["areamun"]]) * 100 # % munic. area
  dta[[paste0("r_", y)]] = if (startsWith(y, "way")) {
    dta[[paste0("rm_", y)]] # road density is a control: municipal area
  } else {
    (dta[[y]] / dta[[norm_denom]]) * 100 # norm_area_unit
  }
}

# ── Count outcomes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_list = colnames(dta)[startsWith(colnames(dta), "n_")]
for (y in n_list) {
  dta[[paste0("rm_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[["areamun"]]) * count_scale # per count_scale km² munic.
  dta[[paste0("r_", y)]] = (dta[[y]] / dta[[norm_denom]]) * count_scale # norm_count_unit
}


dta = dta %>%
  mutate(
    areamun = areamun / 1000,
    area_forest = area_forest / 1000,
    dist_coast = dist_coast / 1000,
    dist_brasilia = dist_brasilia / 1000,
    # microregion-by-year key for the two-way {codmun + microreg:year} cluster
    # scheme. The PRODES reference-year panel reloads dta from a separate file,
    # so microreg_year must be rebuilt here exactly as on the calendar panel
    # (otherwise every two-way-clustered PRODES estimate errors with
    # "variable 'microreg_year' ... not in the original data set").
    microreg_year = paste(microreg, year, sep = "_"),
  ) %>%
  select(-any_of(c("r_areamun", "rm_areamun", paste0("r_", norm_denom))))

# ── Control set: identical to the calendar panel ──────────────────────────────
# Both panels use the common Model A controls defined at the top of this
# document. Only the SPEI-12 endpoint changes to match the outcome window.
#
# Verified on the 2025 build before adopting it (2026-08-13), PRODES-specific
# set -> Model A: deforestation by progressive degradation (flags) 0.0796** ->
# 0.0842**, DETER degradation flags 0.1330** -> 0.1418**, PRODES total null
# under both (-0.008 -> -0.021), first-stage Wald F 10.66 -> 11.08. Cost: the
# joint pre-2022 placebo for PRODES TOTAL deforestation goes 0.103 -> 0.018 and
# now rejects at 5% for that outcome; the progressive-degradation class (0.802)
# and DETER degradation (0.350) stay clean.
#
# On that pre-trend, tested 2026-08-13 (calendar 2024 / PRODES 2025): folding the
# two road terms into one summed density repairs it (0.018 -> 0.140) but costs
# PM1 and PM2.5 their 5% significance on the calendar panel (0.450** -> 0.343*,
# 0.500** -> 0.376*). Paved-only is indistinguishable from the split and does
# NOT repair it (0.017). Unpaved-only repairs it best (0.698) but breaks the
# fire-scar pre-trend (0.032). The split is kept; note that r_way_road_pav still
# carries the SNV concurrency inflation (~3.6%, see TODO.md), so this pre-trend
# is worth retesting after that fix rather than designing the spec around it.
#

# Replace only the drought endpoint in Model II. Model I and every other control
# remain identical to the calendar-year specification.
covlist = normal_year_covlist
covlist[[covs_headline_idx]][
  covlist[[covs_headline_idx]] == ctrl_model_ii_extra_calendar
] = ctrl_model_ii_extra_prodes
prodes_headline_covs = normal_year_headline_covs
prodes_headline_covs[
  prodes_headline_covs == ctrl_model_ii_extra_calendar
] = ctrl_model_ii_extra_prodes

stopifnot(
  all(c(ctrl_interact, ctrl_uninteract_vars) %in% names(dta)),
  all(is.finite(dta$spei12_jul)),
  identical(covlist[[1]], normal_year_covlist[[1]]),
  identical(covlist[[covs_headline_idx]], prodes_headline_covs),
  ctrl_model_ii_extra_calendar %in% normal_year_headline_covs,
  ctrl_model_ii_extra_prodes %in% prodes_headline_covs
)
covs_placebo = covlist[[covs_headline_idx]]
covs_full = covlist[[covs_headline_idx]]
covs = covlist[[covs_headline_idx]]
# robust_covs is what estimate_starlink() and muni_var_share() read. It is bound
# in the RobustTrim chunk on the calendar panel; rebound here so the PRODES
# robustness tables read the same object rather than depending on chunk order.
robust_covs = covlist[[covs_headline_idx]]

# Control-by-year interaction columns, rebuilt on this panel for the same reason
# microreg_year is: the PRODES section reloads `dta` from its own file.
# Retained ONLY for the interaction-structure comparison in the diagnostics
# section, which reconstructs the superseded hand-built {2022, 2023} columns to
# show what they did to the pre-period. No model here uses these columns:
# covlist and the placebo both use `year:x`, which fixest expands from the year
# levels present in whichever sample it is given.
dta = add_ctrl_interactions(dta)

# ── PRODES-year outcome lists ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Only native municipal PRODES outcomes from polygons of at least 6.25 ha
# belong on this panel. Retain both polygon counts and mapped area by class.
prodes_varlist = c(
  "r_n_mun_prodes_defo",
  "r_n_mun_prodes_defo_ccut",
  "r_n_mun_prodes_defo_cces",
  "r_n_mun_prodes_defo_ccwv",
  "r_n_mun_prodes_defo_dpdp",
  "r_n_mun_prodes_defo_mine",
  "r_area_mun_prodes_defo",
  "r_area_mun_prodes_defo_ccut",
  "r_area_mun_prodes_defo_cces",
  "r_area_mun_prodes_defo_ccwv",
  "r_area_mun_prodes_defo_dpdp",
  "r_area_mun_prodes_defo_mine"
)
stopifnot(all(prodes_varlist %in% names(dta)))

# The diagnostics and robustness checks use the same 12 native PRODES outcomes:
# six polygon-count densities and the corresponding six mapped-area shares.
prodes_diagnostic_requested = prodes_varlist
missing_prodes_diagnostics = setdiff(prodes_diagnostic_requested, names(dta))
if (length(missing_prodes_diagnostics)) {
  stop(
    "Missing requested PRODES diagnostic outcomes: ",
    paste(missing_prodes_diagnostics, collapse = ", ")
  )
}
prodes_diagnostic_outcomes = prodes_diagnostic_requested
prodes_robust_outcomes = prodes_diagnostic_outcomes

prodes_diagnostic_labels = c(
  setNames(var_names$varname[match(prodes_varlist, var_names$var)], prodes_varlist)
)
prodes_diagnostic_titles = setNames(
  paste0(
    "(", letters[seq_along(prodes_diagnostic_outcomes)], ") ",
    unname(prodes_diagnostic_labels[prodes_diagnostic_outcomes])
  ),
  prodes_diagnostic_outcomes
)
prodes_diagnostic_ylabs = c(
  setNames(rep(norm_count_unit, 6L), prodes_varlist[1:6]),
  setNames(rep("% 2021 forest", 6L), prodes_varlist[7:12])
)

message(
  "PRODES diagnostics/robustness outcomes: ",
  paste(prodes_diagnostic_outcomes, collapse = ", ")
)

# Olea-Pflueger effective F on the PRODES panel, per outcome. Generalizes the
# single-outcome op_F_prodes further down this document: same caP_<year> instrument
# materialization, same helpers from WeakIVSetup, but callable for any outcome so the
# results table can carry an OP F column.
#
# THE n-1 CONVENTION IS WHAT MAKES THIS COMPUTABLE. With time-invariant controls and
# municipality FE, x*1(y1) + ... + x*1(yn) = x, which the FE absorbs, so only n-1 year
# interactions and n-1 instruments are identified. The PRODES estimation sample begins
# in 2023, so 2023 is omitted explicitly. Do not rely on factor ordering here: `year`
# is stored newest-to-oldest, which made `sort(unique(year))[-1]` drop the newest year.
# Any n-1 subset spans the same space, but the code should match the stated reference.
prodes_iv_years = function(data) {
  years = sort(unique(as.integer(as.character(data$year))))
  stopifnot(prodes_iv_base_year %in% years)
  setdiff(years, prodes_iv_base_year)
}

op_F_prodes_outcome = function(y, covst) {
  tryCatch(
    {
      d = dplyr::filter(
        dta,
        reg_sample == 1,
        !is.na(.data[[y]])
      )
      pys = prodes_iv_years(d)
      if (!length(pys)) return(NA_real_)
      for (yy in pys) {
        d[[paste0("caP_", yy)]] = d$coverarea * (d$year == yy)
      }
      sp = split_controls_for_ivdiag(covst, d)
      op_F_clustered(
        data = d,
        yvar = y,
        formula_controls = sp$formula,
        bare_controls = sp$bare,
        iv = paste0("caP_", pys),
        cluster_chars = main_cluster_chars,
        cluster_form = main_cluster_form
      )
    },
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )
}
```


*This table presents municipal annual average statistics as mean ± standard deviation for each variable. Variable names and units are listed in the first column. The following columns represent periods before (2017–2022) and after (2023–`r PRODES_END_YEAR`) Starlink's entry into the Brazilian Amazon.*


## Estimations

- Model `r as.character(as.roman(1))`: no covariates
- Model `r as.character(as.roman(length(covlist)))`: all covariates

```{r EstimationsProdes, message=F, warning=F, R.options = list(width = 1200), echo=F}
# The 12 native PRODES outcomes estimated on the August--July reference year.
varlist = prodes_varlist

# Setting results table.
# The covariate block is not printed here either -- see the note in
# print_se_result_table on the calendar panel. N stays visible for auditability;
# the 12 native PRODES outcomes share the same 2023--2025 sample.
result = data.frame(matrix(
  ncol = 1 + length(covlist),
  nrow = 2 + 2 * length(varlist) + 1,
  data = ""
))
result[1, 1 + ceiling(length(covlist) / 2)] = "Starlink"
result[2, 1] = "Outcomes"
result[2, 2:ncol(result)] = paste0("  (", as.roman(1:length(covlist)), ")")

# +N, +OP F. Both are kept on each outcome row for auditability.
result = cbind(result, data.frame(ci95 = "", t = "", p = "", N = "", opF = ""))
result[2, (ncol(result) - 4):ncol(result)] = c(
  "95% CI",
  "t-stat",
  "p-val",
  "N",
  "OP F"
)

# Closing rule under the last outcome.
result[3 + 2 * length(varlist), ] = "-------"

i = 3
for (vardep in varlist) {
  rownames(result)[i] = paste0(vardep, "_est")
  rownames(result)[i + 1] = paste0(vardep, "_se")
  result[i, 1] = var_names$varname[which(vardep == var_names$var)]

  i = i + 2
}


# options(width = 1200)
# knitr::opts_chunk$set(width = 1200)
print(paste0("Covariates: ", paste(covs, collapse = ", ")))

bd_fig = data.frame() # Store results to create figures
# The PRODES panel contains only native deforestation outcomes, so every outcome
# uses the same 2023--2025 estimation frame.
dta_prodes_est = dplyr::filter(dta, reg_sample == 1)

j = 2
for (covs in covlist) {
  for (y in varlist) {
    model = paste0(
      y,
      " ~ ",
      # Covariates
      paste0(covs, collapse = " + "),
      " | codmun + interaction(uf, year)", # fixed-effects
      " | starlink ~ ",
      prodes_iv_rhs
    ) %>%
      as.formula()

    est = feols(
      model,
      data = dta_prodes_est,
      cluster = main_cluster_form,
      notes = FALSE
    )
    tab = broom::tidy(est, conf.int = T, conf.level = .95)

    result[paste0(y, "_est"), j] = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", tab$estimate[1]),
      case_when(
        tab$p.value[1] <= .01 ~ "***",
        tab$p.value[1] <= .05 ~ "**",
        tab$p.value[1] <= .10 ~ "*",
        TRUE ~ ""
      )
    )
    result[paste0(y, "_se"), j] = paste0(
      "(",
      sprintf("%.3f", tab$std.error[1]),
      ")"
    )

    if (all(covs == covlist[[covs_headline_idx]])) {
      if (y == varlist[1]) {
        # 1st stage results
        tab_1st = round(summary(est, stage = 1)$coeftable, 4)
        tab_1stA = fitstat(est, ~ cd + ivwald)
        tab_1stB = paste0(
          "R² = ",
          sprintf("%.4f", r2(summary(est, stage = 1))["r2"])
        )
      }

      result[paste0(y, "_est"), "ci95"] =
        paste0(
          "[",
          sprintf("%.3f", tab$conf.low[1]),
          ", ",
          sprintf("%.3f", tab$conf.high[1]),
          "]"
        )
      result[paste0(y, "_est"), "t"] = sprintf("%.3f", tab$statistic[1])
      result[paste0(y, "_est"), "p"] = sprintf("%.3f", tab$p.value[1])
      result[paste0(y, "_est"), "N"] = formatC(
        nobs(est),
        format = "d",
        big.mark = ","
      ) # +N

      # Olea-Pflueger effective F on this outcome's own estimation sample. With
      # only two treated years the design is just-identified (one instrument
      # survives the FE) and the statistic is the usual robust first-stage F.
      opF_y = op_F_prodes_outcome(y, covlist[[covs_headline_idx]])
      result[paste0(y, "_est"), "opF"] = if (is.na(opF_y)) {
        "."
      } else {
        sprintf("%.1f", opF_y)
      }

      # First-stage strength (Kleibergen--Paap rk Wald F). Identical across outcomes
      # sharing the same first-stage sample/instruments, but captured per outcome so
      # reduced-sample outcomes (e.g., the PRODES reference-year panel) carry their own.
      fstat_kp = tryCatch(
        fitstat(est, ~ivwald, simplify = FALSE)$ivwald1$stat,
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      aux = broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>%
        rename(conf.low95 = conf.low, conf.high95 = conf.high) %>%
        left_join(
          broom::tidy(est, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>%
            select(term, conf.low, conf.high) %>%
            rename(conf.low90 = conf.low, conf.high90 = conf.high),
          by = "term"
        ) %>%
        filter(term == "fit_starlink") %>%
        mutate(term = y, N = nobs(est), fstat_kp = fstat_kp, op_F = opF_y)

      # Saving results for figures
      bd_fig = bind_rows(bd_fig, aux)
    }
  }

  j = j + 1
}
rownames(result) = 1:nrow(result)
colnames(result) = NULL

# PRODES estimation-sample size, taken off the headline deforestation fit above.
# It is defined HERE, in a live chunk, because prose further down references it
# inline as `r n_prodes_panel`. knitr evaluates inline code in markdown even
# inside an HTML comment (it runs before pandoc strips the comment), so leaving
# the only definition inside the eval=FALSE FigCoverProdes chunk made the render
# fail with "object 'n_prodes_panel' not found".
n_prodes_panel = bd_fig$N[match("r_area_mun_prodes_defo", bd_fig$term)]

print("# 2nd Stage # # # # # # # # # #")
# drops the 95% CI and t-stat columns, keeping p, N and OP F. The offsets shift by one
# relative to the calendar panel because this table carries the extra OP F column.
print(format(
  result[, -c((ncol(result) - 4):(ncol(result) - 3))],
  justify = "left"
))
local({
  ty = sort(unique(dta$year[dta$reg_sample == 1]))
  k = max(0L, length(ty) - 1L)
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0(
      "OP F = Olea-Pflueger effective F on each outcome's own estimation sample.\n",
      "      Treated years %s -> k = %d instrument(s) survive the fixed effects.\n"
    ),
    paste(rev(as.character(ty)), collapse = ", "),
    k
  ))
  # Thresholds depend on the clustered estimate of K_eff, not the raw instrument
  # count. Outcome-specific values are computed by momentfit where reported.
  if (k >= 2L) {
    cat(
      "      Read each OP F against its momentfit Patnaik critical value based on\n",
      "      the sample-specific clustered K_eff, not a k=2 lookup-table value.\n",
      sep = ""
    )
  } else {
    cat(
      "      k=1: the design is JUST-IDENTIFIED and the effective F reduces to the\n",
      "      usual robust first-stage F, so the k=2 MOP thresholds do NOT apply.\n",
      "      Two overidentifying instruments only reappear once 2025 is included,\n",
      "      which gives three treated PRODES years.\n",
      sep = ""
    )
  }
})
```
